☆ Typed Transverse Momentum Parton distribution function computations
Dustin Keller
A transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution enters an extraction through a specified observation map and a parameter- dependent numerical calculation. Equal units and matching array dimensions do not establish that two implementations represent the same inference problem. We present typed-TMD, a computational framework that makes observation semantics, parameter dependencies, and admissible evaluation plans explicit.
☆ QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding for Nuclear Deformation Landscapes
Abhishek, P. Arumugam
Locating the minimum of a nuclear collective landscape can require many interacting many-body calculations. QDMin (Quantum Deformation Minimum Finding) searches a parameterized Hamiltonian family with a coherent collective-coordinate register and an on-demand ground-energy threshold oracle. The oracle supplies the predicate required for quantum minimum-finding without first constructing the energy landscape point by point. We implement it for a schematic pairing-plus-multipole model using circuit-generated energy estimates during the search. In a four-point calculation, one Grover round raises the probability of the true minimum from 0.25 to 0.921. A $4\times4$ quadrupole--octupole-field calculation extends the complete circuit to two coordinates, although its minimum is first sampled in a round with zero Grover iterations. Its worst-case branch-preparation fidelity of 0.744 falls below the declared target, identifying coherent ground-state access as the current bottleneck. QDMin inherits expected $O(\sqrt{N_q})$ candidate-query scaling in the unstructured model; total advantage depends on the many-body oracle cost and remains unestablished.
☆ Complex potential and the thermal width of quarkonium in quark-gluon plasma
Rasmus Normann Larsen, Peter Petreczky, Jorge Luis Dasilva Golan, Johannes H. Weber
We study the complex heavy quark anti-quark potential in lattice 2+1 flavor QCD at non-zero temperature. We point out a close relation between the imaginary part of the potential and the thermal quarkonium width. Using this relation, we estimate the thermal width of charmonia and bottomonia at high temperatures, which are not yet accessible with direct lattice QCD calculations of the quarkonium correlation functions and compare these to the results of the T-matrix analysis. For some of the excited quarkonia states, our estimates of the thermal width are smaller than the ones obtained in the T-matrix analysis.
☆ Comments on $\bf{η'}$ nuclei and on the $Λ$ binding energy of the hypertriton
Avraham Gal
I briefly discuss two apparent puzzles: (i) is the observation of $η'$(958) bound states in $^{11}$C at GSI [1] compatible with a nearly vanishing real part of $η'N$ scattering length [2]? and (ii) is the $Λ$ binding energy of the hypertriton (${{_Λ}^3}$H), the lightest particle-stable hypernucleus, very small (63$^{+38}_{-31}$ keV, J-PARC E73 [3]) or very large (523$\pm$76 keV, MAMI [4])? Here, I suggest that MAMI's observed weak-decay pion momentum peak originates from ${{_Λ}^7}$He, not from ${{_Λ}^3}$H \cite{Gal26}.

☆ Inverse Problem Approach for Non-Perturbative QCD: Applications
Yong Zheng, Ao-Sheng Xiong, Fu-Sheng Yu, Ting Wei
In arXiv:2211.13753 we proposed a novel theoretical approach for non-perturbative QCD, named the inverse problem approach. It extracts non-perturbative quantities by solving a dispersion integral equation as an inverse problem, using perturbative QCD and operator product expansion as inputs. In this work, we apply this approach to the pion and $a_1(1260)$ decay constants, as well as the continuum spectral function. The extracted $f_π= 130.8 \pm 8.1$ MeV agrees with the experimental value, and the reconstructed spectral function reproduces the ALEPH $τ$-decay data from threshold up to $s \simeq 3$ GeV$^2$. The advantages of this approach are as follows: (i) the whole non-perturbative range is solved simultaneously, yielding the ground state, excited states, and the continuum spectrum within a single framework; (ii) it is based on rigorous mathematics, with not only statistical but also systematic uncertainties well controlled and quantifiable; (iii) the regularized solutions exhibit convergence, allowing the precision to be systematically improved with better inputs; (iv) quark-hadron duality emerges naturally at high energy scales, avoiding the low-energy duality assumption and the Borel transformation, and eliminating their associated uncertainties. Finally, the successful physical application of the inverse problem approach demonstrates its broad applicability to non-perturbative quantities.

T. Beck, T. Stetz, N. Gavrielov, N. Pietralla, V. Werner, K. Yanase, M. Boromiza, A. Coman, C. Costache, N. M. Florea, I. Gheorghe, A. Ionescu, R. Lica, N. Mărginean, R. Mărginean, H. Mayr, C. Mihai, R. E. Mihai, A. Mitu, C. R. Nita, T. Otsuka, O. Papst, S. Pascu, C. Sotty, L. Stan, S. Toma, Y. Tsunoda, A. Turturică, S. Ujeniuc, J. Wiederhold
Lifetimes of excited states of the nucleus $^{96}$Zr were studied with the Doppler-shift attenuation method following the $^{94}$Zr($^{18}$O,$^{16}$O)$^{96}$Zr two-neutron transfer reaction. The obtained $B(E2;2^+_2\to0^+_2)$ and $B(E2;4^+_1\to2^+_2)$ transition strengths, amounting to $26(2)$ and $39(7)$\,W.u., respectively, firmly attribute the $2^+_2$ and $4^+_1$ states to the collective intruder band built on top of the $0^+_2$ state. The nature of this structure is discussed against predictions of the collective model using the Bohr Hamiltonian, the interacting boson model with configuration mixing, and the quasiparticle vacua shell model. The collective, interband $B(E2;4^+_1\to2^+_1)=11.2(8)$\,W.u. transition strength, refuting the previously assumed purity of both structures, is reproduced in the calculations. The quasiparticle vacua shell model predicts, in agreement with a simple two-state model based on experimental $E2$ transition strengths, considerable mixing between the normal and intruder $2^+$ states.

☆ Learning nuclear mass systematics with hybrid quantum-classical mixtures of experts
Shijiang Ji, Heyi Yang, Zu-Xing Yang, Xiao-Hua Fan, Zhi-Pan Li, Haozhao Liang
We introduce a mixture-of-experts framework combining sixteen hybrid quantum-classical neural networks with nucleus-dependent classical gating to learn residual corrections to the WS4 nuclear mass model. On a fixed AME2020 test set, the framework reduces the root-mean-square error from 456.22 to 179.83 keV and outperforms a parameter-matched classical counterpart. The learned corrections improve shell-gap systematics near the Sn and Pb shell closures, while analysis of the gating networks identifies shell-related descriptors as the leading inputs. For 66Ca, the model predicts Sn = 0.577 MeV and S2n = -0.252 MeV, allowing two-neutron emission while the one-neutron channel remains closed.
☆ $P$--wave quarkonia in jets at the LHC
Taewook Ha, Byungsik Hong, Daekyoung Kang, Soohwan Lee, Bayu Adi Nugraha Putra
We present the first systematic theoretical study of the production of $P$-wave charmonium states $χ_{cJ}$ and bottomonium states $χ_{bJ}(nP)$ within jets at the LHC using the fragmenting jet function framework at next-to-leading order in $α_s$. Our calculation resums both collinear DGLAP logarithms and threshold double logarithms in the fragmentation functions and accounts for feeddown contributions from higher quarkonium states. We observe a notable contrast between the charmonium and bottomonium sectors. For $χ_{bJ}(nP)$, the normalized momentum-fraction distributions exhibit a nearly universal shape, with remarkably weak dependence on the choice of long-distance matrix element sets, the radial excitation ($n=1,2,3$), and the total angular momentum ($J=0,1,2$). We attribute this universality to the overwhelming dominance of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ fragmentation channel, while feeddown contributions from higher bottomonium states remain small. In contrast, the shape of $χ_{cJ}$ distributions exhibits a stronger dependence on the matrix-element set, reflecting the different relative contributions of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ and ${}^3P_J^{[1]}$ channels. We provide predictions for the $χ_{cJ}$ and $χ_{bJ}(nP)$ distributions for the CMS and LHCb kinematic selections across a range of jet transverse momenta. We also compare our predictions with \textsc{Pythia}~8 simulations for selected $P$-wave quarkonium states.

☆ Deposition of $α$ clusters on the surface of $^{28}$Si
W. Horiuchi, N. Itagaki, Y. Yamaguchi
The possibility of the appearance of the clustering structure in the surface is one of the key features determining the nuclear structural properties. In this work, we study the ground-state structure of $^{28}\text{Si}$ using the antisymmetrized quasicluster model (AQCM), focusing on the deposition of the $α$ cluster structure on the surface. Three candidate structural configurations constrained to reproduce the experimental charge radius are investigated based on the $\text{SU}(3)$ shell model, the $j$-$j$ coupling shell model, and a localized $7α$ cluster model. Using Glauber-model calculations for intermediate-energy proton elastic scattering, we demonstrate that the angular distribution at and beyond the first diffraction peak is highly sensitive to surface diffuseness, and that the $7α$ cluster model configuration best reproduces the experimental data due to its sharper surface profile. Also, the elastic charge form factors from electron scattering support the existence of the cluster-induced oblately deformed structure.

☆ The effect of Coulomb interaction on Levy source parameters
Kristof Csiki, Mate Csanad, Barnabas Porfy
Femtoscopy plays an important role in the study of heavy-ion collisions and particle sources generated within them. In both experimental measurements and theoretical models, a Lévy distribution is used to describe the shape of the source, as the Gaussian distribution has proven to be inaccurate based on experimental observations. Despite this, there are still discrepancies between experimental data and the results of theoretical models. One reason may be that these theoretical models either approximate the Coulomb interaction poorly or omit it entirely. In our research, we focused on how the Coulomb effect influences the stability index $α$ value of the Lévy distribution. For this, we used a custom-developed simulation framework written in C++ and Python. The C++ module integrates the equations of motion for relativistic pions using the Leapfrog algorithm, while the Python post-processing script generates the two-particle spatial source function from the phase-space coordinates. We investigate the ratio and slope of the generated and pair-source fitted $α$ as a function of the number of particles, fitting range, and the initial source size and density.

☆ Glashow-Weinberg relation in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter
Kihong Kwon, Daisuke Jido, Yamato Suda
The conservation of the axial-vector currents in nuclear matter with finite isospin asymmetry $ρ_n/ρ_p$ is explored in this paper. In explicit calculations in the in-medium chiral perturbation theory, a charged pion becomes massive in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter. In the presence of the massive charged pion, two components of the axial-vector current are not conserved from the two-loop order when applying the massive in-medium pion state. As a result, the in-medium Glashow-Weinberg relation for the charged pions cannot be derived in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter from operator relations in quantum chromodynamics.
☆ Absorption of bound supernova axion-like particles by the neutron star weakens the heating limits on their photon coupling
Probit J Kalita, Subha Mitra, Bharat Kumar
Axion-like particles (ALPs) that couple to protons are produced in a core-collapse supernova, and the slow ones remain bound to the new neutron star. Bose, Ganguly, Kumar, and Raj [arXiv:2610.30255] proposed that the photons from the decay of this bound cloud reheat old neutron stars, and they derived strong limits on the ALP-photon coupling. They neglected the absorption of the ALPs by the star, but a bound ALP on an orbit that enters the star and reaches 50 km crosses it about $6\times 10^{18}$ times over the 333 Myr age of PSR J2144$-$3933. We show that inverse nucleon bremsstrahlung in the cold star absorbs every ALP whose orbit enters it within minutes, long before it decays, so only ALPs born outside the final star on nearly circular orbits survive; they carry $9\times 10^{-9} - 6\times 10^{-5}$ of the heating. We compute the protoneutron-star evolution, the production, the general-relativistic orbits and the absorption ourselves, for twelve protoneutron-star evolutions, three nucleon-bremsstrahlung rates normalized to the same supernova energy loss of light ALPs, and equations of state with and without $Δ(1232)$ isobars. PSR J2144$-$3933 still excludes a window at $m_a\simeq 7.7-196$\ MeV, with a lower edge in the photon coupling $280-700$ times higher than without absorption. Pion conversion and the $Δ(1232)$ resonance, which raise the production of surviving ALPs more than their absorption, widen this window to $m_a\simeq$ $7.7-260$\ MeV. The window depends at similar levels on the bremsstrahlung rate and on the radius of the final star. It requires a direct photon coupling that cancels the one induced by ALP-pion mixing, and existing supernova gamma-ray limits may already cover it.
☆ Irreducible representations of $SU(3)$ for nucleons in a oscillator shell $η$ with $η\le 8$: Application to nuclei with proxy-$SU(4)$ symmetry
V. K. B. Kota
Applying some simple rules, established in group theory literature, generated are codes (easy to modify as required) for obtaining $SU(3)$ irreducible representations (irreps) for a given number of nucleons in a given oscillator shell $η$ with $η\le 8$. In this approach, first the $SU(3)$ irreps are obtained for spinless fermions in a given $η$ shell. Using the codes developed, tables of $SU(3)$ irreps are generated for identical nucleons (protons or neutrons) with a given total spin $S$. Similarly, the $SU(3)$ irreps are generated for nucleons with a given spin-isospin $SU(4)$ irrep. Some applications of these tables for $η=4$ shell for $52 \le \mbox{Z,N} \le 78$ nuclei with proxy-$SU(4)$ symmetry are presented. Also, the procedure used for the shell model $SU(3)$ limits is easy to be extended for the $SU(3)$ limit of various interacting boson models and some examples for these are also presented.

☆ Effects of the $a_0(980)$ Meson on Finite Nuclei in a Parity Doublet Model
Yuk Kei Kong, Youngman Kim, Masayasu Harada
We investigate nuclear structure within the parity doublet model (PDM), with particular emphasis on the role of the isovector-scalar $a_0(980)$ meson. We adopt the models with and without the $a_0$ meson and fit their parameters to nuclear matter saturation and ground state properties of selected nuclei, subject to constraints from the vacuum. The resulting parameter sets reproduce the nuclear matter saturation properties and provide a good description of binding energies and charge radii of selected nuclei. Our fits show that a large value of the chiral invariant mass of nucleon is preferred by the fitting: the best fitted value is $m_0 = 689 \pm 71 $ MeV with $a_0$ and $m_0 = 689 \pm 69 $ MeV without $a_0$. We find that the effects of the $a_0$ meson on the binding energies and charge radii are negligibly small. It is difficult to clarify the effect of $a_0$ meson to neutron skin thickness of Sn, Pb, and Ca isotopes, due to the large uncertainty of the predictions. We note that our prediction of $^{208} \text{Pb}$ is consistent with the measurement by PREX-II collaboration, while that of $^{48} \text{Ca}$ cannot explain the CREX result.
☆ Enhanced structure-dependent alpha decay tunneling in deformed odd-odd nuclei via intense two-color laser pulses
Jun-Hao Cheng, Qiong Xiao, Liang Gao, Tong-Pu Yu
In the present work, we investigate the effect of ultra-intense laser fields on the $α$ decay tunneling of deformed odd-odd nuclei. Calculations performed within the deformed density-dependent cluster model show that, for deformed odd-odd $α$ emitters, the laser-induced variation in the penetration probability separates into distinct branches associated with different valence particle-hole configurations relative to the $Z=82$ and $N=126$ shell closures. In contrast to the even-even and odd-$A$ cases, the odd-odd parent nucleus most sensitive to the laser field is not the one with the lowest $α$ decay energy. This indicates that the laser response is governed not only by $Q_α$ but also by structural correlations associated with the simultaneously unpaired proton and neutron. We further examine the pulse-averaged response under a two-color laser field. The results show that an optimized two-color field enhances the pulse-averaged laser response for most of the studied nuclei, while highly sensitive nuclei exhibit an effective gain equivalent to increasing the laser intensity by more than one order of magnitude. These findings identify structural determinants of laser-assisted $α$ decay in odd-odd nuclei and provide guidance for selecting candidate nuclei and optimizing laser parameters in future experiments.

☆ Muon-to-positron conversion from light Majorana neutrino exchange: nuclear responses and pion-pole-improved multipoles
Yi Liao, Hao-Lin Wang
We study muon-to-positron conversion in nuclei that is mediated by light Majorana neutrinos, which probes lepton-number violation in the electron-muon sector. As the second paper in a series, this work extends our study of local dimension-nine interactions to the mass mechanism. We derive the conversion amplitude from the second-order effective four-Fermi interaction and express it in terms of nuclear responses in the one-body impulse approximation. Using phenomenological nucleon form factors, we retain convection, axial charge, weak magnetism, and the longitudinal pion-pole current in a specified pion-pole-improved prescription. The two physical time orderings and the distinct momentum transfers are derived in the intermediate-state response. We complete its angular reduction and derive the corresponding closure operator, including spin-gradient terms. Both the symmetric (scalar) and antisymmetric (vector) lepton-hadron Lorentz contractions contribute to the spin-averaged, angle-integrated rate. For $0^+\!\to0^+$ transitions we give explicit formulas in terms of two coherent radial amplitudes, without restricting the intermediate nuclei to spin zero. This provides an interface to nuclear calculations of the required nuclear matrix elements. However, in this work, no isotope-specific numerical predictions are attempted. The present treatment uses approximate lepton wavefunctions and recoil-free nuclear propagation. Two-body weak currents and systematic chiral effective-field-theory matching are left for future work.

☆ Proton GTMDs and Wigner Distributions in the Chiral Quark Soliton Model: Orbital Angular Momentum and Spin-Orbit Correlation with Sea Quarks
Josuke Minamiguchi, Tomoya Uji
We calculate the leading-twist vector and axial-vector quark generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) of the proton in the chiral quark soliton model, including both the discrete valence level and the regularized Dirac sea. We consider the isosinglet and isotriplet combinations of GTMDs at zero and nonzero skewness. At zero skewness, we construct Wigner distributions and resolve the orbital angular momentum (OAM) and spin-orbit correlation (SOC) densities in transverse position and momentum space, separately for quarks and antiquarks. This provides a phase-space picture of the sea-quark and sea-antiquark contributions, displaying OAM aligned with the proton spin and anti-aligned with the partons' own spin.

♻ ☆ Why Stellar Sequences Turn Over: Fixed Points, Instability, and Equation-of-State Universality
Isaac Legred, Nicolas Yunes
We reformulate the stellar structure equations in the language of dynamical systems and show that the maximum mass of stellar sequences arises from the existence of a fixed point in the relativistic regime. In an appropriate representation of the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, this fixed point becomes manifest and is directly associated with the turnover of the mass-radius curve. The existence of a fixed point implies an effective reduction in dimensionality near the onset of instability, which provides a simple explanation for several equation-of-state-insensitive relations and predicts new ones. In the weakly relativistic limit, we identify a complementary universal structure shared by stellar sequences at their maximum mass, which we term the "compressible limit," and derive distinct universal relations governing the maximum mass in the Newtonian and post-Newtonian regimes. Combining these theoretical results with current astrophysical constraints, we show that the J0740+6620 pulsar is unlikely to lie near the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff maximum mass unless the equation of state exhibits a strong first-order phase transition at densities just above its central density.

♻ ☆ A short-range effective theory for single-neutron halo nuclei with a deformed core
Live-Palm Kubushishi, Daniel R. Phillips
We establish a short-range effective theory for deformed s-wave halos. The theory applies to a system in which neutrons are weakly bound to a core nucleus, and that core nucleus also exhibits a low-lying rotational band with a $0^+$ ground state and a first $2_1^+$ excited state. The effective theory then must have both halo degrees of freedom and degrees of freedom associated with rotation of the core. This leads to the particle plus rotor model of Bohr and Mottelson at leading order. We identify the relevant leading-order operators in the Hamiltonian that respect the symmetries of the system and the small parameters which define the effective theory's power counting. We carry out calculations for the $^{11}$Be and $^{17}$C systems in which we compute the low-lying positive-parity states of the core $+$ neutron systems up to the core$(2_1^+)$-neutron threshold. We do this for several different regulator parameters and establish that these energies can be renormalized using the leading-order set of operators. The spectrum is accurately described at leading order in both cases. Decay widths to d-wave core-neutron states have sizable cutoff dependence, but the Asymptotic Normalization Coefficients (ANCs) in $s$-wave channels exhibit regulator dependence of a size consistent with next-to-leading-order effects. We also compute Coulomb breakup observables and compare with experimental data, finding leading-order results in reasonable agreement with data for both ${}^{11}$Be and ${}^{17}$C. The addition of one next-to-leading-order operator renders the ANCs of all s-wave states stable with respect to the regulator. It consequently also removes most of the 30\% variation of the leading-order Coulomb dissociation cross section with the regulator.

♻ ☆ Parameter adjustment of nuclear leading-order local pairing energy density functionals
Michael Bender, Karim Bennaceur, Valentin Guillon
(See paper for full abstract) This study reports on the benchmarking of a protocol for the adjustment of the parameters of a local leading-order (LO) T=1 (like-particle) pairing EDF that consists in adjusting the density-dependence of the 1S0 pairing gap at the chemical potential in infinite nuclear matter (INM). When using a suitably chosen reference calculation, this protocol leads to consistent results for the odd-even staggering of masses of spherical and heavy deformed nuclei and also for the rotational moments of inertia calculated in a time-reversal-breaking cranked HFB approach. The implementation of the HFB solver for infinite matter at arbitrary isospin asymmetry used for this study is sketched in appendices. Additional points that are discussed concern (i) the illustration that the gaps at the chemical potential are not necessarily sufficient to completely characterise the pairing interaction in infinite matter, and that adjusting LO pairing EDF to reproduce gaps obtained from finite-range pairing interactions in HFB or from more microscopic calculations can lead to unrealistic predictions for finite nuclei; (ii) the finding that some regions of the parameter space for the density dependence of the T=1 LO pairing EDF lead to a spurious transition to a Bose-Einstein condensate of di-nucleons in spite of producing realistic pairing correlations for well-bound nuclei; (iii) the correlation between effective mass and the parameters of the LO pairing EDF that control the form factor of the density dependence when reproducing pairing gaps in infinite matter, (iv) the significant impact on the odd-even staggering of masses made by either including or not the spin-gradient terms in the particle-hole part of the Skyrme EDF; (v) the sizeable impact of keeping or not the contribution from the density-dependent LO pairing EDF to the mean fields on the odd-even staggering of radii.

♻ ☆ Systematic Study of Proton, Two-Proton, Alpha, and Cluster Radioactivity Half-Lives based on the Deformed Gamow-like Model and Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network ($\mathrm{TabPFN}$)
Anqi Yang, Panpan Qi, Qingning Yuan, Gongming Yu, Haitao Yang, Zhangyan Li, Yanbing Cai
A hybrid framework combining the deformed Gamow-like model ($\mathrm{DGLM}$) with the Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network ($\mathrm{TabPFN}$) is developed to improve half-life predictions for two-proton emission, proton emission, $α$ decay, and cluster radioactivity. A total of 583 radioactive nuclei are investigated, including 17 two-proton emitters, 42 proton emitters, 498 $α$ emitters, and 26 cluster emitters. Among the four considered models, $\mathrm{DGLM}^{b}+\mathrm{TabPFN}$ achieves the best overall performance, with $σ_{\mathrm{RMS}}=0.423$, corresponding to an improvement of approximately $82.2\%$ over $\mathrm{DGLM}^{b}$. The model parameters are optimized for each decay mode using the least-squares method. After introducing $\mathrm{TabPFN}$, the prediction errors for proton emission and $α$ decay are reduced by approximately $80.6\%$ and $87.6\%$, respectively. For $α$ decay, the training, test, and overall RMSEs are 0.208, 0.305, and 0.240, indicating good generalization capability without evident overfitting. The model also reproduces the systematic evolution of $α$-decay half-lives and the shell-closure effect around $N=126$. These results demonstrate that combining $\mathrm{DGLM}$ with $\mathrm{TabPFN}$ significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of radioactive-decay half-life predictions while retaining the physical interpretability of the original model.

☆ {DEMAND}: {A}n organic glass scintillator array for direct measurements of $(α,n)$ and $(p,n)$ reactions in inverse kinematics
G. Christian, B. J. Reed, G. Lotay, G. Bartram, S. Blackmore, D. T. Doherty, A. Katrusiak, J. Henderson, D. A. Hutcheon, A. Lennarz, M. Loria, J. O'Neill, C. O'Shea, C. J. Paxman, C. Ruiz, L. Wagner, M. Williams
We have developed an array of up to 20 organic glass scintillator detectors, each consisting of a $3~\mathrm{cm}\times3~\mathrm{cm}\times3~\mathrm{cm}$ scintillator cube coupled to a photomultiplier tube. Sensitive to neutrons from a few hundred keV to several tens of MeV, the array was designed for use with recoil separators in inverse-kinematics measurements of astrophysical $(α,n)$ and $(p,n)$ reactions. It provides a prompt start signal for identifying recoil-neutron coincidences from the recoil time of flight. We characterize eight detectors used in an inverse-kinematics measurement of $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(α,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$, using source and in-beam data. From the widths of $γ$-ray Compton-edge peaks at 311, 341, 477, and 1062 keVee, we find an energy resolution described by $\mathrm{FWHM}(E)/E=\sqrt{A^2/E+B^2/E^2+C^2}$, with $A=0.00(7)$, $B=0.0618(54)$, and $C=0.135(5)$. The time-difference spectrum of nearest-neighbor $γ$-$γ$ coincidences from a $^{22}\mathrm{Na}$ source (250--600 keVee) gives a FWHM coincidence timing resolution of $910(40)$ ps, corresponding to a single-detector resolution of $640(30)$ ps. Mixed neutron-$γ$ fields from the in-beam reaction and a $^{241}\mathrm{AmBe}$ source show pulse-shape discrimination with an $n$-$γ$ figure of merit $>1$ down to about 100 keVee. Below 100 keVee, the total neutron yield can still be extracted using two-Gaussian fits to energy-gated pulse-shape discrimination spectra. Monte Carlo simulations of the present $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(α,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$ measurement give a neutron singles detection efficiency of $1.56(45)%$, with uncertainty dominated by systematic effects in the simulation inputs.

☆ Neutron spectrometry of (p,n) based neutron fields at the University of Helsinki using the NCT-WES single-moderator directional spectrometer

NCT-WES (Neutron Capture Therapy Wide Energy Spectrometer) is a recently developed single-moderator neutron spectrometer with a sharply directional response, and it is a very convenient instrument to characterise neutron facilities, as it determines the whole spectrum in a single exposure, and has a low sensitivity to room-scattering. The data acquired with NCT-WES were unfolded using the FRUIT unfolding code, starting from guess spectra obtained from \texttt{GEANT4} or \texttt{MCNP6} simulations. The unfolding analysis showed that both transport codes produced plausible spectra, \texttt{MCNP6} being more accurate for the 1960 and 2040 keV irradiations and \texttt{GEANT4} for 2310 keV. We show that a rich dataset spanning multiple transitions enables a test of a restricted isotope-shift ansatz comprising the leading mass and field shifts, one effective factorized higher-order Standard Model contribution, and a new-particle contribution. Within this ansatz, the five-transition data are inconsistent with the new-particle contribution serving as the sole additional contribution over the mass ranges $m_φ\leq 6.5$ keV and $18$ keV $\leq m_φ< 100$ keV, while the previous works rely on another bound set by the neutron scattering and $(g-2)_e$ measurements. ♻ ☆ Performance Benchmarks for 2-View and 3-View Fiber-Projection Fine-Grained Particle Detectors
Haohui Che, Guang Yang
Fine-grained scintillator detectors are critical for precision measurements in nuclear and particle physics, where accurate reconstruction of interaction vertices and secondary particle directions enables separation of signal from background events. A well-known design choice is the fiber readout geometry: traditional 2-View systems use orthogonal X and Y fibers, while next-generation 3-View designs add a third Z-fiber layer that provides unambiguous 3D voxel identification. The 2-View approach suffers from combinatorial ''ghost hits'', which are false 3D candidates arising from fiber projection ambiguities, that degrade reconstruction performance in high-multiplicity events. This paper presents comprehensive simulation benchmarks quantifying the performance difference between 2-View and 3-View geometries across key metrics. We find that the 3-View geometry reduces ghost hits by 30 to 90% depending on event topology, provides robust vertex resolution across complex topologies, and maintains superior angular resolution for shower direction reconstruction. These benchmarks inform the design optimization of future detectors and provide quantitative guidance for reconstruction algorithm development across a broad range of experiments including neutrino physics, rare kaon/pion decays, and collider calorimetry.

☆ A Lighter QCD-Axion from Small Instantons
Sourav Bera, Susobhan Chattopadhyay, Rick S. Gupta
We propose models where the QCD axion mass can be much smaller than the standard expectation. We show that this is possible in models where both QCD and the Standard Model flavor structure get modified in the ultraviolet (UV). In these models, both the axion mass and the up-quark Yukawa can receive sizeable non-perturbative contributions from instantons in the UV. If both these effects are carefully taken into account, the QCD axion is not necessarily heavier than usual expectations and can, in fact, be much lighter. We show that if small instanton contributions account for a large fraction of the up-quark Yukawa, the QCD axion can be lighter than standard expectations whereas it is heavier otherwise. We propose two different models where this condition is realised: (1) one where the QCD gauge group emerges as a subgroup from a product of $SU(3)$ groups in the UV; and (2) a composite Higgs model that also implements partial compositeness. In both these models the QCD axion can lie not only in the region to the right of the QCD axion band but also far to its left. This is especially relevant for a range of proposed haloscope and helioscope experiments that will probe a region mostly to the left of the QCD band.

☆ On Geometric Observables in Gravity
Manthos Karydas, Murat Kologlu, Allic Sivaramakrishnan
Measures of geometry like distance and time are staples of classical gravity. While geometric quantities arise broadly in quantum gravity, their graviton corrections are less explored. In this paper, we study geometric observables in perturbative quantum gravity. We form distance and time observables that model measurements, including in the presence of spacetime fluctuations. Gravitational dressing ensures these constructions are coordinate invariant. Then we show how these finite-distance observables become memory and Shapiro time delay operators upon taking asymptotic limits. We compute leading graviton effects in correlators of geometric observables throughout. Altogether, our results identify a class of geometric observables that link experiments and operations on the celestial sphere.

☆ Gravity between two masses beyond Newton's law

Newton's law of universal gravitation describes the attraction between two masses through an inverse-distance potential. In Einstein's theory gravity gravitates: each mass reshapes the spacetime geometry through which the other acts. More than a century later, extracting the two-body interaction from this coupled geometry remains a fundamental analytical challenge. Even without motion or radiation, the static sector of the interaction harbours an infinite hierarchy of field couplings: the purest laboratory for gravitational non-linearity. Here we determine the static interaction from ninth to twelfth order in Newton's constant for arbitrary mass ratios, and derive a closed expression for the first backreaction beyond the Schwarzschild test-body limit to all orders in the gravitational coupling. We achieve both advances by formulating the problem around the stationary interaction energy. An exact one-body background resums one source's self-interaction, stationarity reduces the fields required from the other, and integrated response identities reveal cancellations across the coupled modes. Complementary expansions then resolve the complete mass dependence at finite order. Together, these results bridge the gap between an infinitesimal probe and comparable masses, exposing hidden analytical simplicity within Einstein's theory and providing essential building blocks for modelling orbital dynamics and gravitational-wave generation.

In this work, we investigate the gravitational wave signatures of hyperonic neutron stars containing $Δ$ baryons within a density-dependent relativistic mean-field framework based on the DDME2 parametrization. Within this framework, the baryons interact among themselves via mesons. For $Δ$ baryons, the interaction is uncertain to date. We investigate how variations of the scalar and vector $Δ-$meson couplings, subject to \(x_{σΔ}-x_{ωΔ}=0.2\), modify the tidal properties and inspiral gravitational-wave signals. These waveform differences arise through changes in tidal deformability and are not unique signatures of $Δ$ resonances. Our calculation tests, at two loops, the recursive subtraction of ultraviolet subdivergences and the cancellation of infrared singularities between virtual and real contributions in a framework that does not rely on analytical continuation in spacetime dimension. After renormalization and phase-space integration, the regulator-dependent logarithms cancel and the known $N_f$ contribution to the inclusive rate is recovered. The result provides a non-trivial NNLO check of gauge invariance, renormalization consistency, and perturbative unitarity in IReg. In precision multi-loop calculations, fixed-dimension regularization methods can be advantageous by avoiding the dimensional continuation of intrinsically four-dimensional structures, such as $γ_5$ matrices and Levi-Civita tensors, thereby reducing ambiguities and symmetry-restoring counterterms.

Exceptional points (EPs), at which two quasinormal frequencies and their eigenvectors coalesce, can strongly enhance the spectral instability of black hole quasinormal modes. We investigate this behavior in Kerr--Newman spacetimes through pseudospectra and condition numbers for neutral massless scalar fields and coupled gravitoelectromagnetic (GE) perturbations. For the scalar field, we follow the $(\ell,m)=(1,1)$ spheroidal branch and derive the energy norm from the stress-energy tensor. For GE perturbations, we use a coupled four-field system equipped with a positive radiative energy. At the selected near-EP backgrounds, the condition numbers of both modes in the close pair exceed those of the two more-damped modes shown for comparison at the same background. Along a matched GE parameter path, the frequency splitting follows a square-root law and the condition numbers grow as the inverse square root of the distance to the EP. The pseudospectral contours resolve the transition from individual-mode sensitivity to the collective response of the pair. Within the discretized problems and energy norms considered here, these results quantify the amplification of spectral instability near EPs and provide a basis for studying their contribution to black-hole ringdown.

Within the standard ncdm module, the DFA significantly outperforms the default CLASS fluid approximation in the cross and neutrino power spectra, and reduces errors in the cold dark matter power spectrum by up to an order of magnitude, while adding only 1-4% to the total runtime. Combined with the DFA and tested on massive neutrinos, the GBH reproduces the matter power spectrum to better than permille accuracy and cosmological parameter constraints to better than 0.05 sigma, at a computational cost comparable to that of the standard implementation. We argue that the GBH is particularly well suited to non-thermal relics whose distribution function varies with time or across parameter space. Our implementation of both the DFA and the GBH in CLASS is publicly available at https://github.com/aradn97/class_GBH.

☆ Probabilistic Energy-Based Neural Networks for Uncertainty-Aware Collider Data Analyses
Raymundo Ramos, Ahmed Hammad, Amit Chakraborty, Pyungwon Ko, Stefano Moretti
We introduce a probabilistic energy-based Neural Network (NN) for uncertainty-aware classification in collider analyses. Standard discriminative classifiers can give highly confident predictions even for events that are different from the data used during training. Energy-Based Models provide an alternative by assigning an energy score to each event, which measures how well the event agrees with the learned data distribution. In this framework, a NN maps the input features into a latent space, where the energy is defined with respect to class-specific embeddings. This allows the model to identify noisy, anomalous or shifted events while maintaining good classification performance. We first study the method using controlled synthetic examples and then test it in a realistic collider analysis based on the $h \to τ^+ τ^-$ process at the Large Hadron Collider, where $h$ is the discovered Standard Model Higgs boson. We show that the associated energy score can help identify events affected by mismodelling and/or systematic variations and can thus be used to define uncertainty-aware event selections. Although we use this specific Higgs process as a testbed, the method is general and can be applied to other collider classification problems where robustness against systematic and distributional uncertainties is important.

In this work, we apply this approach to the pion and $a_1(1260)$ decay constants, as well as the continuum spectral function. The extracted $f_π= 130.8 \pm 8.1$ MeV agrees with the experimental value, and the reconstructed spectral function reproduces the ALEPH $τ$-decay data from threshold up to $s \simeq 3$ GeV$^2$. The advantages of this approach are as follows: (i) the whole non-perturbative range is solved simultaneously, yielding the ground state, excited states, and the continuum spectrum within a single framework; (ii) it is based on rigorous mathematics, with not only statistical but also systematic uncertainties well controlled and quantifiable; (iii) the regularized solutions exhibit convergence, allowing the precision to be systematically improved with better inputs; (iv) quark-hadron duality emerges naturally at high energy scales, avoiding the low-energy duality assumption and the Borel transformation, and eliminating their associated uncertainties. In contrast, the shape of $χ_{cJ}$ distributions exhibits a stronger dependence on the matrix-element set, reflecting the different relative contributions of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ and ${}^3P_J^{[1]}$ channels. We provide predictions for the $χ_{cJ}$ and $χ_{bJ}(nP)$ distributions for the CMS and LHCb kinematic selections across a range of jet transverse momenta. The discrete no-monopole constraint is preserved to machine precision without staggered grids, even during BNS mergers with moving refinement regions. These results establish \texttt{RAKI} as a high-order, non-staggered GRMHD framework for accurate modelling of magnetic field evolution in neutron star mergers and its implications for multimessenger astrophysics.

The C++ module integrates the equations of motion for relativistic pions using the Leapfrog algorithm, while the Python post-processing script generates the two-particle spatial source function from the phase-space coordinates. We investigate the ratio and slope of the generated and pair-source fitted $α$ as a function of the number of particles, fitting range, and the initial source size and density.

This provides a phase-space picture of the sea-quark and sea-antiquark contributions, displaying OAM aligned with the proton spin and anti-aligned with the partons' own spin.

☆ Certified Access: Test-Time Compute on Conservative Physics-Structured AI Memory NeurIPS 2026
Pratik Jawahar, Riccardo Maggioni, Jonas Petersen, Matteo Cozzi, Gian-Alessandro Lombardi, Marek Gajewski, Camilla Mazzoleni, Federico Martelli
Test-time compute mechanisms, such as retries, confidence-based escalation and non-local routing, are conventionally deployed as black-box additions to trained models. They typically add forward passes or halting heads, but give no structural account of what the extra compute buys or what it costs against the model's stability guarantees. We therefore propose a theoretical and empirical framework for test-time compute on a Latent Dynamics Model used as the memory. When an encoder's latent state $(q,p)$ is advanced by a damped symplectic (velocity-Verlet) step of a learned Hamiltonian, every mechanism that expands access has an exact phase-volume Jacobian, a bounded energy change and an exact latch-transport law. We split reachability failures into escape failures and reach failures. A Lorentz squeeze resolves escape failures by injecting bounded, re-absorbable energy. A gated canonical translation (a one-step channel across $C_T$) resolves reach failures at $\detJ=1$ exactly. We verify this certificate stack on a designed analytic testbed. Reaching just beyond $C_T$ with the squeeze requires energy that grows quadratically in the excess distance. The gated channel's energy cost equals the potential difference between its endpoints, which is zero on the matched channel measured here, and so does not grow with distance in this testbed. An untrained state-replacing map annihilates phase volume and erases stored charge, while the gated channel transports it. On a learned physics-structured memory, we show calibrated compute rationing and evaluate the scaling limits of non-local routing against a physics-free baseline. The main contribution is the formalization and verification of the certificate stack, not benchmark performance.
comment: Accepted at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026); Workshop: Long-Context Foundation Models
☆ Off-lightcone Wilson-line operators in gradient flow at next-to-next-to-leading order
Xiang-Peng Wang
We consider gauge-invariant off-lightcone Wilson-line operators constructed from local fields connected by spacelike or timelike Wilson lines. The lattice evaluation of their matrix elements requires a suitable renormalization prescription. Gradient flow offers such a prescription and, by smoothing the fields, suppresses ultraviolet fluctuations and can reduce statistical noise. We use the previously established matching framework based on the one-dimensional auxiliary-field formalism. In the small-flow-time limit, this framework reduces the matching of nonlocal off-lightcone Wilson-line operators to that of local current operators. We calculate the matching coefficients for these local current operators from the gradient-flow scheme to the modified minimal subtraction ($\MS$) scheme through next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in QCD. Our results can be applied to lattice calculations of unpolarized and polarized quark and gluon quasi-parton distributions, as well as meson and baryon quasi-distribution amplitudes. They also apply to gluonic correlators entering quarkonium transport and heavy-quark momentum diffusion in the quark-gluon plasma (QGP). Further applications include quarkonium decay and production in potential nonrelativistic QCD (pNRQCD) and spin-dependent relativistic corrections to the static potential.

♻ ☆ Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
Tanmay Vachaspati, Anja Wachowitz
Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.

♻ ☆ Evolution of Binaries Under Stochastic Perturbations
Andrea Caputo, Giovanni Maria Tomaselli, Chris Hamilton
We develop a general Fokker-Planck framework describing the dynamical evolution of Keplerian binaries subjected to stochastic perturbations. The formalism provides an algorithmic way to obtain the Fokker-Planck drift and diffusion coefficients of any set of orbital variables given the statistics of the perturbations. We apply the method to three physically distinct regimes: adiabatic tidal perturbations, white-noise tidal perturbations, and impulsive encounters with a third body of arbitrary density profile. In each regime we provide explicit drift and diffusion coefficients for all six orbital elements, derive the associated evolution timescale, and obtain analytic steady-state distribution functions. Our results extend previous treatments by including the evolution of the binary's orientation, retaining the complete tensor structure of tidal correlators, treating non-pointlike perturbers, and resolving the exact geometry of impulsive encounters. The latter correction leads to a steady-state eccentricity distribution that is slightly sub-thermal. We also show how these equations can be applied directly in several astrophysical scenarios, including binaries perturbed by dark matter subhaloes, ultralight dark matter, and the interstellar medium. This work delivers both a complete mathematical framework and a practical toolkit for stochastic binary evolution, providing ready-to-evaluate equations to be applied directly to binary population data.

♻ ☆ Precision Isotope-Shift Measurement of the ${}^1S_0 \leftrightarrow {}^3P_2$ Transition and a Multi-Transition King-Plot Consistency Test
Taiki Ishiyama, Koki Ono, Reiji Asano, Hokuto Kawase, Tetsushi Takano, Ayaki Sunaga, Yasuhiro Yamamoto, Minoru Tanaka, Yoshiro Takahashi
We present precision spectroscopy and isotope shift measurement of the ${}^1S_0 \leftrightarrow {}^3P_2$ clock transition in neutral ytterbium ($\mathrm{Yb}$) atoms. By revealing a magic wavelength at $905.4(2)$ nm, we successfully achieve the atomic spectrum narrower than $100$ Hz. The interleaved clock operation between isotopes allows us to determine isotope shifts of four bosonic isotope pairs at Hz-level uncertainties, which is combined with those of other four ultra-narrow transitions in $\mathrm{Yb}$ and $\mathrm{Yb}^+$ to construct the King plot. We show that a rich dataset spanning multiple transitions enables a test of a restricted isotope-shift ansatz comprising the leading mass and field shifts, one effective factorized higher-order Standard Model contribution, and a new-particle contribution. Within this ansatz, the five-transition data are inconsistent with the new-particle contribution serving as the sole additional contribution over the mass ranges $m_φ\leq 6.5$ keV and $18$ keV $\leq m_φ< 100$ keV, while the previous works rely on another bound set by the neutron scattering and $(g-2)_e$ measurements. This work paves the way for the effective use of precision isotope shift data in the King plot analysis and stimulates further measurements in Yb and other elements.
♻ ☆ Walking Sudakov: From Cusp to Octagon
Luis F. Alday, Elisabetta Armanini, Andrei V. Belitsky, Kelian Häring, Alexander Zhiboedov
We study the Sudakov form factor and the four-point scattering amplitude on the Coulomb branch of planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM as functions of the Coulomb-branch parameters and kinematic invariants. This setup provides a controlled probe of the interpolation between on- and off-shell regimes of infrared-sensitive quantities in gauge theories. We identify a novel scaling limit in which both observables exhibit double-logarithmic behavior governed by a walking anomalous dimension. As the mass scales are varied, this walking anomalous dimension interpolates between the cusp anomalous dimension of the on-shell regime and the octagon anomalous dimension of the off-shell regime. Based on the explicit two-loop result and the expected all-order structure, we propose an all-loop form for the walking anomalous dimension both for the form factor and for the four-point scattering amplitude. These all-loop expressions depend on new, presently unknown functions of the 't Hooft coupling.

♻ ☆ Molien--Weyl Singlet Counting and BFSS$_2$--Factorization in Gaussian Matrix Quantum Mechanics
Badis Ydri
We study the singlet-sector structure of mass-deformed BFSS$_{d+1}$ matrix quantum mechanics by combining the large--\(d\) Gaussian reduction with the Molien--Weyl projection. The Gaussian reduction captures the bulk matrix dynamics through a gauged harmonic oscillator, while the Molien--Weyl integral imposes the Gauss law and reorganizes the physical Hilbert space into holonomy-projected singlet excitations. We show that the very-low-temperature bosonic singlet spectrum is universally controlled by the quadratic Gram operators \(\Tr(X_aX_b)\), whose number is \(d(d+1)/2\). For \(N=2\), this result is established by explicit residue computations and character methods; for \(N>2\), it is supported by the character analysis. Thus the infrared spectrum begins as a collection of BFSS$_2$--like Gram towers, although higher invariant structures generally modify the full partition function. We also give a Hamiltonian derivation of the exceptional exact factorization at \((d,N)=(2,2)\), where the BFSS$_3$ singlet partition function equals the cube of the BFSS$_2$ one for all temperatures. This rigidity is special to the \(SU(2)\) invariant tensor structure and distinguishes exact singlet factorization from the possibility of smooth deconfinement--like holonomy crossovers at finite $N$. Finally, we extend the Gram-counting picture to supersymmetric BFSS/BMN models and indicate how the Molien--Weyl formulation can benchmark Monte Carlo simulations in both \(X_a\)-space and holonomy space.

♻ ☆ Lepton Flavor Violating Higgs decays at the Compact Linear Collider
Francisca Garay, Gabriel Vega, Philipp Roloff
Lepton flavor violating Higgs decays could appear in scenarios beyond the Standard Model of particle physics. In this article, we study the sensitivity of a future Compact Linear Collider (CLIC) to such processes, namely, $h\rightarrow eμ$, $h\rightarrowτμ$, and $h\rightarrow eτ$. In the absence of any observation, 95\% CL\ upper limits in the region of $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-5}$ could be placed on the branching fractions of these processes, assuming integrated luminosities of $4$\,ab$^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=1.4$ TeV and $5$\,ab$^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=3$ TeV.
♻ ☆ Transferable Fast Calorimeter Shower Generation via Multi-Geometry Pre-training
Thorsten Buss, Henry Day-Hall, Frank Gaede, Gregor Kasieczka, Katja Krüger, Peter McKeown, Lorenzo Valente
Detailed Geant4 simulation of calorimeter showers dominates the computing budget of high-energy physics experiments. Deep generative surrogates reduce this cost, but they have remained tied to the detector they were trained on, so each new geometry needs a large in-domain dataset. We study whether a single point cloud shower generator can be pre-trained on multiple detectors and transferred to unseen calorimeters. The pre-training geometries come from synthetic geometric variation rather than real-detector data. We introduce SimpleBox, a family of $10^4$ box calorimeters spanning the plane of sampling fraction and longitudinal segmentation, and benchmark it against pre-training on realistic detectors. On a calorimeter unseen in pre-training, with $10^3$ target showers for fine-tuning, the two priors reduce the aggregated sliced Wasserstein distance to Geant4 by factors of 5.2 (synthetic) and 8.0 (realistic) relative to training from scratch. At larger target sizes the synthetic prior performs better than the realistic one. Geometric diversity alone is therefore a practical way to pre-train a transferable shower generator.

♻ ☆ Next-to-Leading Order corrections to the Next-to-Eikonal DIS structure functions
Tolga Altinoluk, Guillaume Beuf, Jules Favrel, Michael Fucilla
We compute next-to-leading order (NLO) corrections to next-to-eikonal (NEik) quark background contributions to DIS structure functions. Among NEik corrections, $t$-channel quark exchanges provide the lowest order contributions in $α_s$, and can be represented as insertions of the quark background field of the target. At NLO, we compute NEik corrections induced by both quark and gluon background fields, and suppressed by an explicit factor of $α_s$. We show that the NLO corrections to the NEik longitudinal structure function are finite, while those to the NEik transverse structure function exhibit rapidity and UV divergences. These divergences are analyzed, and the finite contributions are extracted.

♻ ☆ Radiative decays of the predicted P-wave $D\bar{D}^*$ molecular state: The $0^{-+}$ case
Qi Wu, Ming-Qi Cui, Zi-Li Yue, Dian-Yong Chen, Shi-Dong Liu, Gang Li
In the present work, we study the radiative decays of the $P$-wave $D\bar{D}^*$ molecular state $G_0$ with $I^G(J^{PC})=0^+(0^{-+})$ using a phenomenological Lagrangian approach. The molecular coupling is fixed by the compositeness condition with a Gaussian form factor. The partial widths for $G_0\to γγ$, $γJ/ψ$, $γψ(2S)$, $γh_c$, $γρ$, and $γω$ are evaluated. Our results show that the two-photon and $γh_c$ channels are highly suppressed, while $γJ/ψ$, $γψ(2S)$, and $γρ$ are of the order of a few keV, and $γω$ reaches several tens of keV, making it the dominant radiative mode. The ratios $Γ(G_0 \to γψ(2S))/Γ(G_0 \to γJ/ψ)$ and $Γ(G_0 \to γω)/Γ(G_0 \to γρ)$ are predicted to be $1-2.6$ and $3.4-5.4$, respectively, with mild parameter dependence. We also compare with hadronic decays and find that the total radiative decay width is lower than the hadronic decay widths by about one order of magnitude. We propose searching for $G_0$ in the sequential decay $Y(4230)\to γG_0 \to γωJ/ψ$, which is accessible to further experimental measurements by the BESIII, Belle II and LHCb Collaborations.

♻ ☆ Probing Axion-Photon Mixing with High-Resolution X-ray Spectroscopy
Yu Zhou, Jiejia Liu, Volodymyr Takhistov, Kazuhisa Mitsuda
Axion-like particles (ALPs) provide a compelling avenue for exploring physics beyond the Standard Model. In astrophysical magnetized plasmas an ALP-photon coupling $g_{aγ}$ induces energy-dependent oscillations in the photon survival probability that imprint modulations on emission spectra. X-ray observations of bright spectrally-smooth sources can provide particularly sensitive probes of ultralight ALPs with masses $m_a \lesssim 10^{-11}$ eV due to long propagation distances, strong magnetic fields and high photon statistics. We present a comprehensive forecast of ALP-photon conversion in three representative systems: (i) background active galactic nuclei (AGNs) observed through foreground intracluster magnetic fields, (ii) central AGNs within their host cluster halos and (iii) Galactic X-ray binaries viewed through the Milky Way field. Using detailed simulations we assess the prospective sensitivity of high-resolution X-ray missions including XRISM, Athena, and Arcus. For typical magnetic field configurations a 320 ks XRISM observation or an 8 ks Athena observation of the Perseus Cluster AGN NGC 1275 can reach down to $g_{aγ} \sim 5 \times 10^{-13}$ GeV$^{-1}$ at $m_a \lesssim 10^{-12}$ eV, surpassing the current best limit. We quantify the impact of magnetic field modeling, photon statistics, and spectral binning strategies. Our results demonstrate the scientific potential of future X-ray observatories to probe photon-ALP coupling in previously inaccessible parameter space, offering a powerful window into physics beyond the Standard Model.

♻ ☆ Deeply virtual meson production at HERA and at the EIC within the Color Glass Condensate EFT
Renaud Boussarie, Luigi Delle Rose, Michael Fucilla, Alessandro Papa, Lech Szymanowski, Samuel Wallon
Continuing our previous study of Deeply Virtual Meson Production (DVMP) at twist-3 accuracy, we derive compact expressions for all helicity amplitudes. We perform a phenomenological analysis of the helicity-amplitude ratio $\mathcal{A}^{11}/\mathcal{A}^{00}$ and of the spin-density matrix element $r_{00}^{04}$ within the Color Glass Condensate framework. Small-$x$ evolution is incorporated by numerically solving the running-coupling-and-collinearly-improved Balitsky-Kovchegov and Balitsky-Fadin-Kuraev-Lipatov equations with the McLerran-Venugopalan model as the initial condition. Our exploratory phenomenological study shows that parameters fitted to inclusive DIS data capture the shape of the measured helicity observables but overestimate their magnitude, indicating the need for a dedicated fit to exclusive data. To overcome its absence in the literature, we introduce an effective phenomenological matching prescription. Our results are then compared to HERA data, and predictions are presented for electron-lead collisions at the future Electron-Ion Collider. We discuss the impact of non-linear effects at low photon virtuality and the role of genuine higher-twist contributions associated with light vector meson distribution amplitudes, corresponding to higher-Fock-state components of the projectile.

♻ ☆ Four-Fermion Deformations on Line Defects in QED$_4$ with Yukawas
Alessandra D'Alise, Giulia Muco, Francesco Sannino
We elucidate the dynamics induced by a Wilson Line of charge $q$ and electron charge $e$ in $QED_4$ coupled to a real scalar via Yukawa interactions. We observe that there is a range of the fixed product $e^2 q$ with $e\rightarrow 0$ and $q\rightarrow \infty$ for which four-fermion operators play a dominant role for the dynamics of the theory. We uncover the fixed-point dynamics of the theory and analyze their critical behavior.
comment: Corrected the derivation of the fixed point analysis of the theory, added extra material and improved the overall paper and results. 29 pages in Latex
♻ ☆ A dynamical implementation of colour coherence for quenched jets in JEWEL
Korinna Zapp
Colour coherence affects the radiation pattern of hard partons both in vacuum and in a dense coloured background formed in heavy ion collisions. In vacuum evolution it leads to the well-known phenomenon of angular ordering, and in heavy ion collisions the appearance of a medium resolution scale strongly affects the way in which a fragmenting hard parton interacts with the background medium. In this paper I present the implementation of colour coherence in the JEWEL event generator for jet evolution in a dense medium. In each interaction between a hard parton and the medium it is checked whether the momentum transfer of the scattering is sufficient to resolve the colour dipole. In this way it is dynamically decided which structures stay coherent. Importantly, scatterings that resolve an individual parton disrupt the colour coherence, which affects the next splitting via the loss of angular ordering. This leads to a suppression of hard radiation, and consequently a reduction in overall scattering rate, which is the dominant source of effects of colour coherence observable in reconstructed jets. I discuss these modifications using the examples of nuclear modification factor, jet fragmentation function and jet-hadron correlations.

♻ ☆ Determination of the $η$-$η^{\prime}$ Mixing Angle from $F_{η^{(\prime)}γ}(Q^2)$ within the Self-consistent Light-front Quark Model
Shuai Xu
We study the $η$-$η^{\prime}$ system in the self-consistent light-front quark model (LFQM) with the quark flavor mixing scheme, where the single mixing angle is constrained by the transition form factors (TFFs) $F_{η^{(\prime)}γ}(Q^2)$. A continuous combined $χ^2$ fit to the CLEO and BABAR data gives $θ=41.55^{+0.57}_{-0.60}\,{}^\circ$, in close agreement with the recent LHCb result $(41.6^{+1.0}_{-1.2})^\circ$. Using this mixing angle, we calculate the decay constants, light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs), Gegenbauer moments, $ξ$-moments, transverse momentum moments, electromagnetic interaction radii and two-photon decay widths of the $η$ and $η^{\prime}$ mesons. The predicted $a_2^η$ and $\langleξ^2\rangle_η$ are consistent with the latest BABAR results, and the electromagnetic interaction radii also agree well with the A2 and BESIII measurements. These results demonstrate that TFF data strongly constrain the light-front description of the nonperturbative properties of the $η$-$η^{\prime}$ system. After the fit and LFQM-input uncertainties are propagated, the predicted widths are $0.428^{+0.038}_{-0.035}$ keV and $3.067^{+0.190}_{-0.180}$ keV for $η\toγγ$ and $η^{\prime}\toγγ$, respectively. The central values are lower than the corresponding experimental values, indicating that the real-photon point provides a more sensitive test of the absolute TFF normalization.

♻ ☆ Insight on confinement from the QCD effective charge
A. Deur
Like the Gell-Mann--Low coupling $α$ of QED, the effective charge $α_{g_1}$ is a physical, observable-defined running coupling that can serve as the QCD coupling $α_s$. It can be represented by an analytic form consistent with renormalization-group evolution, holographic light-front QCD (HLFQCD), and the world data on $α_s$. As an observable, $α_{g_1}$ has a physically relevant analytic structure that reflects the underlying partonic dynamics. It displays, in the long-distance regime, two imaginary conjugate singularities at $Q^2 = \pm iΛ_s^2$, with $Λ_s$ the QCD scale. To connect this structure to confinement, we combine known general relations between $α_{g_1}$ and the parton dressed propagators and vertices with a recent phenomenological representation of $α_{g_1}$ within HLFQCD. Since, unlike vertices, propagators characterize a field variation between separate locations, the two singularities are assigned to the propagators. This results in the parton propagators displaying a long-distance behavior $e^{-Λ_s |x|/\sqrt{2}} |x|^{-5/2 + d_a}$ where propagation is suppressed beyond distances of order $1/Λ_s$, as expected from confinement. This offers an intuitive interpretation of confinement as the suppression of QCD Green's functions at long distance.

♻ ☆ Revisiting predictions for cosmic-ray antinucleon fluxes from Galactic Dark Matter
Lorenzo Stefanuto, Mattia Di Mauro, Fiorenza Donato, Nicolao Fornengo, Jordan Koechler, David Maurin
The data on cosmic antiprotons have reached an outstanding precision on energies spanning from GeV to hundreds of TeV, thanks to the space-based AMS-02 experiment. The balloon-borne GAPS experiment, which just completed its first Antarctic flight, will address antiproton and antideuteron fluxes well below GeV energies. Antinuclei in cosmic rays, as well as being produced by spallation reactions between cosmic-ray nuclei and the atoms of the interstellar medium, may hide contributions from exotic sources, such as particle dark matter annihilation in the Galaxy. In this paper, we present predictions for cosmic antiproton, antideuteron and antihelium fluxes both from secondary and dark matter origin. We use state-of-the-art production spectra, nuclear coalescence for antinuclei, and Galactic propagation models to derive upper limits on the dark matter annihilation cross-section from AMS-02 antiproton data in different propagation scenarios (BIG and QUAINT). We quantify the impact of future GAPS data, showing that its sensitivity to sub-GV antiprotons could improve the $\langleσv\rangle$ constraints by up to an order of magnitude for light DM ($m_χ \lesssim 50$ GeV). For heavier antinuclei, the detection perspective with existing and upcoming experiments are derived for those scenarios consistent with AMS-02 antiproton flux. The detectability of such signals strongly depends on the experiment, the propagation model, and the hadronization tuning. Our analysis underscores the complementarity of antinuclei channels for indirect DM searches and the critical role of low-energy windows in constraining light DM candidates.

♻ ☆ Probing Extragalactic Ultralight Axion Dark Matter with Decade-Long Blazar Optical Polarimetry of 1ES 1959+650

Axions or axion-like particles (ALPs) are well-motivated dark matter (DM) candidates whose coupling to photons induces periodic oscillations in the polarization angle of astrophysical light. This work reports the first search for such a signature using 10 years of optical polarimetric monitoring of the blazar 1ES~1959+650. No statistically significant periodicity is detected, determined by a Lomb-Scargle periodogram combined with Monte Carlo analysis. Assuming a central DM density in the host galaxy, this null result places tight upper limits on the ALP-photon coupling constant at $g_{aγ}<(1.3\times10^{-13}-6.0\times10^{-10})\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ across a broad ALP mass range of $m_a \sim (1.4\times10^{-23}-5.2\times10^{-20})\,\mathrm{eV}$. Assuming a soliton-core DM density, we obtain upper limits of $ g_{aγ}< (2.5\times10^{-13}-6.2\times10^{-13})\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1} $ over the same ALP mass range. Our constraints surpass those from Very Long Baseline Array polarimetry of active galactic jets and from polarimetric data of the European Pulsar Timing Array, and are competitive with those from long-term Galactic pulsar timing of PSR J0437-4715 over the same ALP mass window. These results establish long-term blazar polarimetry as a competitive and complementary approach for probing axion-like DM on extragalactic scales.

♻ ☆ Theoretical Aspects of Direct Waves in Kerr Black Holes: Pole-Splitting Method for Ringdown Analysis
Nao Nakamoto, Naritaka Oshita, Hiroki Takeda
We develop a theoretical description of direct waves (DWs) from a particle plunging into a Kerr black hole in the extreme-mass-ratio regime. A DW is characterized by a source-driven complex frequency $ω_{\rm G}$ that reflects the particle's orbital motion, including motion inside the ergoregion. Hence, it is expected to be a probe of rich structures of Kerr black holes. We show that the contribution of the quasinormal-mode (QNM) pole sector to the DW is part of dynamical QNM excitation. We also show that the apparent horizon-mode poles cancel at every order of a consistent near-horizon expansion of the trajectory, homogeneous radial solution, and complete point-particle source. This result assumes that the point particle follows a geodesic near the horizon and leaves open the possibility of a transient DW while the particle passes near the ergosurface or the vicinity of the potential barrier. To investigate this possibility in simulated plunge waveforms, we develop a pole-splitting method that decomposes the transfer function into QNM-pole and non-pole parts. The resulting waveform decomposition avoids the frequency-dependent time shift (group delay) introduced by the QNM filtering. For quasi-circular plunges into moderately and rapidly rotating Kerr black holes, the frequency and decay rate of the non-pole waveform show qualitative agreement with our theoretical prediction over finite time intervals. These results support the potential use of DWs as probes of the ergoregion and gravitational redshift effect around black holes.

♻ ☆ Gravitational form factors of the pion in light-front holographic QCD
Jiali Deng, Xiaolong Wang, Yang Zhou, Defu Hou
Understanding the internal structure of the pion-particularly the energy-momentum distributions of quarks and gluons and the internal mechanical properties encoded in its gravitational form factors-is a fundamental challenge in quantum chromodynamics (QCD). In this work, we study the gravitational form factors using light-front QCD (LFQCD), combined with the holographic QCD. Our main innovation is the introduction of an effective light-front wave function, with its five-dimensional component obtained from holographic QCD, which is then employed, within the light-front QCD framework, to calculate the pion's gravitational form factors $A(Q^2)$ and $D(Q^2)$ as well as its radius. Our computed pion gravitational form factors show agreement with lattice QCD results, providing nontrivial support for the viability of our phenomenological model.

Supernova cooling provides a powerful probe of physics beyond the Standard Model (SM), in particular for new, light states interacting feebly with SM particles. In this \textit{Letter}, we investigate for the first time the production of fermionic dark matter (DM) via the neutrino-devouring process inside a core-collapse supernova, which contributes to the excessive cooling of the supernova. By incorporating state-of-the-art supernova simulation data and the full time evolution information, we derive stringent and robust limits on DM interactions, which can improve upon direct detection limits by several orders of magnitude. We exclude the cross sections down to $10^{-51}-10^{-58}$~cm$^2$ in the keV-MeV mass range for DM-electron scattering, and $10^{-49}-10^{-56}$~cm$^2$ in the 0.1-100~MeV mass range for DM-nucleon scattering, supplemented by complementary constraints from cosmology, astrophysics, colliders and direct detection experiments in the larger cross section regime. We also close almost the entire window in which fermionic DM constitutes $\mathcal{O}(1)$ fraction of DM due to its coupling to electrons in the keV-MeV mass range.

We study the processes $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η$ and $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-$ at center-of-mass energies $\sqrt{s}$=(10.73 -- 11.02) GeV using a $142.5\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ data sample, including 122~fb$^{-1}$ near the $Υ$(10860) peak ($\sqrt{s}$ = 10.866 GeV), collected with the Belle detector at the KEKB asymmetric-energy $e^+e^-$ collider. From the peak sample, the products of Born cross section times branching fraction are obtained for $σ_{\rm Born}(e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η)$ or $σ_{\rm Born}(e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-)$ and ${\cal B}(Υ_J(1D)\toχ_{b1}γ)$ or ${\cal B}(Υ_J(1D)\toχ_{b2}γ)$ for each $Υ_J(1D)$ state. The corresponding branching fractions for $Υ(10860)$ decays are also obtained. The significances of the $Υ_1(1D)$, $Υ_2(1D)$, and $Υ_3(1D)$ signals are 4.8$σ$, ${>}10σ$, and 3.0$σ$, respectively, including systematic uncertainties. The mass for $Υ_2(1D)$ is measured to be $(10167.0\pm 1.0\pm 0.2)$ MeV/$c^2$, where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic. The mass splittings $Δm_{12}=m(Υ_2(1D))-m(Υ_1(1D))$ and $Δm_{23}=m(Υ_3(1D))-m(Υ_2(1D))$ are $(11.8\pm1.5\pm0.4)$ MeV/$c^2$ and $(7.6\pm2.4\pm0.6)$ MeV/$c^2$, respectively.~We determine the energy dependence of the cross sections for $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)η$ and $e^+e^-\toΥ_J(1D)π^+π^-$ for the $Υ_1(1D)$, $Υ_2(1D)$, and $Υ_3(1D)$ states, combined.

♻ ☆ Models with rank-reducing discrete boundary conditions on $T^2/{\mathbb Z}_4$
Yoshiharu Kawamura, Eiji Kodaira, Kentaro Kojima, Toshifumi Yamashita
We study six-dimensional $SU(n)$ gauge models with rank-reducing discrete boundary conditions on the orbifold $T^2/{\mathbb Z}_4$, without and with continuous Wilson line phases. For the latter case, we find that a minimal model can describe the breakdown of the electroweak symmetry based on an $SU(6)$ gauge group. This model possesses excellent features that two Higgs doublets come from the zero modes of the extra-dimensional gauge field, and the quarks in each generation can be unified into one multiplet, without exotic quarks, as the zero modes of a bulk field in the $\boldsymbol{15}$ representation of $SU(6)$. There exists a vacuum where the electroweak symmetry is slightly broken by the Hosotani mechanism, with the addition of suitable bulk fields.

♻ ☆ On Compositeness of $D_{s0}^*(2317)$ and its decay to $D_sπ^0$
Yu-Hui Zhou, Xiu-Li Gao, Bin Wu, Jun-Xi Cui, Zhi-Yong Zhou
We demonstrate that the $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ can be described as a bound-state pole arising from the coupling between a discrete $c\bar{s}(1^3P_0)$ state and the $DK$ continuum state in the Lee-Friedrichs model. The elementariness and compositeness of the $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ are determined to be about $Z:X\approx 51.1 \%:48.9\%$, indicating a nearly equal admixture of compact quark-model state and hadronic molecular components. The decay width of $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)\rightarrow D_s^{+}π^0$ is evaluated within the quark rearrangement framework. The transition $c\bar{s}(1^3P_0)\rightarrow D_sπ^0$ proceeds via the OZI-allowed $c\bar{s}(1^3P_0)-D_sη$ coupling followed by $η-π^0$ mixing, which serves as the primary source of isospin violation in this channel. The coupling between $DK$ and $D_sπ^0$ is computed in a quark rearrangement model, where the isospin violation effect originates from the mass difference between the $D^0K^+$ and $D^+K^0$ thresholds. The parameters of the scheme shares the same ones with those of the underlying potential model and only the vacuum production strength is adjusted to reproduce the physical $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ mass. This calculation may shed more insight to the nature of exotic $D_{s0}^{*}(2317)$ state and its isospin-breaking decay properties.

In a nonrelativistic potential quark model framework, we carry out a precise calculation of the mass spectrum of the all-heavy tetraquarks with different flavors, $bb\bar{b}\bar{c}$, $cc\bar{c}\bar{b}$, $bb\bar{c}\bar{c}$, and $bc\bar{b}\bar{c}$, by adopting the explicitly correlated Gaussian method. A complete mass spectrum for the $1S$ states is obtained. For the $bb\bar{b}\bar{c}$, $cc\bar{c}\bar{b}$, $bb\bar{c}\bar{c}$, and $bc\bar{b}\bar{c}$ systems, the $1S$ states are predicted to lie in the mass ranges of $ \sim(16.06,16.14)$, $\sim(9.65,9.74)$, $\sim(12.89,12.94)$, and $\sim(12.75,12.99)$~GeV, respectively. Moreover, by using the obtained masses and wave functions, we evaluate the fall-apart decay properties within a quark-exchange model. The results show that the $1S$ states of the all-heavy tetraquarks with different flavors may have narrow fall-apart decay widths, which range from a few tenths to several MeV. Some all-heavy tetraquarks with different flavors could be search for at LHC in their optimal fall-apart decay channels, such as $ΥJ/ψ$, $ΥB_c^-$, and $J/ψB_c^+$.

♻ ☆ Analytic Gravitational Wave Spectrum in Next-to-Minimal Bouncing Cosmology
Changhong Li
Bouncing cosmology offers a singularity-free alternative to inflation. However, its minimal realization, known as minimal bouncing cosmology (MBC), comprises only four cosmic phases and produces a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) with a single power-law spectrum. Interpreting the pulsar timing array (PTA) signal within this framework faces tension with the $ΔN_{\rm eff}$ bound and has required trans-Planckian bounce energies, restricting its observational viability. In this work, we propose next-to-minimal bouncing cosmology (NMBC) by adding an earlier phase of cosmic evolution to MBC. Using our previously developed primordial gravitational-wave propagation-matrix method, with an improved matching prescription, we derive explicit analytic expressions for the resulting SGWB spectrum. The spectrum takes a broken power-law form: the low- and high-frequency tilts are determined by the equations of state of the additional and original contraction phases, respectively, while the spectral amplitudes depend jointly on these equations of state and the characteristic transition-time scales. This additional freedom allows a PTA-band signal to coexist with a scale-invariant or red-tilted high-frequency branch, providing a way to satisfy the $ΔN_{\rm eff}$ bound. For the scale-invariant high-frequency branch, a pointwise benchmark using the adopted $ΔN_{\rm eff}$ radiation budget gives $ρ_{s\downarrow}^{1/4}\lesssim2.65\,m_{\rm pl}$, where $m_{\rm pl}$ is the reduced Planck mass. This provides a conservative comparison estimate for the setup considered here, since integrating the spectrum over the adopted illustrative frequency interval gives a tighter bound. The resulting upper limit is therefore of order the reduced Planck scale. please refer to the PDF for the full abstract.
