☆ Growth Phase Map of α and \b{eta} Tantalum as a Function of Growth Temperature and Oxygen Partial Pressure
Marius O. Eji, Tyler J. Kirkpatrick, Ty J. Cawein, Joseph P. Corbett
Tantalum thin films are used in low-loss superconducting quantum circuits, yet the growth conditions governing selection of $α$-Ta(110), $α$-Ta(111), and metastable $β$-Ta on c-plane sapphire remain uncertain. We deposited 100 nm Ta films by dc magnetron sputtering on Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) at 300-900 $^\circ$C while varying the O$_2$ partial pressure from a $5.5\times10^{-11}$ Torr ultrahigh-vacuum baseline to $2.23\times10^{-4}$ Torr. Absorption-corrected X-ray diffraction texture coefficients were used to construct a ternary phase-orientation growth map in terms of temperature and the oxygen-to-Ta impingement flux ratio ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}\leq4.8\times10^{-6}$ to 19). Without added oxygen, $α$-Ta(110) dominated at every temperature. At an O$_2$ pressure of only $2.5\times10^{-9}$ Torr ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}=2.2\times10^{-4}$), $α$-Ta(111) accounted for 98-99% of the normalized texture weight from 300 to 700 $^\circ$C, decreasing to 65% at 900 $^\circ$C. Substantial $β$-Ta formed only at the highest oxygen dose, dominating at 300 $^\circ$C and disappearing at 900 $^\circ$C. The apparent $β$(001)/$α$(110) selection energy of $1.07\pm0.16$ eV is comparable to the activation energy for oxygen diffusion in Ta, consistent with oxygen transport influencing phase selection. Oxygen also produced orientation-dependent changes in crystallite size and microstrain. These findings establish oxygen-controlled processing windows for phase- and orientation-selective growth of Ta films for superconducting devices.
☆ Theoretical description of high-harmonic spectroscopy for uniaxial nematic and isotropic liquid crystals
Simon Vendelbo Bylling Jensen, Marta L. Murillo-Sánchez, Andrea Annunziata, Angel Rubio, Laura Cattaneo, Nicolas Tancogne-Dejean
Enabled by their controllable optical anisotropy, liquid crystals form a cornerstone of linear optical and display technologies. Bringing the versatile platform into the nonlinear regime, we explore its nonlinear optical anisotropy by high-order harmonic generation spectroscopy. Through a comprehensive study targeting gas, liquid, nematic, and crystalline phases, we present a semi-empirical tight-binding approach that provides insight into the intermolecular character of ultrafast light-driven electron dynamics across soft-matter mesophases. We demonstrate how intermolecular electron hybridization enables spectroscopic access to structural properties, such as the nematic director and order parameter. Outlining such foundational mechanisms opens avenues towards nonlinear liquid crystal devices and ultrafast soft-matter spectroscopies.
☆ Phonon-assisted shift-current from first-principles: application to AlN monolayer
Yuncheng Mao, Pierre Lechifflart, Elena Cannuccia, Claudio Attaccalite
In this work, we present a first-principles approach to investigate phonon-assisted shift current in extended systems. Our method combines the special displacement technique with real-time simulations based on the dynamical Berry phase. Merging these two frameworks enables direct access to non-linear optical responses at finite temperatures, while naturally incorporating phonon scattering and phonon-assisted electronic transitions into the time-dependent dynamics. This allows us to capture temperature-dependent features and lattice fluctuations that are essential for a realistic description of non-linear photocurrent generation. As a representative example, we apply our approach to the shift-current response of a monolayer of hexagonal AlN (h-AlN). This system provides an ideal testing ground because it features an indirect band gap and lacks inversion symmetry. Moreover, h-AlN layers of different thicknesses have been fabricated and characterized in a variety of experimental settings, opening the concrete possibility of testing our predictions. Our results demonstrate the relevance of phonon-mediated processes and the importance of temperature in determining the magnitude and spectral features of the shift current in layered materials.
☆ Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
Yue Wu, Yuan Tian, Deng Pan, Mingwei Chen
Adapting a pre-trained machine-learning interatomic potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity requires improving defect accuracy without degrading the near-equilibrium elastic and vibrational response. Here we achieve this balance for the aluminium MACE potential QP17 by integrating conditional readout uncertainty, iterative full-parameter updates and protocol-compatible relative-energy anchoring. Sensitivities over 144 linear readout weights guide acquisition, with within-batch covariance updates and evolving neural representations. After four active-learning rounds (32 acquired configurations and 400 gradient updates), force-uncertainty acquisition reduces mean development force error from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Angstrom, outperforming random sampling (22.70), geometry-diversity selection (22.46) and uniform training across all 104 candidate labels (22.71) under the same update budget. All three force-uncertainty runs satisfy bulk-mechanical retention criteria: historical relative-energy error decreases from 0.375 to 0.207 meV/atom, while harmonic phonon root-mean-square drift remains below 0.05 THz. Matched objective ablations reveal that relative-energy anchoring suppresses harmonic drift. Out-of-sample evaluations across planar faults, twin boundaries and grain boundaries demonstrate transferable gains in defect energies and deviatoric stresses, even though virial stresses are never fitted. A closed-loop molecular dynamics and density functional theory (MD-DFT) pilot confirms that automated acceptance gating intercepts updates that violate historical elastic-group energy or vibrational tolerances. Together, these components establish a retention-constrained fine-tuning protocol for improving plastic-deformation observables while preserving the tested bulk mechanical response.
☆ High-efficiency solid-state electrochemical thermal switching through phonon engineering of 2D materials

Among the candidates, Li$_a$ZrS$_2$ combines exceptional thermal conductivity switching with low heat capacity. Lithiation to Li$_{0.125}$ZrS$_2$ reduces the cross-plane thermal conductivity from approximately 3.7 to 0.05 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. We attribute the switching behaviour to substantial softening of the Zr--Zr framework, with the mean force constant decreasing from approximately 4.2 to 1.2 eV $\mathrm{\mathring{A}}^{-2}$, alongside enhanced scattering of heat-carrying acoustic phonons. ☆ Multi-objective Bayesian optimization reveals HiPIMS deposition rates exceeding direct current sputtering
Nathan Rodkey, Felix Thelen, Alfred Ludwig, Sebastian Siol
Pulsed sputter processes are essential for a wide range of applications from hard coatings to microelectronics. High power impulse magnetron sputtering (HiPIMS) offers unique possibilities for process design due to its high ionized flux fraction. Because of the high peak-current densities involved, correspondingly high plasma densities generate many ions. This enables tuning of kinetic energies by applying accelerating bias potentials. However, some HiPIMS processes have low deposition rates due to the back-attraction these ions experience with the negatively charged sputter target. Recent work in HiPIMS has targeted this problem, exploring complex pulsing schemes such as bipolar, multi-pulse, or chopped HiPIMS. These pulsing schemes introduce another problem: process complexity. As such, the process space, even with coarse intervals quickly blows up to 1E5-1E20 possible process combinations. This calls for efficient and intelligent sampling, which can be enabled by machine-learning algorithms such as Bayesian optimization. In this work we use multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) to efficiently sample the process space of pulse-packets, targeting high ionization flux fractions and deposition rates. Over 2,000 distinct processes were sampled during this exploration. Surprisingly, we found that many HiPIMS processes, including single pulse, can achieve deposition rates higher than DC references. In fact, at a working pressure of 1.0 Pa and moderate ionization rates of 5-20% we found that ms-scale pulses were ideal. We hypothesize these processes maximize gas rarefaction, creating a low-collision channel between the target and the substrate. These results showcase previously unreported behavior of pulsed sputter processes and challenge a long-held trade-off between film quality and speed in thin-film manufacturing.

Together, these complementary structural, chemical, electrostatic, and device-level measurements established a quantitative strain-polarization-built-in field-charge separation relationship. This work transforms ferroelectric photoanode engineering from empirical optimization into an atomically controllable and predictive materials strategy for high-efficiency solar water-splitting devices. This approach is readily extendable to visible-light absorbers and complex ferroelectric heterostructures.

☆ Precursor Ratio-Controlled Chloride Vacancies in Lead-Free KCuCl3-x Memristors for Forming-Free Gradual Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Learning

An optimal VCl concentration (~ 1.3*10^21 cm^-3) provides a balance between ionic mobility and defect controllability, resulting in highly linear potentiation/depression characteristics and superior pulse endurance (>104 cycles). When the experimentally measured conductance characteristics of the optimized memristor are implemented as synaptic weights in artificial neural network simulations, recognition accuracies of 98.96% and 91.82% are achieved on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, respectively. These findings establish precursor ratio-controlled VCl engineering as an effective strategy for simultaneously optimizing ionic transport, analog switching, and neuromorphic learning in lead-free halide perovskite memristors, providing a general materials design principle for energy-efficient neuromorphic electronics.
☆ Zeeman-field-induced three-spin interactions and relativistic coupling to the scalar spin chirality

Magnetic fields are commonly incorporated in atomistic spin models through the Zeeman energy of individual magnetic moments. Starting from a microscopic electronic Hamiltonian, we show that the Zeeman coupling of conduction electrons also generates field-linear three-spin interactions, the lowest-order corrections allowed by time-reversal symmetry. The elementary quaternions ia,ib,ic are geometrically represented by pair of perpendicular and oriented planes intersecting along the axis a,b,c, respectively. Three other complementary quaternions were also introduced. They are the pairs of planes ma, mb, mc. The elementary quaternions follow Hamilton rules on the squares of imaginary numbers. The complementary quaternions follow Hamilton rules on the bi and tri-products. For Cartesian basis, the quaternions i,j,k appear as a specific case of crystallographic quaternions. They are formed by the pairs of perpendicular faces of the cube mx, my, mz.

The absence of imaginary phonon frequencies and the existence of a thermodynamically stable region indicate dynamical and thermodynamic stability. Chemical-potential analysis identifies the chlorine vacancy as the most stable neutral defect under chlorine-poor conditions and the thallium vacancy under chlorine-rich conditions. Unlike conventional collinear AM wherein zero magnetism is protected by, e.g. rotation or mirror reflection, which globally flip the spin in the magnetic pattern, the zero magnetism in these 2D-IRRP states is instead protected by a special group-theory-orthogonality theorem that basis functions belonging to different IRRPs are always mutually orthogonal. The special group-theory-orthogonality compensation mechanism and the absence of the PT symmetry finally leads to AM states, which are to be verified by the spin split in the spin-dependent angle-resolved-photoemission-spectrum and the spin conductance. These intriguing collinear and coplanar AM can also emerge in other QCs.

Using this approach, emergent spatial textures can be imaged and converted into an experimentally-accessible observable: the computable information density (CID), a compression-based measure of information complexity that approaches the Shannon entropy rate in the large-system limit. The same framework tracks fractional quantum Hall transitions and resolves isolated fractional puddles that coexist with a disordered background. We further show that the geometric information encoded in CID is not reducible to a correlation length, and it can even distinguish spatial textures with identical multifractal statistics. Together, these results establish lossless compression as a framework for quantifying emergent spatial organization in quantum materials, with portability across imaging modalities and physical systems.

Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.

All arithmetic is exact and AlgebrasTQD can be used with any finite group $G$ and 3-cocycle $ω$, limited only by the time and size of the calculation. The code is available at https://github.com/AlisonWarman/AlgebrasTQD

♻ ☆ Evaluating the Structural Basis for Polar Altermagnet Candidate Ca$_{3}$(Ru,Ti)$_{2}$O$_{7}$
Akash Saha, Yihuang Xiong, Vladimir A. Stoica, Subin Mali, Aaron Pearre, Saugata Sarker, Huaiyu Wang, Yufei Zhao, Evguenia Karapetrova, Yu Wang, Jadupati Nag, Zachary W. Hazenstab, Seng Huat Lee, Long-Qing Chen, Geoffroy Hautier, Binghai Yan, Zhiqiang Mao, Venkatraman Gopalan
The interplay between polar and altermagnetic orders remains largely unexplored in the broader landscape of correlated electron systems. Density functional theory (DFT) within the PBEsol + $U$ treatment propose Ca$_{3}$Ru$_{2}$O$_{7}$ as a polar altermagnet, reliant on the transformation of the experimentally reported $Bb2_{1}m$ phase to a lower symmetry $Pn2_{1}a$ structure. Here, we perform a targeted search for the $Pn2_{1}a$ phase using synchrotron X-ray diffraction on single crystals of Ca$_{3}$Ru$_{2}$O$_{7}$ and Ca$_{3}$(Ru$_{0.99}$Ti$_{0.01}$)$_{2}$O$_{7}$. No diffraction signature of the $Pn2_{1}a$ structure is detected down to 20 K within experimental limits. Through diffraction simulations, we translate this result into a quantitative upper bound on the symmetry breaking distortion amplitude, which we find to be significantly smaller than the DFT predicted distortion. Our DFT calculations further motivate dilute Ti substitution ($\lesssim 2\%$) as an alternative route to stabilize the low symmetry phase, for which we again find no clear evidence for this putative $Pn2_{1}a$ structure that hosts altermagnetism. Our findings indicate that PBEsol + $U$ over-stabilizes a $Pn2_{1}a$ distortion, and the measured bounds provide benchmark for future calculations. Ti substitution exceeding $\sim$3% reveals a chemically tunable polar altermagnetic phase within the $Bb2_{1}m$ structure and we theoretically demonstrate that the spin-splitting can be tuned by Ti substitution. By combining DFT, diffraction simulations and synchrotron X-ray measurements, our study demonstrates a general methodology to quantify subtle structural distortions that underlie emergent electronic and magnetic phases.

♻ ☆ Quantum Counting in the Rydberg Blockade
Joseph Gibson, Victor Drouin-Touchette, Stefanos Kourtis
We propose a quantum algorithm for approximately counting the number of solutions to planar 2-satisfiability (2SAT) formulas natively on neutral-atom quantum computers (NAQC). Our algorithm maps Boolean variables to atomic registers arranged in space according to a given formula, so that 2SAT constraints are enforced via the Rydberg blockade between neighboring atoms. A quench of an initial computational basis state then produces a superposition of all solutions after sufficiently long evolution. For almost uniform superpositions, a polynomial number of measurements is enough to estimate the solution count up to any constant multiplicative factor via sampling-based counting. Numerical simulations show that the protocol leads to almost uniform solution sampling in 1D and 2D grids and produces accurate counts for small random 2SAT instances on punctured grids. We implement our algorithm on Pasqal's Orion Alpha NAQC and demonstrate approximate counts within small multiplicative factors of the exact count for a planar grid instance with 81 atoms.

♻ ☆ Transport and Phase competition in three-dimensional Hubbard-Holstein model at half-filling
Sandip Halder, Moshe Schechter
We investigate the magnetotransport properties of the one-band Hubbard-Holstein model at half-filling in three dimensions (3D) using exact diagonalization based semi-classical Monte Carlo simulations with phonons treated in the adiabatic limit. The low-temperature electronic correlation $U$ vs electron-phonon coupling $V$ phase diagram reveals two insulating phases--antiferromagnetic (AF-I) and charge-ordered (CO-I)--separated by a first-order transition, with no metallic phase observed at their intersection, indicating robustness of these phases in 3D. For $U \sim bandwidth$, the $V$ vs temperature $T$ phase diagram exhibits multiple phases including AF-I, CO-I, Mott-Hubbard insulator, bipolaronic insulator, and two bipolaronic metallic states. Several first-order transitions occur near $V \sim 3.75$. Above the ordering temperature, the density of states shows universal behavior dominated by electronic contribution, while susceptibility and DOS analyses reveal pseudogap features. Magnetic and transport properties along the phase boundary highlight strong proximity effects between competing phases, suggesting routes for tuning correlated materials and emergent electronic states.

♻ ☆ Designing Strongly Correlated Quantum Phases of Matter with Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States
Alessandro Sinibaldi, Luciano Loris Viteritti, Riccardo Rende, Federico Becca, Giuseppe Carleo
Materials design is an inverse problem: finding the couplings of a microscopic Hamiltonian whose ground state exhibits a desired property. For strongly correlated quantum systems, this remains largely out of reach, as each candidate Hamiltonian requires its own costly simulation. Here we show that Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States, single wave functions that encode the ground states of an entire family of Hamiltonians, make this search efficient. Because the Hamiltonian couplings enter as neural-network inputs, any ground-state property can be optimized by gradient descent directly in coupling space. We use this approach to search for nonmagnetic phases in two-dimensional spin models in coupling spaces of increasing dimensionality. Specifically, we focus on quantum spin liquids, exotic phases of matter in which quantum fluctuations prevent magnetic order at zero temperature. In the largest search space considered, spanned by eight superexchange couplings and containing many paradigmatic frustrated spin systems, the optimization converges to the $J_1$-$J_2$-$δ$ Heisenberg model when starting from a magnetic phase. We show that the ground state at the optimum set of couplings has neither magnetic nor valence-bond order in the thermodynamic limit, leading to a new quantum spin-liquid candidate. The approach is completely general and can be extended to other models and physical properties to optimize, demonstrating that Neural-Network Quantum States are tools not only for simulating quantum matter but also for designing it.

♻ ☆ Web of Non-invertible Dualities for (2+1) Dimensional Models with Subsystem Symmetries
Avijit Maity, Vikram Tripathi, Andriy H. Nevidomskyy
We extend non-invertible duality concepts from one-dimensional systems to two spatial dimensions by constructing a web of non-invertible dualities for lattice models with subsystem symmetries. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ subsystem symmetry on the square lattice, we build two complementary dualities: a map that sends spontaneous subsystem symmetry-broken (SSSB) phases to the trivial phase (the analogue of the Kramers-Wannier (KW) duality in 1+1D), and a generalized subsystem Kennedy-Tasaki (KT) transformation that maps SSSB phases to subsystem symmetry-protected topological (SSPT) phases while leaving the trivial phase invariant. These dualities are boundary-sensitive. On open lattices, both subsystem KW and KT transformations act as unitary, invertible operators. In particular, the KT map not only matches the bulk Hamiltonians of the dual phases but also carries the spontaneous ground-state degeneracy of the SSSB phase onto the protected boundary degeneracy of the SSPT phase. On closed manifolds, however, both maps become intrinsically non-unitary and non-invertible when restricted to the original Hilbert space. We demonstrate this non-invertibility via ground-state degeneracy matching (in two copies of the Xu-Moore/Ising-plaquette model), analysis of symmetry-twist sectors mapping, and the fusion algebra of the duality operator. Enlarging the Hilbert space to include twisted sectors allows the subsystem KW map to be formulated as a projective unitary preserving quantum transition probabilities, consistent with generalized Wigner-theorem-based constructions. We also show that the KT map faithfully transmits the algebraic content of bulk and edge invariants diagnosing strong SSPT order: although strictly local SSPT repair operators map to highly nonlocal objects in the dual SSSB phase, the essential commutation algebra and the bulk-edge correspondence remain intact.

♻ ☆ Cavity control of quantum phase transitions in a two-dimensional Kondo lattice
Jun Mochida, Atac Imamoglu, Yuto Ashida
Cavity quantum electrodynamics offers a route to control quantum phases by using vacuum fluctuations of confined electromagnetic fields. In particular, planar cavities based on polar van der Waals materials can generate strongly confined modes and are promising for controlling two-dimensional correlated materials. Recently, moiré materials have become central platforms for studying two-dimensional heavy-fermion systems and their quantum phase transitions. Kondo lattices provide a prototypical model for studying quantum phase boundaries, driven by competition between Kondo screening and the ordering of local magnetic moments. We show that a cavity-induced interaction can shift the quantum phase transitions between a heavy-fermion phase and an antiferromagnetic phase in a two-dimensional Kondo lattice through a momentum-dependent self-energy of the conduction bands. For the longitudinal projected field motivated by h-BN hyperbolic phonon polaritons, the self-energy favors Kondo hybridization and expands the heavy-fermion region. Transverse and circular in-plane model structures give distinct effects, with the transverse case relatively favoring the magnetically ordered phase and the circular case lying between the longitudinal and transverse cases. These results indicate that electromagnetic vacuum fluctuations can effectively modify the control parameters of strongly correlated two-dimensional Kondo materials.

♻ ☆ String Order in Quench Dynamics as a Probe of Quantum Phase Transitions
H. P. Zhang, Z. Song
We study the anisotropic XY chain in a transverse field by introducing a global string order parameter and examining its equilibrium behavior and its quench dynamics from a fully polarized initial state. The corresponding string operator is defined as the product of local projected spin operators over the entire chain. The nonequilibrium order parameter is the long-time average of the logarithm of the string-operator expectation value per site after the quench. For the ground state, its field derivative is singular on the Ising critical lines; after the quench, the steady-state response also records the field boundaries and the anisotropy transition. We derive analytically the nonanalytic behavior of the order parameter at the quantum critical lines. Our results reveal a hidden nonlocal order underlying this paradigmatic model of conventional quantum phase transitions. They also connect measurable spin populations with equilibrium and dynamical topological structure.

♻ ☆ Time-reversal symmetry breaking and inherent Josephson diodes in a multi-component order parameter superconductor
Remko Fermin, Matthijs Rog, Guido Stam, Daan Wielens, Joost Ridderbos, Chuan Li, Yoshi Maeno, Jan Aarts, Kaveh Lahabi
Spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking is a defining feature of unconventional superconductivity and a prerequisite of the technologically relevant superconducting diode effect. However, its realization remains rare and exclusive to proximity-engineered weak links. Here we examine an alternative pathway to spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking by examining junctions that appear in single-crystal microstructures of the unconventional superconductor Sr$_2$RuO$_4$, lacking external superconducting proximity. We interpret the Josephson coupling as superconducting domains of a multi-component order parameter based on a plethora of anomalous effects - including a field-free Josephson diode effect, fractional Shapiro steps, magnetic interference patterns deviating from the conventional flux quantum periodicity, and bias current-programmable bistable states. These microscopic devices corroborate earlier bulk probes of time-reversal symmetry breaking, giving a renewed impulse to the long-debated pairing symmetry of Sr$_2$RuO$_4$. Our results highlight superconducting domain walls as a platform for functional Josephson devices and the study of fundamental symmetry breaking.
♻ ☆ Interlayer Phase Locking and Sliding Select Topological Melting Channels in Superconducting Bilayers
Yicheng Zhong, Yi Zhou
Topological transitions in coupled superconducting layers are intertwined: an elementary vortex in one layer carries both common and relative phase winding. We study a Josephson-coupled bilayer in an in-plane magnetic field using renormalization-group analysis and Monte Carlo simulations of the compact layer phases. The field drives Pokrovsky--Talapov (PT) entry of interlayer solitons, and free-energy calculations in fixed soliton sectors show PT square-root scaling over the sampled densities at finite temperature. Interlayer phase locking and sliding then select distinct Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT)-like melting channels. The locked commensurate phase melts through same-vorticity layer pairs when the geometric-mean common helicity modulus $Υ_{+,g}$ reaches $T/(2π)$, with layer correlation exponent $η_l=1/4$. A stable sliding incommensurate phase melts through elementary layer vortices on a line of BKT fixed points, where $Υ_{+,g}+Υ_{-,g}=2T/π$ and $η_l$ is set by the ratio of the relative and common moduli. When the relative helicity modulus is identified with the relative-phase stiffness, our simulations agree with this prediction, and the common superfluid stiffness at incommensurate melting is nearly twice its value at commensurate melting. Near soliton entry, however, the dilute sliding state is unstable to opposite-vorticity layer pairs. Our results connect PT soliton entry with field-tunable BKT-like melting and identify the pair-stability condition that links them.
♻ ☆ Robust spin splitting and fermiology in the layered altermagnet CoNb4Se8
Alessandro De Vita, Chiara Bigi, Davide Romanin, Matthew D. Watson, Vincent Polewczyk, Marta Zonno, François Bertran, My Bang Petersen, Federico Motti, Giovanni Vinai, Manuel Tuniz, Federico Cilento, Mario Cuoco, Brian M. Andersen, Andreas Kreisel, Luciano Jacopo D'Onofrio, Oliver J. Clark, Mark T. Edmonds, Christopher Candelora, Muxian Xu, Siyu Cheng, Alexander LaFleur, Tommaso Antonelli, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Lorenzo Del Re, Ivana Vobornik, Jun Fujii, Fabio Miletto Granozio, Alessia Sambri, Emiliano Di Gennaro, Jeppe B. Jacobsen, Henrik Jacobsen, Iulia Cojocariu, Marcin Szpytma, Andrea Locatelli, Tevfik Mentes, Won Seop Song, Jun Sung Kim, Matthieu Jamet, Jean-François Jacquot, Pasquale Orgiani, Ralph Ernstorfer, Ilija Zeljkovic, Younghun Hwang, Matteo Calandra, Jill A. Miwa, Federico Mazzola
Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three-dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb, layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically. Here, combining termination-resolved micro-ARPES, fine photon-energy mapping, spin-ARPES and density functional theory, we map the three-dimensional fermiology of the layered g-wave altermagnet CoNb$_4$Se$_8$, obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H-NbSe$_2$. We resolve the spin-split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin-ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time-reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry-protected nodal $Γ$--K direction. We further report a weak low-temperature anomaly near $T_0\approx50$ to 60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature-dependent micro-ARPES and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum-resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.
♻ ☆ Open Wilson chain numerical renormalization group approach to steady-state non-equilibrium quantum transport
Anand Manaparambil, Frithjof B. Anders
The numerical renormalization group (NRG) approach was developed to identify and quantify different equilibrium regimes of quantum impurity systems (QISs) with unprecedented accuracy by a tailored finite size representation. Out of equilibrium, the steady-state density operator is not of the Boltzmannian form but one that is determined by the imposed boundary conditions. We extend the NRG to the nonequilibrium setting by augmenting each Wilson site with a reservoir, whose coupling functions are calculated via a continuous fraction expansion in order to recover the continuum limit exactly. The nonequilibrium parameters such as a finite bias as well as a finite temperature gradient enters through the Bloch-Redfield tensor (BRT), whose zero eigenvector gives the steady-state density operator. We used the resulting open chain full density matrix (OC-FDM) approach with an effective single lead description to investigate the charge and spin transport through a quantum dot (QD) under finite bias and temperature gradient. The influence of lead asymmetry and an external magnetic field on the transport properties are also studied. For completeness, we have also investigated local properties of the QD, such as charge fluctuations and find excellent agreement with real-time quantum Monte Carlo (RT-QMC) data. The OC-FDM approach was able to explore Kondo energy scales as low as $T_K/D \approx 10^{-8}$ in the non-equilibrium regime, as well as show convergence with the established equilibrium benchmarks, such as a quantitative agreement with full density matrix numerical renormalization group (FDM-NRG) and Fermi-liquid scaling at small bias and temperature. Owing to the effective single lead description, a single OC-FDM data point takes orders of magnitude less time on a standard laptop, compared to other state-of-the-art numerical methods.

♻ ☆ Lattice Symmetry Remnants in Spatial and Temporal Entanglement of Quantum Critical Spin Chains
Xiao-Han Yang, Rui-Zhen Huang
Quantum critical lattice models retain universal information about their lattice symmetries beyond the bulk data of their infrared conformal field theory (CFT). We probe these lattice symmetry remnants by comparing the spatial and temporal entanglement of two Euclidean-evolved states from the same critical model. At large length scales, short-range initial states define conformal boundaries and boundary CFT (BCFT) organizes the universal low-lying entanglement spectrum. In the temporal construction, the translation invariance along Euclidean time requires a uniform state. Moreover, the time slice $δτ\rightarrow 0$ forces a split-gate basis, resulting in a new regular uniform symmetry-preserving transfer representation. For the Ising and Potts chains, onsite symmetries result in the same BCFT structure in the spatial and temporal constructions. The spin-$1/2$ XXZ chain instead realizes the Lieb--Schultz--Mattis (LSM) constraint differently in the two Euclidean quantization. A $U(1)$-preserving spatial state has a doubled unit cell and inequivalent entanglement cuts, whereas the temporal state remains uniform and alternates between translation relation related Dirichlet sectors with integer and half-integer compact-boson zero modes. Breaking $U(1)$ removes the zero mode and the alternation. Thus microscopic symmetry and anomaly data remain visible in universal entanglement by constraining the boundary realization of the infrared CFT.

♻ ☆ Coexistence of Ferromagnetic and Overscreened Kondo Effects in a Single Molecule
Elia Turco, Nils Krane, Hongyan Chen, Simon Gerber, Wulf Wulfhekel, Roman Fasel, Pascal Ruffieux, David Jacob
The quest for quantum ground states beyond the Fermi-liquid paradigm remains a central challenge in many-body physics. The ferromagnetic Kondo effect is an intriguing variant of the Kondo effect in which an asymptotically free spin gives rise to singular Fermi-liquid behavior. Despite its theoretical importance, this regime has eluded experimental observation owing to subtle spectroscopic signatures, small energy scales, and symmetry constraints in nanostructures. Here, we demonstrate the coexistence of ferromagnetic and overscreened Kondo effects within a molecular spin system---a triangulene dimer comprising spin-1 and spin-1/2 units adsorbed on a metal surface. Low-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals signatures of singular Fermi-liquid behavior, supported by many-body calculations. The molecular design provides control over spin configuration and coupling asymmetry, allowing distinct regimes within the same platform. Our results establish a strategy for realizing non-Fermi-liquid physics at the atomic scale and demonstrate that ferromagnetic Kondo behavior can be deliberately engineered in molecular systems.

♻ ☆ Subspace-Protected Topological Phases and Bulk-Boundary Correspondence
Kenji Shimomura, Ryo Takami, Daichi Nakamura, Masatoshi Sato
While tremendous research has revealed that symmetry enriches topological phases of matter, more general principles that protect topological phases have yet to be explored. In this Letter, we elucidate the roles of subspaces in free-fermionic topological phases. A subspace property for Hamiltonians enables us to define new topological invariants. It results in peculiar topological boundary phenomena, i.e., the emergence of an unpaired zero mode or zero-winding skin modes, characterizing subspace-protected topological phases. We establish and demonstrate the bulk-boundary correspondence in subspace-protected topological phases. We further discuss the interplay of the subspace property and internal symmetries. Toward application, we also propose possible platforms possessing the subspace property.

♻ ☆ Topological Quantum Criticality in Quasiperiodic Cluster Ising Chain
Sheng Yang, Hai-Qing Lin, Xue-Jia Yu
Topological classifications of quantum critical systems have recently attracted growing interest, as they go beyond the traditional paradigms of condensed matter and statistical physics. However, such classifications remain largely unexplored in aperiodic environments, particularly under quasiperiodic modulations. In this Letter, we uncover a family of topological quasiperiodic fixed points with critical scalings intermediate between the clean and infinite-randomness limits. By exactly solving the quasiperiodic cluster-Ising chain, we demonstrate that all phase boundaries separating quasiperiodically modulated phases are governed by topological Ising-like fixed points unique to strongly modulated quasiperiodic systems. Although their local bulk critical properties match those of conventional quasiperiodic Ising critical points reported before, these fixed points host robust topological edge degeneracies and exhibit a distinct symmetry-enriched realization of the quasiperiodic Ising criticality, as further supported by complementary lattice simulations.
comment: Accepted version
♻ ☆ Topological Superradiant Universality Classes in Cavity-Mediated Spin Chains
Yunhao Liu, Sheng Yang, Mingyuan Chen, Xue-Jia Yu
Superradiant phase transitions are fundamental phenomena in light-matter coupled systems. Here, we uncover a novel class of superradiant criticality that is topologically distinct from previously known superradiant transitions. Using cavity-mediated cluster-Ising chains as an illustrative example, we numerically demonstrate that the critical line separating the superradiant phase from the cavity topological phase hosts robust symmetry-protected edge degeneracies, a feature absent in conventional superradiant transitions. Remarkably, although its local bulk critical properties are indistinguishable from those of the previously identified topologically trivial superradiant transition, the two criticalities cannot be smoothly connected without breaking the protecting symmetries or passing through a multicritical point. We further show that such topological superradiant criticality is generic, also occurring in cavity-mediated $\mathbb{Z}_{n}^{}$ cluster-qudit chains, as supported by complementary lattice simulations.

♻ ☆ Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
Ao Chen, Johnnie Gray, Si-Jing Du, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan
The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

♻ ☆ Quantized Collective Fluctuations in Correlated Fermion Systems
S. S. Onuchin, Ya. S. Lyakhova, L. D. Silakov, A. N. Rubtsov
Collective excitations in fermionic systems play a crucial role in determining their physical properties. An important challenge is to develop efficient theoretical approaches for describing these excitations and their coupling to fermionic degrees of freedom. In this work, we revisit the problem of quantifying the contributions of individual bosonic modes of collective fluctuations to observable properties of correlated fermion systems within the framework of the Fluctuating Local Field (FLF) method. Whereas the auxiliary field in this method was previously considered only classically, we formulate its systematic extension termed Quantum FLF (Q-FLF) that incorporates selected bosonic Matsubara modes, thus tailoring it to description of quantum collective fluctuations. As a testbed, we apply the approach to a half-filled one-dimensional Hubbard chain and compute the Green's function, the total energy, and the antiferromagnetic susceptibility. Our results demonstrate that the proposed scheme enables an efficient and selective characterization of the contributions of individual bosonic modes. In particular, low Matsubara frequencies are found to have a quantitative impact on integrated observables such as total energy and antiferromagnetic susceptibility. At the same time, an accurate description of single-particle properties requires inclusion of higher-frequency bosonic modes.

♻ ☆ Electronic correlations and dynamical screening with ab initio quantum embedding
Chia-Nan Yeh, Francesco Petocchi, Alexander Hampel, Philipp Werner, Olivier Parcollet, Antoine Georges, Miguel Morales
First-principles descriptions of correlated quantum materials require a simultaneous treatment of strong local many-body effects and nonlocal dynamical screening. We present an efficient fully self-consistent implementation of $GW$+EDMFT that combines nonlocal correlations at the $GW$ level with a non-perturbative treatment of local correlations within extended dynamical mean-field theory (EDMFT), with a well-defined double-counting correction and a self-consistently determined impurity interaction. Self-consistency in both the Green's function and the dynamically screened interaction is essential for describing screening processes across energy scales. A key ingredient that makes it computationally feasible is the compression of two-particle correlation functions using interpolative separable density fitting (ISDF). Applying the scheme to the Mott insulator SrMnO$_3$ and the correlated metal LaNiO$_3$, we show that the self-consistent effective local interaction resolves the overscreening inherent to constrained-RPA approaches. For SrMnO$_3$, this stabilizes a Mott-insulating state in quantitative agreement with experiment, while for LaNiO$_3$ local EDMFT corrections yield a quasiparticle mass enhancement consistent with ARPES. These results establish fully self-consistent $GW$+EDMFT as a reliable \emph{ab initio} framework for strongly correlated quantum materials.

☆ Lévy-stable pion emission sources in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV from the vHLLE+SMASH hybrid model
Zeinab A. Abdelrazik, Máté Csanád
Revealing the space-time evolution of the quark-gluon plasma created in heavy-ion collisions is a central challenge, as this information is encoded in the properties of particles emitted at freeze-out. We reconstruct the pion emission source in Au+Au collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 200 GeV (0-5% centrality), simulated with the vHLLE+SMASH hybrid framework, which combines a Glauber Monte Carlo initial state, (3+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics, and a hadronic afterburner describing resonance decays and hadronic rescattering. Hanbury Brown-Twiss (HBT) interferometry is used to characterize identical-pion pair sources, which can also be reconstructed directly from the last scattering points of final-state particles in simulations. The projected pair-separation distributions in the Bertsch-Pratt out, side, and long directions are analyzed using a three-dimensional Levy-stable parameterization. Over the investigated fit range, extending to approximately 100 fm, a single Levy-stable function provides a satisfactory description of the distributions. The extracted Levy index, alpha approximately 1.5-1.6, is below the Gaussian value of 2 and increases slowly with transverse mass mT. At larger pair separations, the total source deviates from the fitted distribution, consistent with a halo contribution from long-lived resonance decays. Short-lived resonance decays and hadronic rescattering may contribute to the non-Gaussian shape through the Levy-walk phenomenon. The HBT radii Rout, Rside, and Rlong decrease with mT, qualitatively consistent with collective expansion. These results demonstrate the utility of Levy-stable femtoscopy for connecting hadronic-stage dynamics in hybrid simulations with experimentally accessible observables.
☆ Constraining Nuclear Matter from Finite Nuclei: the Ab Initio Perspective
Francesca Bonaiti, Sonia Bacca, Ingo Tews
This review surveys recent developments in ab initio calculations of finite nuclei aimed at constraining the nuclear matter equation of state. Particular emphasis is placed on observables that connect finite-nucleus structure to bulk properties of nuclear matter, including neutron-skin thicknesses, electric dipole polarizabilities, and monopole sum rules. We discuss how neutron skins and dipole polarizabilities provide information on the density dependence of the symmetry energy, while monopole observables constrain the incompressibility of nuclear matter.

☆ Nucleon polarizabilities revisited: insights from the Bernabéu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach sum rule
Xiong-Hui Cao, Ling-Yun Dai, Feng-Kun Guo
We present a complete dispersive evaluation of the Bernabéu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach (BEFT) sum rule for the nucleon dipole polarizability difference $α_{E1}-β_{M1}$. The analysis is based on hyperbolic dispersion relations, which separate the $s$- and $t$-channel contributions without double counting and are particularly suited to backward real Compton scattering. This framework makes it possible to precisely determine the polarizability difference from independent dispersive input rather than from fits to low-energy Compton scattering data. The $s$-channel part is updated with modern single-pion photoproduction multipoles and model estimates of non-$πN$ inelastic channels. For the $t$-channel, we use contemporary dispersive input for $γγ\toππ/K\bar K_{I_t=0}$ together with Roy-Steiner equation solutions for $ππ/K\bar K_{I_t=0}\to N\bar N$, and we extend the calculation to the isovector $πη/K\bar K_{I_t=1}$ channel associated with the $a_0(980)$. The resulting treatment resolves the long-standing puzzle of earlier BEFT evaluations driven by the scalar-isoscalar two-pion channel and gives a controlled estimate of the subleading isovector contribution. Combining the resulting BEFT values with the Baldin sum rule, we obtain, in units of $10^{-4}\,\mathrm{fm}^3$, \[ α_{E1}^p=11.17(52),\quad β_{M1}^p=2.84(52),\quad α_{E1}^n=12.18(59),\quad β_{M1}^n=3.03(59). \] For the proton, these values provide a benchmark with a precision comparable to state-of-the-art dispersive and chiral effective field theory extractions. For the neutron, whose polarizabilities are much less directly constrained experimentally, the result provides an independent dispersive benchmark with an uncertainty comparable to that of the proton.

☆ Probing In-Medium Neutron-to-Dark-Fermion Conversion with Multimessenger Neutron Star Observations
Davood Rafiei Karkevandi, Mahboubeh Shahrbaf, Hamid Reza Moshfegh, Reza Karimi, Gordon Baym
Neutron stars provide a natural environment for probing in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion and its impact on the dense-matter equation of state (EOS). We use multimessenger neutron star observations to map excluded and not-excluded regions of dark-sector parameter space for an EOS ensemble within a non-linear $σ$--$ω$--$ρ$ relativistic mean-field (RMF) framework and determine their overlap across the ensemble. We include a fermionic dark component with repulsive self-interactions of strength $G_χ$. We consider masses $m_χ$ near the neutron mass and heavier states accessible in neutron star cores at sufficiently large neutron chemical potentials. To reduce sensitivity to the nucleonic EOS within this framework, we scan $m_χ=939$--$1500$ MeV and $G_χ=1$--$100$ fm$^2$ across 21 nucleonic EOSs: a main baseline set of 13 EOSs and soft and stiff limiting cases. Stellar sequences are tested against the requirement that the EOS support at least $2M_\odot$ neutron stars, GW170817 tidal-deformability bounds, and NICER mass--radius constraints, considering the Illinois--Maryland and X-PSI/Amsterdam inference sets separately. For the full ensemble of 21 EOSs, both NICER analyses identify similar regions excluded by all EOSs, with approximate minimum--maximum extents of $m_χ=939$--$1300$ MeV and $G_χ=1$--$11$ fm$^2$. The soft and stiff limiting cases show how these regions shift when the nucleonic EOS predicts a maximum neutron star mass near $2M_\odot$ or large tidal deformabilities. These findings indicate that the initial-state geometry retains useful information about nuclear radial structure and provide a baseline for future studies that incorporate transport evolution and experimental final-state observables.

☆ Remembering Brown-Rho scaling
Su Houng lee
The properties of hadrons in dense matter have been a core interest of mine since I entered graduate school at Stony Brook in 1984. This interest was shaped both by the strong research activity on the subject at Stony Brook at the time and by the influence of Mannque Rho, who was a frequent visitor there. In this memoir dedicated to Mannque, I describe a selection of his works that sparked my interest in the subject and present my current perspective on what Mannque, together with Gerry Brown, sought to emphasize in the often-misinterpreted Brown--Rho scaling. In light of recent developments, I also discuss refinements of Brown--Rho scaling for mesons and baryons, associated with spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking and $U_A(1)$-breaking effects.

♻ ☆ Dark-Matter-Induced Nuclear Deexcitation at the Short Baseline Near Detector with Ab Initio Nuclear Theory
Bhaskar Dutta, Debopam Goswami, Baishan Hu, Wei-Chih Huang, Vishvas Pandey
We explore the sensitivity of the short-baseline near detector (SBND) experiment to light dark matter using MeV-scale electromagnetic activity. Inelastic scattering of dark matter with argon nuclei can excite nuclear states that subsequently deexcite via the emission of MeV-scale photons, producing localized low-energy "blip" signatures in a liquid argon time projection chamber. We perform state-of-the-art ab initio nuclear calculations, including all relevant argon excited states with energies up to 18 MeV, to provide reliable predictions for these signals. After accounting for relevant backgrounds, we find that SBND can probe previously unexplored regions of parameter space for light dark matter.

We include electron screening and modeling of ions as finite-size Gaussian distributions in the interaction potential, together with an efficient Ewald energy summation procedure. From this, the EoS relation $P(n_B,T)$ is obtained as a function of baryonic number density $n_B\in[7.48\times 10^{-10},2.09\times10^{-4}]$ $ \rm fm^{-3}$ and temperature $k_{B}T\in[1,5]$ MeV in the NS outer crust conditions. In order to improve the usability of our results we provide tabulated data values along with a neural network parametrization available in the Zenodo repository, see https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15348712. We find that even at moderate temperatures, thermal effects of ions are key in the higher density region closer to the inner crust, when described using a thermal effective parametrization based on the thermal adiabatic index $Γ_{th}$. We compare our results with other EoS in the literature performing a critical discussion.

♻ ☆ Proton Femtoscopy in Heavy-Ion Collisions: From Transport Theory to Source Imaging
Pierre Nzabahimana, Pawel Danielewicz, Giuseppe Verde
Two-particle correlations play a pivotal role in understanding the space-time characteristics of particle emission in Heavy-Ion Collisions (HIC). A relative emission source typically represents these characteristics and can be obtained from transport model simulations such as the Boltzmann-Uehling-Uhlenbeck (BUU) transport model. We investigate the angular dependence of Ca + Ca correlations to infer the angle dependence of slow emissions. Our parametrization for the tail may be employed when no deblurring for source inference is pursued.
♻ ☆ Neutrino absorption in two-flavor color-superconducting quark matter
Mark G. Alford, Liam Brodie, Michael Buballa, Hosein Gholami, Alexander Haber, Marco Hofmann
We calculate the absorption mean free paths of electron and muon neutrinos in two-flavor color-superconducting (2SC) quark matter in the density and temperature range that is relevant to binary neutron star mergers. We model the strong interaction between quarks using a Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, performing calculations self-consistently in the mean-field approximation. Since the 2SC gap is large we restrict our analysis to the contribution of unpaired quarks. We find that at low temperatures absorption by a down quark $ν+d \to u+e^-/μ^-$ is kinematically not allowed, so absorption by a strange quark $ν+s \to u+e^-/μ^-$ dominates the mean free path. As temperature or neutrino energy rises, the $d$ quark absorption channel becomes active, and the mean free path shrinks. We find that in equilibrated 2SC matter with an electron lepton fraction $Y_{L_e}=0.1$, the neutrinos form a degenerate gas with a mean free path of meters or less, independent of the temperature.

♻ ☆ Precision Sum Rule for Nucleon Isovector Polarizabilities and the Proton-Neutron Mass Difference

The precision of the electromagnetic proton-neutron mass difference $δm_\mathrm{QED}$ extracted from the Cottingham formula hinges on a subtraction function whose low-energy normalization $\bar S(0)$ is fixed by the isovector combination of the proton and neutron polarizabilities, $(α_{E1}-β_{M1})^{p-n}$. Combining empirical pion-photoproduction multipoles with coupled-channel Muskhelishvili-Omnès representations of the scalar-isovector $πη/K\bar K$ amplitudes, we obtain $(α_{E1}-β_{M1})^{p-n}=-0.82(33)\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{fm}^3$, fixing its sign and reducing the uncertainty by one order of magnitude compared with the previously known value. This result yields $\bar S(0)=-0.56(28)\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$, leading to $δm_\mathrm{QED}=0.75^{+0.02}_{-0.04}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, substantially more precise than previous Cottingham determinations. The negative $\bar S(0)$ also provides a low-energy test of Reggeon dominance in the subtraction function.

☆ Constraining Nuclear Matter from Finite Nuclei: the Ab Initio Perspective
Francesca Bonaiti, Sonia Bacca, Ingo Tews
This review surveys recent developments in ab initio calculations of finite nuclei aimed at constraining the nuclear matter equation of state. Particular emphasis is placed on observables that connect finite-nucleus structure to bulk properties of nuclear matter, including neutron-skin thicknesses, electric dipole polarizabilities, and monopole sum rules. We discuss how neutron skins and dipole polarizabilities provide information on the density dependence of the symmetry energy, while monopole observables constrain the incompressibility of nuclear matter.

☆ Nucleon polarizabilities revisited: insights from the Bernabéu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach sum rule
Xiong-Hui Cao, Ling-Yun Dai, Feng-Kun Guo
We present a complete dispersive evaluation of the Bernabéu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach (BEFT) sum rule for the nucleon dipole polarizability difference $α_{E1}-β_{M1}$. The analysis is based on hyperbolic dispersion relations, which separate the $s$- and $t$-channel contributions without double counting and are particularly suited to backward real Compton scattering. This framework makes it possible to precisely determine the polarizability difference from independent dispersive input rather than from fits to low-energy Compton scattering data. The $s$-channel part is updated with modern single-pion photoproduction multipoles and model estimates of non-$πN$ inelastic channels. For the $t$-channel, we use contemporary dispersive input for $γγ\toππ/K\bar K_{I_t=0}$ together with Roy-Steiner equation solutions for $ππ/K\bar K_{I_t=0}\to N\bar N$, and we extend the calculation to the isovector $πη/K\bar K_{I_t=1}$ channel associated with the $a_0(980)$. The resulting treatment resolves the long-standing puzzle of earlier BEFT evaluations driven by the scalar-isoscalar two-pion channel and gives a controlled estimate of the subleading isovector contribution. Combining the resulting BEFT values with the Baldin sum rule, we obtain, in units of $10^{-4}\,\mathrm{fm}^3$, \[ α_{E1}^p=11.17(52),\quad β_{M1}^p=2.84(52),\quad α_{E1}^n=12.18(59),\quad β_{M1}^n=3.03(59). \] For the proton, these values provide a benchmark with a precision comparable to state-of-the-art dispersive and chiral effective field theory extractions. For the neutron, whose polarizabilities are much less directly constrained experimentally, the result provides an independent dispersive benchmark with an uncertainty comparable to that of the proton.

Revealing the space-time evolution of the quark-gluon plasma created in heavy-ion collisions is a central challenge, as this information is encoded in the properties of particles emitted at freeze-out. We reconstruct the pion emission source in Au+Au collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 200 GeV (0-5% centrality), simulated with the vHLLE+SMASH hybrid framework, which combines a Glauber Monte Carlo initial state, (3+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics, and a hadronic afterburner describing resonance decays and hadronic rescattering. Hanbury Brown-Twiss (HBT) interferometry is used to characterize identical-pion pair sources, which can also be reconstructed directly from the last scattering points of final-state particles in simulations. The projected pair-separation distributions in the Bertsch-Pratt out, side, and long directions are analyzed using a three-dimensional Levy-stable parameterization. Over the investigated fit range, extending to approximately 100 fm, a single Levy-stable function provides a satisfactory description of the distributions. The extracted Levy index, alpha approximately 1.5-1.6, is below the Gaussian value of 2 and increases slowly with transverse mass mT. At larger pair separations, the total source deviates from the fitted distribution, consistent with a halo contribution from long-lived resonance decays. Short-lived resonance decays and hadronic rescattering may contribute to the non-Gaussian shape through the Levy-walk phenomenon. The HBT radii Rout, Rside, and Rlong decrease with mT, qualitatively consistent with collective expansion. These results demonstrate the utility of Levy-stable femtoscopy for connecting hadronic-stage dynamics in hybrid simulations with experimentally accessible observables.
☆ Nucleon tomography from a calibrated diquark spectator model

We calculate the twist-2 vector GPDs $H^{q}$ and $E^{q}$ in a spectator model containing both scalar and axial-vector diquark configurations. To regulate the transverse-momentum integrations while retaining a physically sensible dependence on the momentum transfer, we introduce a momentum-transfer-dependent quasi-hard cutoff. The model parameters are determined through two complementary calibrations: one using proton observables only and another simultaneously including proton and neutron observables. Electromagnetic moments and radii, together with selected constraints on gravitational form factors, determine the quark and diquark masses, the relative scalar and axial-vector contributions, and the transverse-momentum scale. The two calibrations yield compatible parameter ranges, while the inclusion of neutron observables reduces the parameter uncertainties and more strongly constrains the flavor structure. From the resulting zero-skewness GPDs $H^{u,d}(x,0,t)$ and $E^{u,d}(x,0,t)$, we calculate the valence-quark PDFs and the impact-parameter distributions of unpolarized up and down quarks in both unpolarized and transversely polarized nucleons. The transverse distributions exhibit the expected localization of large-$x$ quarks near the transverse center of momentum and a flavor-dependent distortion when the nucleon is transversely polarized. Our results provide a unified phenomenological description of the longitudinal-momentum and transverse-position structure of valence quarks in the nucleon.

The higher-order cumulants develop sign reversals on the high-temperature side of the transition, with the onset moving to lower baryon chemical potentials as the order increases. Ratios of different cumulant orders provide a consistency check of the expected mean-field critical behavior. At fixed chemical potentials, their limits on both sides of the critical point agree with the predictions for the critical-isotherm exponent $δ=3$. The freeze-out analysis reveals nonmonotonic collision-energy dependence that need not be accompanied by sign reversals. On a representative trajectory, the variance reaches a local minimum near $\sqrt{s_{NN}}\simeq6$~GeV, with its position and depth depending on the freeze-out path. Temperature cumulants probe the thermal response and its critical scaling, providing information complementary to conserved-charge fluctuations for exploring the QCD phase diagram.

In string compactifications, dilaton-like moduli always come paired with axions, and the two fields interact through a curved field-space metric. We study the cosmology of such an axio-dilaton system, in which the dilaton rolls down an exponential potential corrected by a polynomial prefactor and couples to a massless axion through the kinetic function $W=e^{-ξφ_1/M_p}$. A dynamical systems analysis shows that the late-time attractor follows a non-geodesic trajectory in field space with equation of state $ω_φ=(λ-2ξ)/(λ+2ξ)$, so accelerated expansion is possible for steep potentials provided $ξ\ggλ$. No physical fixed point is phantom. A Bayesian analysis with DESI DR2 BAO, binned Pantheon supernovae and Planck 2018 distance priors gives $λ\gtrsim7$--$9$ and $\log_{10}ξ\gtrsim2.5$ at 95% confidence, together with a degeneracy between the two parameters. The model is slightly favoured over $Λ$CDM by current data, while the different polynomial corrections cannot yet be distinguished. This contribution is based on arXiv:2609.22539.

In particular, we point out the correspondence of BPM to e-values, proposed as an alternative to conventional p-values in statistics.

Oliver H. E. Philcox
Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic and counterterm contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the VEGAS algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.20h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$, or $0.27h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.42h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for an emission line galaxy sample at $z=1.1$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $σ_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference.

The processes of paired charmonium and bottomonium production in Z-boson decays are investigated within the relativistic quark model. Various decay mechanisms are examined, and relativistic decay amplitudes are constructed, taking into account the relative momenta of heavy quarks. Decay widths are calculated for various mechanisms in the nonrelativistic approximation and taking into account relativistic corrections.

♻ ☆ Neutrino absorption in two-flavor color-superconducting quark matter
Mark G. Alford, Liam Brodie, Michael Buballa, Hosein Gholami, Alexander Haber, Marco Hofmann
We calculate the absorption mean free paths of electron and muon neutrinos in two-flavor color-superconducting (2SC) quark matter in the density and temperature range that is relevant to binary neutron star mergers. We model the strong interaction between quarks using a Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, performing calculations self-consistently in the mean-field approximation. Since the 2SC gap is large we restrict our analysis to the contribution of unpaired quarks. We find that at low temperatures absorption by a down quark $ν+d \to u+e^-/μ^-$ is kinematically not allowed, so absorption by a strange quark $ν+s \to u+e^-/μ^-$ dominates the mean free path. As temperature or neutrino energy rises, the $d$ quark absorption channel becomes active, and the mean free path shrinks. We find that in equilibrated 2SC matter with an electron lepton fraction $Y_{L_e}=0.1$, the neutrinos form a degenerate gas with a mean free path of meters or less, independent of the temperature.

♻ ☆ Electroweak phase transition triggered by a long-lived scalar and LHC searches

We investigate a long-lived scalar $S$ that triggers a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition (SFOEWPT) in the singlet scalar extension of standard model (SM). A sufficient small mixing angle between $S$ and the SM-like Higgs boson $h$ naturally leads to a long lifetime for $S$. We focus on the mass range $m_S>m_h/2$, where the dominant production channel at the LHC is the Higgs-mediated process $gg\to h^*\to SS$ with an off-shell $h$. By analyzing the finite-temperature effective potential, we identify the parameter space realizing an SFOEWPT and calculate the associated gravitational-wave spectra, finding that part of the parameter space can be probed by LISA. We further study the LHC sensitivity to the long-lived $S$ using the ATLAS detector and proposed far detectors, including ANUBIS, CODEX-b, FACET, FASER2, MoEDAL-MAPP1 and MAPP2, and MATHUSLA. The combined sensitivity of the main detector and far detectors, particularly ANUBIS and MATHUSLA, allows a large fraction of the SFOEWPT parameter space to be probed for $10^{-10}\leq \sinθ\leq 10^{-5}$, with $m_S$ up to $250~\mathrm{GeV}$. For $\sinθ\leq 10^{-11}$, however, the SFOEWPT parameter space becomes inaccessible to both the main detector and the far-detector searches.

The focus of this paper is the production of magnetic monopoles via the Drell-Yan and photon-fusion mechanisms to generate velocity-dependent scalar, fermionic, and vector monopoles of spin angular momentum 0, 1/2, 1, respectively at a future muon collider. A computational study compares the monopole pair-production cross-sections for both methods at various center-of-mass energies ($\sqrt{s}$) with different magnetic dipole moments. The comparison of kinematic distributions of monopoles at the generator and reconstructed level is demonstrated for both DY and PF mechanisms. We demonstrate the observability of magnetic monopoles against the most relevant Standard Model background using multivariate analysis techniques. Specifically, we apply three different classifiers based on neural networks, e.g., Boosted Decision Trees, Multilayer Perceptrons, and Likelihood methods, to evaluate their effectiveness. Our results highlight the efficiency and robustness of these approaches in distinguishing magnetic monopole signals from background noise. Quantitatively, our analysis shows that the Photon-Fusion mechanism significantly dominates at high energies; for a spin-1/2 monopole with a mass of 1.5 TeV at $\sqrt{s}=30$ TeV, the PF cross-section (13.33 Pb) is approximately 30 times larger than the Drell-Yan process (0.44 Pb). Furthermore, the Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) classifier outperforms other methods, reaching a signal efficiency of 0.97 and a statistical significance of 22.80 at an optimal cut of 0.042, with an AUC value of 0.989, underscoring the high discovery potential for magnetic monopoles in multi-TeV muon collisions.

The precision of the electromagnetic proton-neutron mass difference $δm_\mathrm{QED}$ extracted from the Cottingham formula hinges on a subtraction function whose low-energy normalization $\bar S(0)$ is fixed by the isovector combination of the proton and neutron polarizabilities, $(α_{E1}-β_{M1})^{p-n}$. This result yields $\bar S(0)=-0.56(28)\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$, leading to $δm_\mathrm{QED}=0.75^{+0.02}_{-0.04}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, substantially more precise than previous Cottingham determinations. ♻ ☆ Accidental Peccei-Quinn Symmetry from Chiral Gauge Symmetry and Mirror QCD
Hajime Fukuda, Keisuke Harigaya
We present a solution to the strong CP problem in which a simple chiral U(1) gauge symmetry gives rise to an accidental Peccei-Quinn symmetry that is both explicitly and spontaneously broken by mirror QCD dynamics, yielding a framework without massless fermions or a light QCD axion. The model contains no stable domain walls or colored relics, and it accommodates a sufficiently high reheating temperature to account for the baryon asymmetry of the Universe via leptogenesis. Metastable domain walls and first-order mirror QCD phase transition generate a stochastic background of primordial gravitational waves. Additionally, one of the pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone bosons serves as a viable WIMP dark matter candidate. The gauge boson associated with the chiral U(1) gauge symmetry, which kinetically mixes with the Standard Model hypercharge gauge boson, provides a vector portal connecting dark matter to the Standard Model and plays a central role in the dark-matter phenomenology. Colored pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone bosons can be probed at the LHC through searches for dijet resonances, jets plus missing energy, multijet events with leptons, and displaced vertices.

♻ ☆ An $A_4$-Symmetric Double Seesaw for Neutrino Masses and Mixing in Light of JUNO results
Swaraj Kumar Nanda, Maibam Ricky Devi, Chandini Dash, R. N. Panda, Sudhanwa Patra
We discuss a double seesaw mechanism for generating light neutrino masses within the Standard Model extensions that include both right-handed neutrinos and extra gauge-singlet sterile fermions. The flavour structure of the double seesaw framework is invoked by an $A_4$ discrete symmetry which yields predictive textures for the Dirac neutrino mass matrix $M_D$, the mixing matrix $M_{RS}$ connecting right-handed and sterile neutrinos, and the bare Majorana mass matrix $M_S$ for the sterile neutrinos. The interesting feature of the present framework is that the combination of the double seesaw mechanism and $A_4$ flavour alignments yields a leading-order TBM structure, corrected by a single rotation in the (1-3) sector. We also derive analytic expressions for the heavy sterile eigenvalues and for the resulting light neutrino masses, thereby clarifying the role of the symmetry in shaping the neutrino mass hierarchy. We further incorporate the most recent JUNO measurements, which improve the precision of the solar mixing angle $\sin^2θ_{12} \simeq 0.31$, along with updated constraints on $\sin^2θ_{13}$. We show that these results significantly restrict the allowed parameter space of the model. In particular, the observed value of $\sin^2θ_{12}$ constrains the magnitude of the (1--3) rotation and the phases associated with the $A_4$ flavon couplings, while the value of $\sin^2θ_{13}$ sharpens these restrictions further. Overall, the interplay between double seesaw dynamics, $A_4$ flavour symmetry, and the recent JUNO constraints yields a highly predictive framework for neutrino masses and mixings, offering a coherent explanation for the generation of light neutrino masses and testable predictions for future experiments.

♻ ☆ Four-loop electron EDM matching and timelike $τ$ electric dipole form factor
Chia-Wei Liu, Zi-Yue Zou
We compute the four-loop matching of a CP-odd four-$τ$ interaction onto the electron electric dipole moment (EDM), together with the leading timelike $τ$ dipole form factor generated by the same source. Both results are scale independent at this order. Without a local electron dipole, exact electron-EDM cancellation still leaves a timelike $τ$ signal proportional to the four-$τ$ coefficient. Its absorptive part cannot be canceled by a real local dipole, allowing collider limits to constrain the cancellation direction and complement static electron-EDM searches.

♻ ☆ Unconventional Materials for Light Dark Matter Detection

We propose the use of several unconventional materials as detectors for dark matter with mass beneath the MeV scale. These include the transition-metal dichalcogenide TiSe$_2$ hosting a low-energy plasmon in the charge-density-wave phase, Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ containing a low-energy acoustic demon mode, and hole-doped diamond with tunable optical and acoustic plasmon frequencies. We perform first-principles density functional theory computations of their loss functions at non-vanishing momenta and establish their reach into light dark matter parameter space. We show that due to intense low-energy plasmon modes -- of different microscopic origin in each -- the reach of detectors based on these materials could surpass existing proposals by several orders of magnitude for both dark matter scattering and absorption on electrons. The anisotropic response of these materials, which enables directional detection, renders them exceptionally strong detector candidates, motivating the design and fabrication of future devices.

☆ Spiralling into Dark Energy: Axio-Dilaton Attractors in Light of Current Data
Mario Ramos-Hamud
In string compactifications, dilaton-like moduli always come paired with axions, and the two fields interact through a curved field-space metric. We study the cosmology of such an axio-dilaton system, in which the dilaton rolls down an exponential potential corrected by a polynomial prefactor and couples to a massless axion through the kinetic function $W=e^{-ξφ_1/M_p}$. A dynamical systems analysis shows that the late-time attractor follows a non-geodesic trajectory in field space with equation of state $ω_φ=(λ-2ξ)/(λ+2ξ)$, so accelerated expansion is possible for steep potentials provided $ξ\ggλ$. No physical fixed point is phantom. A Bayesian analysis with DESI DR2 BAO, binned Pantheon supernovae and Planck 2018 distance priors gives $λ\gtrsim7$--$9$ and $\log_{10}ξ\gtrsim2.5$ at 95% confidence, together with a degeneracy between the two parameters. The model is slightly favoured over $Λ$CDM by current data, while the different polynomial corrections cannot yet be distinguished. This contribution is based on arXiv:2609.22539.
☆ Exact lattice bosonization of the double-scaled $c=1$ matrix model

In a recent paper by two of us, it has been shown that entanglement entropy (EE) of matrix quantum mechanics (or, equivalently, of a non-relativistic fermion model) has a natural interpretation in terms of an exact bosonization of the fermion theory in terms of a lattice boson with lattice spacing $\sim 1/N$ (where $N$ is the rank of the matrix, equal to the number of fermions). The theory of this lattice boson is distinct from a latticized version of the "collective variable'' theory which is formulated in terms of the fermion density $ρ(λ)$ ("collective variable''); it is, in fact, more closely related to the Wigner distribution of the fermions. In this paper, we develop this connection further for the $c=1$ double scaled matrix model. Even though $N$ becomes infinite, the double scaled theory is described by a boson on a finite and non-uniform lattice spacing, of order $\sim g_s(x) l_s$ (where $g_s(x) \equiv g_s {\rm cosech}^2(x/l_s)$ is a position dependent string coupling). We explicitly derive the $c=1$ EE, as well as the one and two-point functions of fermion density from the lattice boson. The results are explicitly finite, unlike the collective variable theory which is shown to yield divergent answers. Our results suggest that while local observables such as the EE and $\langle ρ(λ) \rangle$, are characterized by a unique short distance scale $g_s(x) l_s$, the asymptotic observables such as the S-matrix at every genus are characterized by a short distance scale $l_s$. We show how this arises and discuss a possible interpretation in terms of D0 brane physics.

☆ Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
Akio Tomiya
When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory define a family of probability distributions that forms a statistical manifold, and its Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. In the large-$N$ limit of the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ is taken to zero with the mass gap $Λ$ fixed, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $σ$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and the Fisher metric of the full $P(σ)$. In the former, the lengths of the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term shrink, relative to the mass-term direction, to order $aΛ\log(1/(aΛ))$ or smaller, and when several modes are combined, only the two directions $(Λ,m)$ of the continuum theory remain. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink at the same rate as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in correlations at distances of the order of the lattice spacing. An exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator: as $a\to0$ its length goes to zero in both metrics, and it becomes indistinguishable from a change of the coupling $1/g^2$ (a lattice version of Kutasov's result). The curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(aΛ))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point is infinitely far in Fisher distance from any point at finite $a$.
