☆ All-plus Yang--Mills and gravity wavefunctions in de Sitter space
Song He, Jiajie Mei, Yuyu Mo
We present sewing representations for tree-level all-plus wavefunctions in four-dimensional de Sitter space. For Yang--Mills theory, the arbitrary-multiplicity formula is a sum over noncrossing polygon dissections, with each cell carrying energy differences of a full lower-point wavefunction. The absence of a generic total-energy pole is manifest, while partial-energy residues are determined by the lower-point factors. We derive this representation from self-dual Yang--Mills solutions. For Einstein gravity, we propose an arbitrary-multiplicity formula consisting of an alternating sum over labelled sewing trees plus a local gravitational Chern--Simons term. This local term arises from the self-dual Einstein action and supplies boundary data not fixed by internal-energy cuts. We derive a generating formula for it from the boundary connection and give explicit expressions through seven points.

☆ Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories

We establish global control of perturbative D-term data governing semiclassical vacuum sectors in chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$. A closed-form, one-loop-exact D-term coefficient, including 4d Fayet--Iliopoulos (FI) parameters, gives a uniformly controlled leading potential away from massless thresholds and fixes local FI and Chern--Simons couplings near them. This allows lifting the 3d Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua to $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$ across the compact holonomy space. The framework is showcased by finding a remarkably rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple abelian model and reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory, first found on $S^3\times S^1$. The examples demonstrate the stakes of global matching: true vacua may lie at nontrivial holonomy even with nonzero threshold values of the Coulomb-slice D-coefficient, and despite vanishing D-coefficient at trivial holonomy.

☆ Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation

We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $θ$ and $η$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response. By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $θ$ and $η$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.
☆ Lifshitz Phase of Quantum Gravity: The Infrared Fixed Point of the (2+1)D Unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons Model
Maxim Zelenko, Dam Thanh Son
We consider a nonrelativistic gravity theory in (2+1) dimensions with $w_\infty$ gauge symmetry that we call unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity. The theory has three dimensionless couplings, one of which is the Chern-Simons level $κ$. At large $|κ|$, the theory flows from an asymptotically free UV fixed point to an IR fixed point with anisotropic scale invariance characterized by a dynamical critical exponent $z=2-\tfrac32|κ|^{-1}$. We speculate that unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity undergoes a phase transition from this scale-invariant phase to a confining phase when $κ$ drops below a critical value.

Monodromy defects are fundamental objects in extended quantum systems with global symmetries. We study such defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories (CFT), which describe the universality class of $\text{O}(N)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking transitions. In particular, we consider partial-monodromy defects, whose corresponding symmetry transformations only act on a subset of the fundamental $\text{O}(N)$ vector field. We develop an analytical theory of the defect phases, using both renormalization group and large $N$ expansion. In general (spacetime) dimensions $3\leq d<4$, multiple defect CFTs are identified, which are described by appropriate boundary conditions for the vector field near the defect. Near $d=3$, we show that in the large $N$ limit, a stable defect CFT always exists, characterized by the so-called ("standard") "alternate" boundary conditions for the (twisted) untwisted fields, whose defect correlations are (suppressed) enhanced. We then perform large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations of monodromy defects in the O(3) CFT in an improved lattice model and numerically extract the defect scaling dimensions. The numerical results are in qualitative agreement with the stable defect CFT identified in the field theory.

♻ ☆ M2 brane in AdS$_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$: 2-loop correction to $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS Wilson loop vs localization in ABJM theory
M. Beccaria, S. A. Kurlyand, A. A. Tseytlin, J. van Muiden
We study the quantization of an M2 brane wrapping $\mathrm{AdS}_2\times S^1$ inside $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$, dual to the $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS circular Wilson loop in ABJM theory. The classical action and the one-loop contribution were previously shown to reproduce the gauge-theory localization result. Here we extend the analysis to the two-loop order. In an adapted static and $κ$-symmetry gauge the world-volume action contains no cubic interaction vertices, so that the two-loop correction is determined entirely by quartic interactions and is manifestly free of logarithmic UV divergences. We find that the bosonic and fermionic contributions combine into a perfect square $ {\mathscr X}^2$ where ${\mathscr X}$ is a linear combination of the bosonic and fermionic 3d Green's functions and their derivatives. The evaluation of $\mathscr X$ requires fixing the $\mathrm{AdS}_2$ boundary quantization of the massless fermionic modes. With the boundary conditions selected by the preserved supersymmetry, $\mathscr X$ vanishes and hence the complete two-loop correction is found to be zero. This result would not be consistent with identifying the M2-brane loop expansion directly with the large-$N$ expansion of the canonical, fixed-$(N,k)$ localization prediction. Instead, it agrees precisely with the recent proposal that the semiclassical M2-brane partition function should be matched to the gauge-theory grand-canonical ensemble, in which the Wilson loop expectation value is perturbatively one-loop exact. The vanishing of the two-loop correction thus provides a non-trivial test of this grand-canonical identification.

♻ ☆ From the massive Schwinger model to unimodular Euclidean gravity with fermions

The massive Schwinger model (two-dimensional electrodynamics coupled to Dirac fermions) in Euclidean spacetime is mapped onto two-dimensional unimodular gravity in the first-order formalism, also including fermions. The idea of the map relies almost entirely on the isomorphism between the gauge groups $U(1)$ and $SO(2)$. However, the resulting fermion-gravity coupling differs from the conventional form, explicitly violating parity and time-reversal symmetries. Moreover, these fermions exhibit an unconventional transformation behavior under $SO(2)$ transformations. We show, however, that these properties are absent on the gravitational side of the mapping when starting from an axial massive Schwinger model. Several explicit examples of the mapping are considered, including the constant electric field and point-particle systems. For these examples, we explicitly derive the corresponding gravitational manifolds and compute the associated metrics. Furthermore, we analyze the consistency of the mapping at the quantum level using the path-integral formalism and Becchi-Rouet-Stora-Tyutin (BRST) techniques. Our results demonstrate that the proposed mapping remains consistent at the quantum level, establishing a formal BRST-compatible field correspondence between quantum electrodynamics and quantum gravity, at least at the $U(1) - SO(2)$ gauge sector, which does not include the diffeomorphic features of gravity.

However, this view relies on the assumption that light interacts with materials solely through its electric field. Here, we demonstrate that interference between the electric and magnetic components of the same light field can induce even-order NLO effects even in centrosymmetric materials. Using charge and spin photocurrents as prototypical examples, we present a unified microscopic theory showing how such electric-magnetic dipole interference (EMDI) drives NLO responses in inversion-symmetric crystals. Bilinear in both electric and magnetic fields, these responses scale linearly with light intensity. Combining symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations, we decompose the EMDI-induced photocurrents into shift-like and injection-like contributions and classify their dependence on crystal symmetry, time-reversal symmetry, and light polarization. Notably, we reveal that these EMDI-induced responses in centrosymmetric materials are weaker than conventional responses in non-centrosymmetric materials roughly by a factor of fine structure constant $α\approx [10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-2}] $. Nevertheless, they remain well within experimental reach. Our work thus unlocks NLO functionalities in centrosymmetric materials for e.g., materials characterization, photonics and optoelectronics. This is vital given that many functionally importantly materials, such as cubic Si and cubic $\mathrm{SrTiO_3}$, possess inversion symmetry.

Materials research relies on scattered and growing data, knowledge, and simulation tools, and a single study often spans multi-day workflows across literature analysis, computation, and experiment. Large language model agents can now retrieve materials data, operate simulation codes, and close design-synthesis-characterization loops with autonomous laboratories. ☆ Designing sustainability under Earth-system rate constraints
José Halloy, Petros Chatzimpiros, François Graner, Thomas Gregor
Sustainability debates are monopolized by quantities: total energy use, material stocks, or recycling volumes. These metrics are informative, but they obscure a more fundamental constraint. On a materially closed but energetically open Earth, long-term viability is governed by rates: power density, areal power density, and the rate at which dispersed materials can be repurified under dif- fuse solar fluxes. We develop a physical framework that links technological metabolism, material dilution, and recycling limits through these rate con- straints. This perspective clarifies why many contemporary technologies remain viable only through stock drawdown and high-power buffering, and why green growth strategies often shift rather than resolve the underlying mismatch between industrial activity and Earth-system dynamics. We argue that long-term sustain- ability requires both quantitative reduction in aggregate industrial throughput toward rate-bounded regimes and the development of technologies qualitatively compatible with biospheric operating conditions.

Yingheng Wang, Tao Yu, Shufeng Kong, Francesco Ricci, John M. Gregoire, Carla P. Gomes
Structured scientific spectra encode rich physical information while obeying hard constraints, such as conservation laws and characteristic spectral geometry. Accurate prediction of these spectra is central to materials discovery, yet existing methods often treat them as unconstrained sequences and therefore fail to enforce the underlying physical structure. Taking electronic density of states (eDOS) as the prototypical example, we introduce DeepSciReasoner, a general paradigm for predicting scientific spectra under physical constraints. The framework combines structure-aware spectrum decoding with constraint-preserving physical reasoning, allowing predictions to capture rich spectral structure while respecting the underlying physics. We evaluate DeepSciReasoner on eDOS, phonon density of states (phDOS), X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), and Raman spectra, where it substantially improves prediction accuracy while maintaining physical consistency. These results establish DeepSciReasoner as a reusable blueprint for structured scientific spectrum prediction under hard physical constraints.

The two baths rank the states differently: the graphene-rate ratios differ from the optical ones, their ordering inverts with spacer thickness, and the distance exponents at $z=10$\,nm spread by more than two units. These ratios are independent of the transition-dipole prefactor. Within the $C_3$-symmetric leading-harmonic model the chiral $p_+$ and $d_-$ states are also dark at normal incidence yet transfer to graphene at rates comparable to the bright ground state. Their graphene rate depends on the sign of the texture phase, a quantity invisible in far-field emission, which we determine from first principles. In a device this prediction requires a splitting, larger than the symmetry-breaking mixing, that protects the chiral partners. Graphene proximity thus acts as a momentum-selective near-field probe of moiré excitons, and we propose its use as a practical spectroscopy.

♻ ☆ Coherent Phonon Generation from Prethermal Carrier Populations in a Semiconductor

Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. Fitting this model to the data yields an excited transition state lifetime of a few femtoseconds. These results identify transition selectivity, rather than a thermalized total carrier density, as a key factor controlling coherent-phonon generation in semiconductors excited near a band gap.

Yaroslav Zhumagulov, Johan Félisaz, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Denis Kochan, Oleg V. Yazyev

We address this limitation by deriving a dynamical proximity operator directly from density functional theory by downfolding the heterostructure Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian onto a fixed low-energy target Wannier subspace. We demonstrate the method for three different graphene heterostructures coupled to magnetic and semiconducting substrates. Graphene/hBN/Co(0001) exhibits proximity-induced exchange resonances driven by hybridization with Co states. Graphene/PtSe$_2$ develops a sublattice-selective, intervalley-coherent, proximity-induced coupling. For graphene/WSe$_2$, we identify the spatial modulation of both Rashba and valley-Zeeman proximity-induced spin-orbit couplings. ♻ ☆ Splicing an exact local self-energy into $GW$: tests on small Hubbard clusters
Michael O. Atambo
$GW$+DMFT-type schemes replace the local part of a $GW$ self-energy by a separately computed local self-energy. A causal double counting removes a non-causal term from the hybridization (Lee and Haule, 2017), but the resulting total self-energy has been flagged as not guaranteed to be causal (Zhu and Chan, 2021). From the Herglotz representation, the spliced self-energy is causal if and only if its spectral measure is positive semi-definite. For translation-invariant single-band systems this becomes a momentum-resolved bound: the local weight may fall short of the local $GW$ weight by at most the momentum minimum of the $GW$ weight. On finite clusters, a mismatch between $GW$ and exact poles generically produces indefinite residues. On the Matsubara axis, a negative damping eigenvalue at one frequency certifies non-causality; passing does not establish causality. We examine these diagnostics in an idealized setting, not self-consistent $GW$+DMFT: one-shot $GW$ on the exact Green's function of small Hubbard clusters with the exact local self-energy inserted. At all 528 parameter sets, our computed $GW$ and exact self-energies pass both tests, as expected. The splice fails the pointwise test at 54 points, none at half filling, all at the lowest Matsubara frequency, and already at $U/t=0.5$; there the local $GW$ damping is 1.3-9 times the exact one. A block Pick test on eight frequencies, run with a second imaginary-time code, flags 481 of the 528 sets; for the other 47 it is inconclusive. Moment checks miss all of these, because the spliced high-frequency moment is exact. The Dyson Green's function is then non-causal too, yet passes the pointwise test everywhere tested. This version replaces a withdrawn one whose reported causality violations of $GW$ itself came from a sign error in the polarization; with the sign corrected, the computed $GW$ shows the expected positivity.

However, carbon-based altermagnets in graphene structures remain elusive, even though magnetism in graphene nanostructures has been widely demonstrated. Here, we establish a symmetry-guided design principle to engineer i-wave altermagnets in graphene antidot superlattices and demonstrate the emergence of altermagnetic states in specific monolayer and bilayer graphene superlattices. By combining first principles methods and atomistic tight binding models, we show the appearance of an interaction-induced i-wave altermagnetic splitting, stemming from the intrinsic magnetic instability of 2D graphene antidot superlattices. Our work establishes a strategy to engineer i-wave altermagnetism in a graphene platform, putting forward a carbon-based platform for altermagnetic spintronics.

Muhammad Arief Mulyana, Budi Adiperdana, Ayi Bahtiar

We study both steps for an 8 nm GdFeCo film inserted across a Si$_3$N$_4$ waveguide. A three-dimensional dispersive finite-difference time-domain calculation gives the energy absorbed from an 800 nm pump pulse. This energy drives a four-temperature model and calibrated stochastic two-sublattice Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch dynamics. After relaxation, a separate 532 nm probe is propagated through the fixed magnetic state for the optical readout. At the reference pump fluence, the model reverses 0.859 of the film from either saturated state. The switched fraction remains within 0.81-0.87 over a 2.4-fold range of incident fluence. A threshold rule applied to the local absorption map reproduces the five three-dimensional simulation points to within $8\times10^{-4}$, showing that, within the model, incomplete reversal results from non-uniform guided-mode absorption. When the film starts from zero magnetization, thermal noise orients the recovered local moments at random; over 16 realizations, $0.502 \pm 0.004$ of the cells end with a negative $x$ component of the FeCo moment. Among the simulated states, the probe transmission, reflection, and absorption fractions vary by at most 0.02. The magnetic Faraday and Kerr rotations are much more sensitive and become about 12 and 130 times smaller, respectively, in the stochastically recovered state than in a saturated film. The reflected signal also contains a magnetization-independent geometric background, which can be removed by subtracting a reference signal. These results link the switching efficiency to the guided-mode absorption profile and predict polarization-based readout of the simulated magnetic states. The model assumes a homogeneous film and neglects spatial exchange stiffness and subsequent domain coarsening.

Here, we employ first-principles density functional theory calculations to quantitatively investigate nonradiative carrier capture processes mediated by multiphonon emission at both the NV center and the N$_{\rm C}$ impurity. Both the magnitude and temperature dependence are in excellent agreement with experimentally measured capture cross sections. Electron capture at N$_{\rm C}^+$ is even faster, with a capture coefficient of $1.0 \times 10^{-4}$ cm$^3$s$^{-1}$ at 300 K. For the NV center, we find that carrier capture rates involving only the ground states of NV$^0$ and NV$^-$ are negligibly slow. However, capture into the excited states (NV$^{0*}$ and NV$^{-*}$) is significantly faster. In particular, the capture coefficient for the hole capture process NV$^-$ $\to$ NV$^{0*}$ is as large as $1.8 \times 10^{-7}$ cm$^3$s$^{-1}$ and largely temperature-independent. ♻ ☆ Revealing the proton slingshot mechanism in solid acid electrolytes through machine learning molecular dynamics

In solid acid electrolytes CsH$_2$PO$_4$ and CsHSO$_4$, the origin of fast proton conduction has long been debated, attributed either to local proton hopping or to polyanion rotation. However, the precise role of polyanion rotation and its interplay with proton hopping remained unresolved. In CsH$_2$PO$_4$, two rotation rates with different activation energies emerge, while CsHSO$_4$ displays a single-rate process with faster productive polyanion dynamics. The higher proton concentration in CsH$_2$PO$_4$ frustrates PO$_4$ rotation, resulting in slower dynamics than for SO$_4$ in CsHSO$_4$. In CsH$_2$PO$_4$, we further identify a unique correlation between oxygen sharing and proton transport, arising from the extra proton per polyanion. Together, our findings establish a unified framework linking polyanion rotation, proton coordination, and long-range transport, and suggest that tuning proton concentration could accelerate rotation and enhance conductivity.

Finite-size effects are ubiquitous in quantum matter, yet typically invisible in the thermodynamic limit; when system size is restricted, boundaries and confinement reveal modified spectra, correlations, and emergent phenomena. With growing access to well-controlled few-spin systems, these effects are now directly observable and offer a route to probing universal physics and enabling quantum information applications. Here, we study finite-size physics in the quasi-one-dimensional Ising-like quantum antiferromagnet Ba(Co$_{1-x}$Mg$_x$)$_2$V$_2$O$_8$ with $x = 2\%$ and $x = 5\%$, where non-magnetic Mg$^{2+}$ ions fragment the Co$^{2+}$ spin chains into finite segments. Our results demonstrate how chemical substitution acts as a quantum microscope providing direct access to boundary-shaped excitations in strongly correlated spin systems.

When electrons move through non-trivial spin textures in magnetic metals, conduction electrons couple to magnetic order through both their charge and their spin, acquiring non-trivial equations of motion and a dynamic spin polarization providing the foundation of spintronics. These mechanisms are, however, almost invariably reciprocal and the resistance a current encounters does not depend on its flow direction. Here we show that a chiral crystal lattice and an independently reversible chiral magnetic order together produce a diode whose forward direction is set by the magnetism rather than by the structure. In the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$, whose chiral lattice hosts a chiral magnetic order of its own, independent handedness, we observe a pronounced nonreciprocal resistance. Unlike conventional electrical magnetochiral anisotropy, which is driven by an external magnetic field, our spontaneous magnetic diode effect arises from an internal noncoplanar spin texture with vanishing net magnetization. Symmetry analysis and model calculations show that the effect originates from the interplay of noncoplanar spin order and spin-orbit coupling, which generates a chiral, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking electronic response. Crucially, reversing the magnetic handedness reverses the sign of the nonreciprocal resistance, demonstrating magnetic control of the diode polarity.

Microscopic calculations reproduce the observed spatial pattern and identify it as a fingerprint of nodeless d-wave pairing. In particular, we consider partial-monodromy defects, whose corresponding symmetry transformations only act on a subset of the fundamental $\text{O}(N)$ vector field. Near $d=3$, we show that in the large $N$ limit, a stable defect CFT always exists, characterized by the so-called ("standard") "alternate" boundary conditions for the (twisted) untwisted fields, whose defect correlations are (suppressed) enhanced. We then perform large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations of monodromy defects in the O(3) CFT in an improved lattice model and numerically extract the defect scaling dimensions. The numerical results are in qualitative agreement with the stable defect CFT identified in the field theory.

♻ ☆ Splicing an exact local self-energy into $GW$: tests on small Hubbard clusters
Michael O. Atambo
$GW$+DMFT-type schemes replace the local part of a $GW$ self-energy by a separately computed local self-energy. A causal double counting removes a non-causal term from the hybridization (Lee and Haule, 2017), but the resulting total self-energy has been flagged as not guaranteed to be causal (Zhu and Chan, 2021). From the Herglotz representation, the spliced self-energy is causal if and only if its spectral measure is positive semi-definite. For translation-invariant single-band systems this becomes a momentum-resolved bound: the local weight may fall short of the local $GW$ weight by at most the momentum minimum of the $GW$ weight. On finite clusters, a mismatch between $GW$ and exact poles generically produces indefinite residues. On the Matsubara axis, a negative damping eigenvalue at one frequency certifies non-causality; passing does not establish causality. We examine these diagnostics in an idealized setting, not self-consistent $GW$+DMFT: one-shot $GW$ on the exact Green's function of small Hubbard clusters with the exact local self-energy inserted. At all 528 parameter sets, our computed $GW$ and exact self-energies pass both tests, as expected. The splice fails the pointwise test at 54 points, none at half filling, all at the lowest Matsubara frequency, and already at $U/t=0.5$; there the local $GW$ damping is 1.3-9 times the exact one. A block Pick test on eight frequencies, run with a second imaginary-time code, flags 481 of the 528 sets; for the other 47 it is inconclusive. Moment checks miss all of these, because the spliced high-frequency moment is exact. The Dyson Green's function is then non-causal too, yet passes the pointwise test everywhere tested. This version replaces a withdrawn one whose reported causality violations of $GW$ itself came from a sign error in the polarization; with the sign corrected, the computed $GW$ shows the expected positivity.

We study the reciprocal Barnett and Einstein--de Haas effects in an exactly solvable quantum spin--rotor model that conserves the total angular momentum. For a single spin-$1/2$, the model describes rotation-dependent spin polarization, coherent transfer of angular momentum between the spin and the rotor, and the accompanying spin--rotor entanglement. At a recoil-compensation point, all angular-momentum sectors become synchronized, allowing complete spin reversal and a one-quantum shift of an arbitrary rotor wave packet. We then extend the model to two spins coupled to the same rotor, where the shared rotational degree of freedom participates dynamically in the generation of spin--spin entanglement. The singlet forms a dark state, while the triplet sector remains coupled to the mechanical motion. At a special parameter point, the rotor returns to its original dynamical branch and disentangles from the spins, leaving behind a maximally entangled two-spin state locally equivalent to a Bell state.

In this work, we present a comprehensive theoretical study for the topological and anomalous transport properties of type-II SDSMs under three scenarios, i.e., static symmetry-breaking perturbations, periodic Floquet driving by two-frequency orthogonally polarized light (TFOPL), and their cooperative effects in the hybrid scenario. We first show that a static mass $m_z$ opens a bulk gap and drives the system into a Chern insulator with Chern number $C^{\rm per}=\pm 2\,{\rm sgn}(m_z)$. In comparison, TFOPL alone only shifts the positions of Dirac points and cannot open a full gap. Nevertheless, it produces a Berry curvature odd in the $x$-direction, yielding a finite Berry curvature dipole (BCD) along $x$ proportional to the sine of the initial phase, while the $y$-component vanishes. The hybrid scenario, by contrast, exhibits a remarkably rich phenomenology. Specifically, its gap-closure criterion becomes cubic and thus admits up to three real roots when the effective parameter along the $x$-direction is negative, thereby producing multiple light-tunable gap-closing points and a series of topological phase transitions. In particular, the BCD exhibits a double-peak structure with strong enhancement near gap-closing manifolds and synchronized sign reversal of the full vector under external tuning. We further analyze the anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC), anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC), and anomalous thermal Hall conductivity (ATHC). The AHC and ATHC exhibit quantized plateaus that serve as signatures of Chern-insulator phases, while the ANC, being a Fermi-surface probe, provides complementary local information and can identify light-induced gaps even when global topological invariants remain unchanged. Taken together, these results offer useful insights into the topological properties of 2D type-II SDSMs and related systems.

We construct new finite-temperature, composition-dependent equation of state (EOS) tables for astrophysical simulations by implementing a recently developed energy-density functional. The functional is constrained by ab initio nuclear matter calculations and neutron-star observations. A distinguishing feature of this functional is a non-monotonic density dependence of the nucleon effective mass, with an increase beyond saturation density. Using these EOS tables, we investigate the impact of current uncertainties in nuclear matter properties on core-collapse supernova (CCSN) evolution with spherically symmetric simulations employing an effective treatment of convective mixing. The magnitude of the EOS effects depends on the progenitor compactness. Within current constraints, variations in incompressibility, symmetry energy, and high-density pressure produce only modest differences during the early post-bounce evolution. In contrast, the effective mass dependence has a much stronger influence on proto-neutron star contraction and the explosion dynamics in a stellar model with high core compactness. Its non-monotonic density dependence leads to a qualitatively different contraction history and can alter the explosion outcome compared to mean-field effective-mass behaviors. Therefore, among the nuclear matter properties considered, the density dependence of the nucleon effective masses has by far the largest impact on CCSN dynamics. This highlights the importance of realistic effective-mass parameterizations in nuclear EOSs used in astrophysical simulations.

Then, we show that the imaginary-time correlation function in a finite volume approaches that of the infinite volume as $τ/L^2 \rightarrow 0$ while it is dominated by the lowest energy mode as $τ/L^2 \rightarrow \infty$, where $τ$ is the imaginary time, $L$ is the volume size. ☆ Subthreshold Resonances in the Scattering of μ^-Mesons by Atomic Nuclei
F. M. Penkov, A. Mukhametkaliuly
A theoretical study of pre-threshold resonant excitation of atomic nuclei is presented. A formalism for utilizing leptonic probes in the energy region of a Feshbach-Baz pre-threshold resonance is proposed. The resonance positions and widths are shown to be intrinsically linked to the nuclear structure parameters. The correspondence of the giant dipole resonance (GDR) region for heavy nuclei to low probe energies, as well as its large resonance widths, is demonstrated. Through this framework, free from the intense background, the observable signatures of GDR excitation and de-excitation channels, including nuclear fission, are predicted

Our analysis confirms that thermal vorticity, which satisfies the global equilibrium condition, is also a solution to the spin-hydrodynamic equations. Additionally, we calculate the magnetization of the system in global equilibrium and introduce a novel phenomenon - thermovortical magnetization - resulting from thermal vorticity, which can be experimentally observed in graphene.

♻ ☆ FUSION: a skill-based research agent for publicly obtainable nuclear-physics codes
Jin Lei
Running an unfamiliar nuclear-physics code is rarely difficult because of the physics alone. One must find and build the program, learn its input conventions, and decide whether a plausible output is actually correct. A general-purpose coding agent helps with the first two tasks but may make the last one harder: it can write an input file that runs with the wrong physical convention. FUSION addresses this problem with code-specific skills. A skill obtains the code from its public source, starts from a verified input, runs and parses the calculation, records known failure modes, and must reproduce a stated benchmark to a stated tolerance before reporting a result. The current release covers twenty codes, spanning optical models and reactions, nuclear structure, fission and statistical models, astrophysics and R-matrix analysis, and heavy-ion transport. It also includes an offline, searchable collection of 61 167 pages derived from the nucl-th literature. User notes and credentials remain outside the public repository. FUSION is available under the MIT license at https://github.com/jinleiphys/FUSION; documentation is at https://vibeinscience.com. Here I describe the design, the checks behind the current release, and one complete calculation from input to comparison with measured data.

The medium modifications of the baryons arise due to interactions with the mean scalar and vector fields within the model. The thermodynamic and transport properties are studied in the hot strange hadronic matter. The diffusion matrix associated with the multiple charges (baryon number, isospin, and strangeness), as well as the coefficient of shear viscosity, are computed from the Boltzmann equation using first-order Chapman--Enskog expansion within the relaxation time approximation. The coefficient of shear viscosity, $η$ is observed to have a large enhancement in the presence of finite strangeness in the medium due to additional contributions from the hyperons. The effects due to isospin asymmetry on the shear viscosity coefficient is however observed to be marginal both in nuclear and hyperonic matter. The present study can be relevant for the experimental observables of asymmetric relativistic heavy-ion collisions, e.g., in the compressed baryonic matter (CBM) experiment at the FAIR facility at GSI as well as in the future J-PARC-HI program.

♻ ☆ Colloquium: Nuclear clocks
Andrei Derevianko, R. Elwell, Eric R. Hudson
The Th-229 nuclear isomeric state has the lowest energy of all known nuclear excited states, placing it within the reach of current table-top laser technology. This extraordinary property has made this nuclear isomer an attractive candidate for a nuclear optical clock of incredibly high precision and accuracy, both as isolated trapped Th-229 ions and embedded into solid-state platforms. Activity around Th-229 has surged in recent years, driven by breakthroughs in its direct laser excitation. The underlying nuclear physics that gives rise to this unique isomer will be elucidated, as well as the nearly half-century of efforts that led to its direct excitation. The design and systematics of a Th-229 nuclear clock will be discussed, both in ion traps and in the solid-state. These systematics, such as frequency shifts and quenching channels, can be leveraged both to probe the local chemical environment, and as a control knob during clock operation. Finally, the nuclear clock's high sensitivity to the variations of fundamental constants will be discussed.

We then investigate the corresponding collider constraints using the ATLAS dilepton resonance search at \(\sqrt{s}=13\) TeV with an integrated luminosity of \(139\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}\), assuming negligible \(Z-Z'\) mixing and kinematically inaccessible exotic fermions. A particularly interesting result emerges for the \(b=c=1\) configuration, where all \(Z'\) couplings to Standard Model fermions are proportional to \(\sinψ\), with \(ψ\) denoting the additional neutral gauge-boson mixing angle. Consequently, these couplings vanish simultaneously at \(ψ=nπ\), giving rise to a fermiophobic limit in which conventional Drell-Yan dilepton constraints disappear. In contrast, the \(b=1,\ c=-2\) configuration does not exhibit a universal fermiophobic limit. Our results demonstrate that collider constraints on additional neutral gauge bosons depend sensitively on the fermion embeddings and neutral gauge-boson mixing structure, and suggest the possibility of comparatively light \(Z'\) bosons in suitable realizations of extended electroweak gauge theories.

☆ Spectroscopy of the SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system under the influence of the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
Axel Maas, Sofie Martins, Georg Wieland
We investigate the ground state spectrum of a dynamical scalar-fermion-gauge system with an SU(2) gauge group, a scalar doublet, and two degenerate generations of vectorial fermions under the influence of the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect. To this end, we employ lattice methods using the HiRep code. We study the dependence of the system on the (bare) fermion mass and find that the spectrum remains unaffected, up to trivial fermion mass effects. The results are in line with a weakly coupled theory exhibiting the Fröhlich-Morchio-Strocchi mechanism.
comment: 29 pages, 11 figures, 12 tables; submission to SciPost
☆ A Tool-Grounded AI Agent for Gauge Coupling Unification and Proton Decay
Shaikh Saad
We present proton_agent, a tool-grounded AI agent that enables natural-language interaction with computational tools for gauge coupling unification and proton decay in grand unified theories. The agent translates user requests into computational tasks, selects and executes the appropriate tools, and interprets their outputs. All numerical calculations, model evaluations, experimental comparisons, parameter scans, and visualizations are handled by a deterministic scientific backend to ensure numerical accuracy and reproducibility. A central objective of this framework is to enable fully local deployment using free and open-source LLMs, while retaining compatibility with commercial LLM APIs. The framework computes one- and two-loop gauge beta coefficients for user-defined scalar and fermion multiplets and performs gauge coupling evolution through the Standard Model and various intermediate symmetry-breaking stages of $SO(10)$, including $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R \times U(1)_{B-L}$, $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_R \times U(1)_{B-L}$, $SU(4)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_R$, and $SU(4)_C \times SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R$. For proton decay, the framework evaluates gauge-mediated dimension-six contributions in non-supersymmetric $SU(5)$ and $SO(10)$, as well as dressed dimension-five contributions in their supersymmetric counterparts. It supports benchmark calculations for user-specified parameter points, random and grid-based parameter scans, Markov-chain Monte Carlo exploration, comparisons with experimental limits, and publication-ready two- and three-dimensional visualizations. We describe the agent architecture, demonstrate its capabilities through representative benchmark calculations and regression tests, and discuss its current physics scope.
comment: 27 pages + references; The code is publicly available at https://github.com/saad-hep/proton_agent
☆ Catastrophe Structure and Stability of Axion Stars
Fedor V Kusmartsev, Joudy J F Beek, Jack C M Hughes
Axion stars are self-gravitating Bose--Einstein condensates of QCD axions or axion-like particles. Their stability determines whether they can survive as dark-matter structures and what astrophysical signatures they may produce. Here we combine a non-relativistic Schrödinger--Poisson description with catastrophe theory to develop a unified picture of axion-star stability. Beginning with the Einstein--Klein--Gordon system for a periodic axion potential, we derive the effective equations of motion and conserved quantities and construct a one-parameter family of star-like solutions. A Gaussian variational ansatz reduces the problem to an analytic energy functional $E(R;N)$. Within this model, equilibria appear and disappear through Arnold $A_2$, $A_3$, and $A_4$ catastrophes as the particle number $N$ and interaction strengths vary. A repulsive sextic interaction produces two stable branches---dilute and dense axion stars---separated by an unstable branch. The same catastrophe criteria apply beyond the sextic truncation: for the full cosine and QCD-corrected potentials, the fold conditions follow from the complete variational energy and can be evaluated numerically. We also separate stability within the collective-coordinate ansatz from full radial perturbative stability and specify the range in which the non-relativistic treatment is reliable. This framework provides a compact classification of axion-star phases and identifies model-dependent critical masses associated with collapse, bosenova-like emission, and black-hole formation.

♻ ☆ More QCD Masterclass Lectures on Jet Physics and Machine Learning
Andrew J. Larkoski
These lectures were presented at the 2026 QCD Masterclass in Saint-Jacut-de-la-mer, France. They supplement the published notes from the 2024 school with presentation of a few new topics that have become popular in recent years. These include event metrics, anomaly detection, scaling laws, the limits of classification performance, and regression that respects spacetime symmetries. Many of the presented results are known, but some new results are derived, especially related to anomaly detection. As was the case in those original notes, while all these problems are motivated from machine learning applied to QCD, no discussion of details of machine learning is presented in these notes. All results follow from application of fundamental principles of QCD. I begin these notes with an apology for humanist physics.

♻ ☆ Weizsäcker-Williams Gluon Helicity Distribution and Inclusive Dijet Production in Longitudinally Polarized Electron-Proton Collisions
Yuri V. Kovchegov, Ming Li
It is well-known that the back-to-back (correlation) limit of inclusive quark-antiquark dijet production in unpolarized high energy electron-proton collisions can probe the Weizsäcker-Williams (WW) gluon transverse momentum-dependent distribution (TMD) at small $x$ \cite{Dominguez:2010xd, Dominguez:2011wm}. In this paper, we consider a helicity-dependent version of the same process: we study the double-spin asymmetry for inclusive quark-antiquark dijet production in longitudinally polarized electron-proton scattering at high energies. We show that in the back-to-back limit this process probes the WW gluon helicity TMD. Furthermore, we derive the small-$x$ evolution equation for the operator related to the WW gluon helicity distribution. We find that in the double-logarithmic approximation and in the large-$N_c$ limit, the small-$x$ asymptotics of the WW gluon helicity distribution is governed by exactly the same evolution equation as that for the dipole gluon helicity distribution. The longitudinal double-spin asymmetry for inclusive dijet production in the longitudinally polarized electron-proton collisions can thus test the small-$x$ helicity evolution equations and facilitate constraining the initial conditions for phenomenology based on these equations.

♻ ☆ Relic density and astrophysical signatures of MeV scale bound state dark matter
Pa. Gokhula Prasad, V. Suryanarayana Mummidi
We study a strongly interacting complex scalar dark matter candidate, $χ$, interacting through an attractive potential mediated by a dark radiation $Φ$. Such interactions allow $χ$ to form bound states: SIMPonium. We systematically investigate the bound-state dynamics of this dark sector, including the formation and decay of SIMPonium and its impact on the thermal evolution of dark matter. We performed Monte Carlo simulations to compute the relic abundances of both free and bound state dark matter. We find that a successful freeze out of the dark sector requires a free dark matter yield of $Y_χ\sim 10^{-9}$ and SIMPonium yield of $Y_B \sim 10^{-13}$. The constraints from $ΔN_{\rm eff}$ reveal that only scalar mediated self interactions remain viable. For Higgs portal models, these constraints require the dark matter mass to satisfy $m_χ< 25~\mathrm{MeV}$. Within this mass range, indirect detection constraints imply that, for $g_χ> 10^{-2}$, the allowed range of the Higgs portal coupling is approximately $10^{-4} \lesssim λ\lesssim 10^{-2}$. For $g_χ< 10^{-2}$, the constraints are satisfied for a broader range, $10^{-4} \lesssim λ\lesssim 1$.

♻ ☆ How to Identify a Majoron: Effective Field Theories of Spontaneous Lepton Number Breaking
Carla Biggio, Marta Fuentes Zamoro, Xu Li, Luca Merlo, Luca Ottonello
We revisit the traditional type~I, II, and III seesaw mechanisms in the presence of a complex scalar field charged under a global $U(1)$ symmetry that can be identified with lepton number and the Peccei-Quinn symmetry. After symmetry breaking, the radial mode becomes heavy while the angular mode appears as an axionlike particle, traditionally dubbed the Majoron. We construct the effective field theory obtained after integrating out the heavy states and analyze two matching orders: first removing the radial mode and then the seesaw fields, and vice versa. Both procedures yield the same low-energy Lagrangian containing only Standard Model fields and the Majoron. Because a single vacuum expectation value fixes the mediator masses, the radial mode, and every Majoron coupling, these models predict relations among observables rather than their individual size, and it is these relations that are testable. Indeed, the invisible Higgs width is locked to the universal suppression of the Higgs couplings, while the Majoron-lepton coupling is fixed by the measured nonunitarity of the leptonic mixing matrix, and the two independently give comparable lower bounds on the same lepton-number-breaking scale, of the order of $1$--$10$~TeV. Neutrinoless double beta decay with Majoron emission, by contrast, has no sensitivity in this class of models. The framework is, thus, falsifiable even when the new states lie far beyond experimental reach.
comment: 67 pages, 2 figures. Version Published on PRD
♻ ☆ Axion-driven spontaneous leptogenesis, precisely
Konstantin Kuckenberg, Martin A. Mojahed, Kai Schmitz, Hidenaga Watanabe
We revisit a minimal scenario for spontaneous leptogenesis where the asymmetry generation is driven by a heavy axion-like field evolving via standard misalignment. We focus on the simplest framework in which lepton number violation originates from the dimension-five Weinberg operator and contributions from standard thermal leptogenesis become negligible. The asymmetry is computed by solving a set of transport equations, which incorporate fully flavor-dependent interaction rates for the Weinberg operator that are presented here for the first time. We also derive a simple algebraic master formula for the generated $B\!-\!L$ asymmetry, valid for arbitrary axion velocities and classically shift-symmetric couplings to the Standard Model, that reproduces the $B\!-\!L$-production dynamics of the full set of transport equations in controlled parameter regions. Along the way, we quantify the importance of low-scale neutrino masses and the two mass orderings on the final prediction for the generated asymmetry. Finally, we assess the cosmological viability of different axion couplings by accounting for entropy dilution from late-time axion decays and imposing constraints from baryonic isocurvature perturbations. We demonstrate that explaining the baryon asymmetry via standard Majoron misalignment is under severe tension due to dilution from late-time decays. In contrast, axions coupled to strong or weak sphalerons can successfully produce the observed asymmetry for decay constants near the energy scale of grand unification and axion oscillation temperatures $T_{\text{osc}} \gtrsim 10^{11\cdots12}$ GeV, provided a cosmological history featuring high-scale inflation and efficient reheating.

♻ ☆ Quasi-linear theory of fast flavor instabilities in homogeneous environments
Damiano F. G. Fiorillo, Georg G. Raffelt
Dense neutrino plasmas can develop instabilities that drive collisionless flavor exchange, equivalent to the emission of flavomons, the quanta of flavor waves. We treat these waves, for the first time, as independent linear degrees of freedom and develop a quasi-linear theory (QLT), including backreaction on the neutrino distribution and nonresonant neutrino--flavomon interactions, while neglecting wave--wave processes. In a homogeneous, axisymmetric model, the saturated neutrino and flavomon distributions agree closely with periodic-box solutions of the original quantum kinetic equation. These results support the use of QLT, well established in plasma physics, to bypass nonlinear small-scale effects that challenge direct simulations.

♻ ☆ Detectable Dark Matter Freeze-in via Low Reheating
Sadayappan Alagappan
This work focuses on freeze-in production of dark matter (DM) during low reheating, where the latter arises from the decay of inflatons leading to a non-adiabatic matter-dominated era. Under freeze-in, DM comoving yield is inversely proportional to Hubble, and during matter domination, as Hubble increases, the coupling, keeping the DM interaction with SM, should be enhanced to have relic density $Ω_{DM}\simeq0.12$, making DM potentially vulnerable to direct detection searches. A renormalizable Yukawa-like Lagrangian is considered for DM interaction with a singlet electron $e$, and a BSM parent particle $P$. With the decay being the dominant freeze-in production channel, the required coupling enhancement is calculated with the aid of freeze-in Boltzmann equation. Dealing with freeze-in, the higher coupling could thermalize the feebly interacting particles, and this places an upper bound on coupling. The coupling has been found to be sensitive to the vacuum energy of the inflaton during the inflationary phase. Keeping this vacuum energy at the upper bound from {\tt planck}, the model fails to feature any detectable direct detection signals even at a reheating temperature of BBN. The findings of this thesis then show that, only under low reheating and low inflationary vacuum energy, the DM-electron cross sections become high enough to be detectable in near-future direct detection searches. However, the proposed model becomes non-perturbative near the direct detection exclusion limits.

♻ ☆ The origin of Bjorken-$x$ dependence in DIS: a case for a $z$-dependent correlator in the CGC
Benjamin Guiot
We discuss an inconsistency of the eikonal Color Glass Condensate (CGC) description of Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS). In this framework, the Bjorken-$x$ dependence enters the cross section solely through the rapidity cutoff $Λ=x_b$, leading to an all-order cross section independent of $x_b$. To address this issue, we explore a natural modification in which the CGC correlators depend explicitly on the light-cone momentum fraction $z$, with integration limits determined by $x_b$. This modification is consistent with the physical expectation that the observed non-perturbative structure depends on the probe energy. Our analysis implies that the (small-)$x_b$ variation of the cross section is not solely driven by small-$x$ evolution equations. We support this conclusion through an analysis of existing DIS fits and by demonstrating that a similarly good description of the data can be obtained within the modified framework. Finally, we show that the modified formulation is compatible with $k_t$-factorization, unlike the standard one.
comment: The central claim, that the all-order eikonal CGC cross section is independent of $x_b$ because $x_b$ enters only through the rapidity factorization scale, is incorrect: the lower limit of the projectile's longitudinal phase space, fixed by its kinematics, carries an $x_b$ dependence that survives the cancellation of the factorization scale
♻ ☆ Spin-hydrodynamics in graphene and thermovortical magnetization
Amaresh Jaiswal
We examine the framework of relativistic spin hydrodynamics in the context of the Dirac quasiparticle fluid in graphene. We develop a spin-hydrodynamic model for a (2+1)-dimensional system of fermions under the condition of small spin polarization. Our analysis confirms that thermal vorticity, which satisfies the global equilibrium condition, is also a solution to the spin-hydrodynamic equations. Additionally, we calculate the magnetization of the system in global equilibrium and introduce a novel phenomenon - thermovortical magnetization - resulting from thermal vorticity, which can be experimentally observed in graphene.

♻ ☆ Higher excited charmed and charmed-strange mesons in an unquenched quark model
Ru-Hui Ni, Jia-Jun Wu, Xian-Hui Zhong
In this paper, as a continuation of our previous work on the low-lying heavy-light meson spectra, we systematically study the mass spectra and Okubo-Zweig-Iizuka-allowed strong decays of the higher $3S$-, $2P$-, $2D$-, and $1F$-wave charmed and charmed-strange mesons within a unified unquenched quark model. It is found that coupled-channel effects induce sizable state dependent mass shifts, which modify the relative level spacings and lower the predicted masses compared with conventional quenched calculations. The newly observed $D_{s1}(2933)^+$ reported by the LHCb collaboration could be identified as the low mass axial vector state $D_s(2P_1)$ via the $2^1P_1-2^3P_1$ mixing. For the broad structure $D_{sJ}(3040)^+$ observed earlier by the \emph{BABAR} collaboration, the $D_s(3^1S_0)$ assignment seems to be favored over the high mass mixed state $D_s(2P_1^\prime)$. Meanwhile, the $D(3000)^0$ signals reported by LHCb cannot be consistently explained by any of the considered $3S$, $2P$, $2D$, or $1F$ assignments. Our predicted masses and decay properties of the missing higher $D$ and $D_s$ mesons may provide useful information for future experimental searches.

♻ ☆ Diffusion and shear viscosity coefficients of hot isospin asymmetric strange hadronic matter using a chiral SU(3) model
Amruta Mishra, Shujun Zhao, Tetsufumi Hirano
We study the diffusion and shear viscosity coefficients of hot isospin asymmetric strange hadronic matter. The effects due to the baryon density, isospin, strangeness, and temperature on the nucleons and hyperons are studied within a chiral SU(3) model. The medium modifications of the baryons arise due to interactions with the mean scalar and vector fields within the model. The thermodynamic and transport properties are studied in the hot strange hadronic matter. The diffusion matrix associated with the multiple charges (baryon number, isospin, and strangeness), as well as the coefficient of shear viscosity, are computed from the Boltzmann equation using first-order Chapman--Enskog expansion within the relaxation time approximation. The diffusion coefficient, $κ_{QQ}$ corresponding to the conserved electric charge has also been studied in the present work. There are observed to be significant effects from the isospin asymmetry as well as the strangeness of the medium on the diffusion coefficients. The coefficient of shear viscosity, $η$ is observed to have a large enhancement in the presence of finite strangeness in the medium due to additional contributions from the hyperons. The effects due to isospin asymmetry on the shear viscosity coefficient is however observed to be marginal both in nuclear and hyperonic matter. The present study can be relevant for the experimental observables of asymmetric relativistic heavy-ion collisions, e.g., in the compressed baryonic matter (CBM) experiment at the FAIR facility at GSI as well as in the future J-PARC-HI program.

♻ ☆ Exploring charmonia $η_c(6S,7S)$ in the $Λ_c^+\barΛ_c^-$ invariant mass spectrum of $B^0 \to K_S^0Λ_c^+\barΛ_c^-$
Cheng-Xi Liu, Jun-Zhang Wang, Xiang Liu
We analyze the $B^0 \to K_S^0 Λ_c^+ \barΛ_c^-$ decay recently observed by the LHCb Collaboration. The $Λ_c^+\barΛ_c^-$ invariant-mass spectrum exhibits an accumulation near 4.63~GeV, which we investigate together with the accompanying $Λ_c^+ K_S^0$ spectrum constrained by the known $Ξ_c(2923)$ and $Ξ_c(2939)$ states. Our amplitude model includes a nonresonant term, the two established $Ξ_c$ contributions, and high-lying charmonium states in the $Λ_c^+\barΛ_c^-$ channel. Guided by screened Godfrey--Isgur and quark-pair-creation calculations, we test the 4.63~GeV enhancement with a fixed $η_c(6S)$ amplitude at $(4629.00, 24.20)$~MeV, {which improves the description of the 4.63~GeV region}, and examine a fixed $η_c(7S)$ contribution at $(4718.84, 22.84)$~MeV, which improves the higher-mass region of the spectrum. We also evaluate the $η_c(nS) \to Λ_c^+ \barΛ_c^-$ baryonic decays via a hadron-loop mechanism and estimate the $B^0 \to K_S^0 η_c(nS)$ production in naive factorization. Within the narrow width approximation, the fit yields a $\mathcal B(B^0\to K_S^0η_c(6S)) \mathcal B(η_c(6S)\toΛ_c^+\barΛ_c^-)$ of about $6.2 \times 10^{-6}$, while the factorization and hadron-loop calculations give rates roughly one to three orders of magnitude lower than the above fitted ratio. These results highlight the need for more precise data and a full amplitude analysis to determine the line shapes and clarify the nature of the higher-mass contribution.

☆ Matrix representations of ${\rm BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations and related long-range spin chains
M. Matushko, A. Mostovskii, A. Zotov
We construct a matrix representation of the algebra defined by the associative Yang--Baxter equations of ${\rm BC}_n$ type. In the elliptic case, two sets of generators are represented in terms of the Baxter--Belavin quantum $R$-matrix in the fundamental representation of ${\rm GL}_N$, while the remaining generators are represented by the elliptic $K$-matrix found by Komori and Hikami. We revisit its derivation using the Felder--Pasquier procedure and correct the unitarity relation for odd $N$. We then use these matrix representations to construct examples of long-range quantum spin chains from $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for the classical Calogero--Inozemtsev system associated with the ${\rm BC}_n$ root system. We also construct $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for Calogero--Moser models in an external field, leading to Haldane--Shastry and Polychronakos--Frahm chains with modified spin positions.

☆ Holographic entropy inequalities & typical states
Guglielmo Grimaldi, Matthew Headrick
As a consequence of the Ryu-Takayanagi formula, static semiclassical states in AdS quantum gravity share a set of special properties expressible as linear inequalities on their entanglement entropies. How general are these properties? Do they still hold when we move away from the regime of validity of RT, i.e. static states in classical Einstein gravity? Do they perhaps hold even for some class of non-holographic states? We will motivate these questions and review what's known about the answers.

☆ Exact Stress Tensor Flows in Causal Electrodynamics: Courant-Hilbert Approach
Zahra Pezhman, Komeil Babaei Velni, H. Babaei-Aghbolagh
It has been shown that for theories whose Courant-Hilbert function depends on a single dimensionful coupling, the energy-momentum tensor is controlled by the two combinations $τ\dot{\ell}$ and $\ell-τ\dot{\ell}$, so that the quadratic invariants $X=T_{μν}T^{μν}$ and $Y=(T^μ_μ)^2$ depend on a single auxiliary variable. Eliminating this variable in favour of $Y/X$ yields the exact autonomous flow $\partial_λ\mathcal L=X\,\mathcal F(Y/X)$, with no explicit dependence on the coupling, the electromagnetic invariants or the CH parameter, on every branch where the map is invertible. The expansion of $\mathcal F$ in powers of $\sqrt{Y/X}$ shows which flows are built from integer powers of $X$ and $Y$ and which require half-integer powers. In this paper, we work out four examples in closed form, each with its analytic structure and physical interpretation: the generalized Born-Infeld theory, whose flow is quadratic in the stress tensor; the $q$-deformed family, in which the odd coefficients of the expansion vanish at $q=1/2$ and are nonzero otherwise; the no-$τ$-maximum theory; and the causal Russo-Townsend logarithmic theory, whose flow involves the lower real branch of the Lambert $W$ function and reproduces the known perturbative result. The singular points of $\mathcal{F}$ are related to the critical fields, energy conditions, and strong-field behavior of each theory.
comment: 30 pages
☆ Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
Prosenjit Paul, Rickmoy Samanta
We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordström (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics. It provides an exact solution of Einstein gravity and admits a finite completion. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. In this setup, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Padé approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.

☆ Fixed Points of the Yang-Mills Gradient Flow in the Vortex Sector
A. M. Silva
We study the Yang-Mills gradient flow of center vortices in SU(2) gauge theory. For axially symmetric vortices the flow reduces exactly to a linear diffusion equation for the radial profile: a Gaussian core keeps its shape while its width grows as $\sqrt{R^2+4t}$, the flux is exactly conserved, and the thin vortex is the unique bounded fixed point, though not an attractor. Off-diagonal perturbations are governed by a pair of radial Schrödinger operators, and a variational computation shows that, frozen at any instant, the Abelian core has a tachyonic mode for every winding $n\geq 1$. Since the core spreads while the mode grows, we pass to self-similar variables, where the unstable modes are known in closed form, with growth exponents $μ_{n,m}=n-1+m$. Multiply wound vortices are therefore unstable, while the fundamental vortex is exactly marginal and stays Abelian. A scaling argument rules out any static vortex in the transverse plane, and the instability acquires a simple geometric meaning that shortens the path traced in SU(2) by the holonomy of a growing loop, lowering the winding by two. The flow thus drives every vortex toward the Abelian core of winding $n \bmod 2$, with non-Abelian structure appearing only as the transient through which multiply wound cores unwind.
☆ Induced Bell-CHSH observables in the Fewster-Verch measurement scheme
M. S. Guimaraes, I. Roditi, S. P. Sorella
The Summers-Werner theorem shows that the vacuum of a relativistic quantum field theory violates the Bell-CHSH inequality maximally on complementary wedges, but it is an existence statement: it exhibits neither the observables nor an apparatus that measures them. We give an explicit operator-level realization within the Fewster-Verch measurement framework, obtaining dichotomic Bell observables of a free Majorana field in $1+1$ dimensions as observables induced by local couplings to Majorana probes. The induced system smearing factorizes exactly as $f_h=k\,b_{λ,h}$, so its support is controlled by the compactly supported coupling profile $k$; dichotomy is imposed by calibrating and normalizing the induced smearings rather than required of the probe observable; and a probe-only normal ordering yields the product of Alice's and Bob's induced bilinears, which the non-multiplicative induced map alone does not provide. Under explicit attainability hypotheses the induced observables saturate the Tsirelson bound in a state prepared from the vacuum. The construction extends to coupled scalar fields.

☆ Berends-Giele currents for higher derivative gauge theories
Pratik Chattopadhyay
We derive Berends-Giele (BG) currents for higher derivative scalar QED (HDQED) and Yang-Mills (HDYM). In HDQED, we first compute the propagators and the vertices from the higher derivative Lagrangian and discuss the pole structures of the photon and the scalar. We then compute the BG currents using the Feynman diagram setup and prove the Ward identities for these currents at two and three points. Next, we used the perturbiner formalism to re-compute these currents and show that they are consistent with the Feynman diagram approach. In a similar fashion, we derive the BG currents in higher derivative Yang-Mills and find that remarkably, these currents are equal to pure Yang-Mills currents when all external on-shell legs are massless gluons. We prove this in all generality using the BG recursion and explicitly show this at lower points. However, the genuine higher derivative structure enters when one or many on-shell states are the so called massive Merlin modes. Using the multi-particle currents, we reproduce the result that all tree level amplitudes with one Merlin particle vanishes and the three and four Merlin amplitudes match the previously computed result. The future prospects of BG recursion for higher derivative gravity and off-shell colour- kinematics duality is also discussed.

☆ Krylov geometry and optimal recovery under uncertain coherent noise
Abhishek Chowdhury
Recovery from a coherent rotation with an unobserved angle depends on both the encoding and what calibration reveals about the noise. We determine their combined limit for a known finite-dimensional generator and one final recovery. Two polynomial projections organize the answer. A physical Krylov chain separates correctable error amplitudes from their first state-dependent distortion; projection onto lower-angle powers identifies the part that a coherent decoder can cancel. Under explicit rank and moment conditions, their combination gives the exact leading optimal entanglement infidelity at weak noise and a recovery attaining it for any finite logical dimension. The optimal worst-input error lies between one and $d$ times that infidelity at leading order, for logical dimension $d$. When the angle distribution is unknown, we optimize one decoder for every distribution compatible with the calibration. When spectral and calibration frequencies are integer multiples of a common frequency, moment positivity turns this into an exact finite optimization. Small measured means can still allow rare finite rotations. If the sole calibration datum is $β_r=\mathbb E[\sin^{2r}(θ/2)]$, with $θ$ the wrapped rotation phase at that common frequency, the optimal worst-prior infidelity is $O(β_r)$ exactly when generator powers through degree $r-1$ are correctable.
