♻ ☆ The growth of $SO(9)$ super-representations in Type II string theory
Alessandro Georgoudis, Joseph A. Minahan, Gustav Ström, Athanasios Zoumis
We study the growth of massive $SO(9)$ super-representations in type II and type I string theories. We do this first directly by finding an empirical formula that specifies which representations appear at any level, and then compute the multiplicities from a refined partition function evaluated over finite fields up to level 501 for individual representations, and level 226 for all representations. We then derive asymptotic formulae for the growth of any representation, which are constructed by integrating about the peaks of the refined partition function. Using a Rademacher sum we can find very accurate approximations for the multiplicities of the representations. Unlike the superstring partition function, which only receives contributions from the odd Rademacher terms, the multiplicities for any representation have contributions from both even and odd terms. Finally, we apply the same techniques to the ordinary representations, where a simplified refined partition function allows for better computational speed and simpler expressions for the asymptotic approximations.
comment: 50 pages, 15 figures, 17 tables; v2: References added, minor changes
♻ ☆ On the nature of the black hole information problem
Thiago T. Bergamaschi
The aim of this work is to present the black hole information problem and discuss the assumptions and hypotheses necessary for its formulation. As the problem arises in the framework of semiclassical gravity, we first review the necessary notions to describe Lorentzian manifolds equipped with physical properties, as well as the physical concepts of the theory that describes the gravitational interaction as the curvature of spacetime, general relativity. From its classical perspective, we develop the formalism to study the dynamical aspects of black holes in spacetimes obeying suitable causality conditions. Equipped with conjectures that nature censors naked singularities and that black holes reach a stationary configuration after they form, the black hole uniqueness theorems allow us to review several relations for the geometrical quantities associated with them. Following considerations of the other fundamental interactions, which are described by quantum field theory, we review the arguments in the formalism of quantum field theory in curved spacetime that give rise to the effective particle creation effect, its approximately thermal character, and the concept of black hole evaporation. With a precise quantification of information in quantum mechanics and assuming that the condition for physically acceptable states is given by the Hadamard condition, we review the result that entanglement between causally complementary regions is an intrinsic feature of quantum field theory. As a consequence, we discuss how the formation and complete evaporation of black holes leads to information loss. Conscious that such a prediction follows if no deviations from the semiclassical picture occur at the Planck scale, we discuss alternatives to this nonunitary dynamical evolution and formulate the black hole information problem. Lastly, we analyze the assumptions and hypotheses that lead to the problem.
comment: MSc dissertation defended at University of Sao Paulo (Brazil) on May 7th 2024. Minor typos corrected
♻ ☆ Bulk Phase Shift and Singularity
Yueke Jia, Manuela Kulaxizi
High-energy scattering of a light particle off a black hole at fixed impact parameter is described by an eikonal phase, which encodes the resulting time delay and angular deflection. This bulk phase shift admits a holographic interpretation as of the thermal momentum-space two-point function of a scalar operator in the CFT in the Regge limit. At small impact parameter, the phase shift acquires an imaginary part signaling inelastic scattering, obscuring the interpretation of time delay and deflection which become complex-valued. However, in a holographic CFT these quantities can also be extracted from the so called bulk-cone singularities of the position space thermal correlator. Extending this analysis to small impact parameters, we find that the position-space correlator develops a singularity precisely when a null geodesic reflects off the black hole singularity and reaches the opposite boundary. This provides a more robust identification of bulk time delay and angular deflection through singularities of position-space correlators.
comment: 92 pp. References added, typos corrected, 10 figures. Extended section 3 on CFT and the Regge limit, and expanded argumentation in Appendix B. Several new appendices: A. WKB analysis, C. Alternative derivation of the position space correlator, D & E. CFT details and Regge parametrisations, H. Absence of singularity in the leading order phase shift, I. Numerical checks in d=4
♻ ☆ Towards differential expansion for generic representations
Ya. Kononov, A. Morozov
We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $δ^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{δ+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,Δ}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $Δ(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $δ+1={\rm deg}\,Δ$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.
comment: 13 pages
♻ ☆ Casimir multiplets suffice: strong generation in $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ SYM
Yifan He
The Schur sector of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang$--$Mills theory contains infinitely many protected operators, while the invariant polynomials of a single adjoint scalar are organized by finitely many Casimir degrees. I prove that the small $\mathcal N=4$ short multiplets built from these invariants strongly generate the associated chiral algebra, thereby establishing the $SU(N)$ case of the strong-generation conjecture of Beem et al. For every $N\ge2$, all field components associated with degrees $2,\ldots,N$ suffice, in every conformal weight and every degree of the standard relative quantum BRST cohomology. The proof brings together cyclic trace cohomology, quantum lifting, and an arbitrary-degree quartic$--$odd transport identity. Exact field relations and a finite-rank Newton obstruction exclude every additional lowest space, including non-scalar flavor representations; the required normal-ordering corrections and BRST primitives are derived explicitly. The resulting completeness theorem explains how a finite family of supersymmetric multiplets organizes an unbounded quantum spectrum. Every Schur class is a normal polynomial in their components and derivatives, even when its gauge-theory representative involves fermions and arbitrarily many derivatives. This supplies a uniform set of local inputs for meromorphic operator products, bounds protected state multiplicities before cancellations in an index, and gives an algebraic account of the finite-rank reorganization of protected trace operators.
♻ ☆ A local second law for black hole dynamics in the charged large $D$ membrane paradigm
Supratim Halder, Mangesh Mandlik
The large $D$ membrane paradigm provides a perturbative, non-gravitational description of black hole dynamics. While the local second law of thermodynamics has been established for neutral membranes, the explicit determination of the local entropy production in the charged large $D$ membrane paradigm remains an open problem. In this paper, we compute the subleading-order correction to the divergence of the membrane velocity for a charged black hole in a flat background. Using the non-affine null Raychaudhuri equation and the Einstein-Maxwell equation at the physical event horizon, we relate the horizon expansion to the auxiliary membrane kinematics. We demonstrate that the membrane velocity produces a non-negative divergence at the first non-vanishing order in the membrane worldvolume, which is driven by two quadratic forms: the membrane shear and an additional term arising from the Maxwell field. Using this result, we subsequently construct the corresponding membrane entropy current and establish the non-negativity of its divergence through this order, thereby establishing the local second law for the charged large $D$ membrane paradigm.
comment: 20 pages
♻ ☆ Impact of a third body on binary neutron star tidal interactions
Meet Khatri, Ankur Renduchintala, Sayak Datta, Sajal Mukherjee
To model a compact binary coalescence, it is commonly assumed that the binary evolves in isolation. In the present work, we relax this assumption by introducing a distant third body and investigate how the third body would affect the binary evolution. We treat this problem perturbatively and study tidal interaction in the binary due to the third body's presence. We introduce appropriate modifications to the equations governing the orbital motions and the evolution equations of the binary component's quadrupole moment. We compute the radiated energy and accumulated dephasing for the binary. Our findings indicate that for extreme-mass-ratio inspirals, these effects would not be significant. However, for binaries such as intermediate-mass-ratio inspirals, these effects are more relevant, and in some scenarios the accumulated dephasing can reach up to $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radians.
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures
♻ ☆ Plabic promotions beyond cluster: quantum cluster structures and the dual canonical basis
Jian-Rong Li, Michael Oren Perlstein, Ran J. Tessler
Plabic tangles define geometric promotion maps between configurations and, after choosing a lift, between Grassmannians. The main conjecture in \cite{Tangles} is that when the tangle is dominant and solvable the induced algebraic promotion is cluster quasi-homomorphism. This work extends the cluster perspective in two directions. First, we initiate the study of quantum promotions. We conjecture that all promotions defined from dominant solvable tangles are naturally lifted to a \emph{quantum cluster quasi homomorphism}, and prove for all cases in the literature that the were shown to be (classical) cluster quasi-homomorphisms. Secondly, we define the notion of cluster-Lusztig quasi-homomorphisms, which are cluster quasi homomorphisms that take Lustig's dual canonical basis elements to dual canonical basis element, up to a Laurent monomial in frozen variables, with clearing and normalization chosen uniformly on each content component. We prove the unexpected result that the classical and quantum $m$-unary star promotions fall into this category, and conjecture that all promotions coming from dominant solvable tangles share the same property. We then consider promotions via non solvable cores of intersection number higher than one. We use it to study facets of amplituhedron cells, and to show that some of them do not lie in zero loci of dual canonical basis elements, disproving a conjecture by T. Lam \cite{LamGP}.
comment: 101 pages; Supplementary computational data previously included in the v1 TeX source have been reorganized as ancillary files
♻ ☆ Anyonic membranes and Pontryagin statistics
Yitao Feng, Hanyu Xue, Yuyang Li, Meng Cheng, Ryohei Kobayashi, Po-Shen Hsin, Yu-An Chen
Anyons, unique to two spatial dimensions, underlie extraordinary phenomena such as the fractional quantum Hall effect, but their generalization to higher dimensions has remained elusive. The topology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces constrains the loop statistics to be only bosonic or fermionic in any dimension. In this work, we introduce the novel anyonic statistics for membrane excitations in four dimensions. Analogous to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-particle exhibiting $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(2,N)}$ anyonic statistics in two dimensions, we show that the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-membrane possesses $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(3,N)}$ anyonic statistics in four dimensions. Given unitary volume operators that create membrane excitations on the boundary, we propose an explicit 56-step unitary sequence that detects the membrane statistics. We further analyze the boundary theory of $(5{+}1)$D 1-form $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry-protected topological phases and demonstrate that their domain walls realize all possible anyonic membrane statistics. We then show that the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ subgroup persists in all higher dimensions. In addition to the standard fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2$ membrane statistics arising from Stiefel-Whitney classes, membranes also exhibit $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics associated with Pontryagin classes. We explicitly verify that the 56-step process detects the nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics in 5, 6, and 7 spatial dimensions. Moreover, in 7 and higher dimensions, the statistics of membrane excitations stabilize to $\mathbb{Z}_{2} \times \mathbb{Z}_{3}$, with the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ sector consistently captured by this process.

♻ ☆ Spin-hydrodynamics in graphene and thermovortical magnetization
Amaresh Jaiswal
We examine the framework of relativistic spin hydrodynamics in the context of the Dirac quasiparticle fluid in graphene. We develop a spin-hydrodynamic model for a (2+1)-dimensional system of fermions under the condition of small spin polarization. Our analysis confirms that thermal vorticity, which satisfies the global equilibrium condition, is also a solution to the spin-hydrodynamic equations. Additionally, we calculate the magnetization of the system in global equilibrium and introduce a novel phenomenon - thermovortical magnetization - resulting from thermal vorticity, which can be experimentally observed in graphene.
comment: 18 pages, 1 figure, published version
♻ ☆ Black holes in thermal bath live shorter: Implications for primordial black holes
Jitumani Kalita, Debaprasad Maity, Ayan Chatterjee
Hawking radiation from a non-extremal black hole is known to be approximately Planckian. The thermal spectrum receives multiple corrections including greybody factors and due to kinematical restrictions on the infrared and ultraviolet frequencies. We show that another significant correction to the spectrum arises if the black hole is assumed to live in a thermal bath and the emitted radiation gets thermalised at the bath temperature. This modification reshapes the thermal spectrum, and leads to appreciable deviation from standard results including modification in the decay rate of black holes. We argue that this altered decay rate has significance for cosmology and, in a realistic setting, show that it alters the life time of primordial black holes (PBHs) in the early universe. In particular, the very light PBHs formed right after the end of inflation decay faster which may have interesting phenomenological implications.
comment: Published in Physics Letters B, 6 pages, 2 figures
♻ ☆ Holographic Timelike c-function
Dimitrios Giataganas
The integration of high-energy degrees of freedom along the renormalization group (RG) flow in Poincaré-invariant theories is captured by a monotonic c-function. For such theories, holographic c-functions have been constructed using entanglement entropy. However, in theories with broken Lorentz invariance, these constructions generally fail, reflecting both the violation of entanglement RG monotonicity and its limitations in capturing essential features of nonrelativistic RG flows. Since many quantum many-body systems lack Lorentz invariance, it is important to identify a quantity that captures the decrease of effective degrees of freedom along such flows. We show that the recently introduced holographic timelike entanglement entropy naturally gives rise to a new c-function applicable to all such theories, which moreover obeys a geometric upper bound on its rate of change. We further demonstrate the existence of this c-function in theories with Lifshitz and hyperscaling-violating fixed points, showing that, provided the null energy condition, thermodynamic stability and explicit geometric conditions on the flow are satisfied, it obeys the expected RG monotonicity.
comment: v3: 9 pages, double-column format; minor improvements
♻ ☆ Timelike Entanglement Entropy and Renormalization Group Flow Irreversibility
Dimitrios Giataganas
We study holographic $c$-theorems based on timelike entanglement entropy and show that timelike $c$-functions capture irreversible renormalization group (RG) flow. We demonstrate that timelike $c$-functions are applicable to both relativistic and nonrelativistic quantum matter in nematic phases with broken rotational symmetry, and that they remain monotonic along holographic anisotropic RG flows under explicit geometric conditions, thereby passing some of the most stringent consistency tests. We derive the exact flow of the composite timelike $c$-function in general homogeneous anisotropic geometries and establish the $c$-theorem for adiabatic flows. Across all classes of scaling backgrounds examined, consistent with the null energy condition and thermodynamic stability, the monotonicity condition universally reduces to a constraint on a running geometric effective dimension. We further construct a second $c$-function purely from the imaginary part of the timelike entanglement entropy and prove its monotonicity under the local effective-dimension condition, without requiring adiabaticity. For Poincaré-invariant flows, this condition follows directly from the null energy condition. Moreover, we identify a geometric upper bound on the rate of change of the timelike $c$-functions, which constrains how rapidly effective degrees of freedom can be coarse-grained. Our results suggest that capturing RG irreversibility in nonrelativistic flows requires observables that are intrinsically sensitive to the temporal direction. The applicability of holographic $c$-theorems is thus extended to highly nontrivial RG flows and points toward a new information-theoretic diagnostic of holographic RG dynamics.
comment: 57+1 pages
♻ ☆ Black hole thermodynamics and KK photon quantum corrections in 2D effective dilaton gravity
Yoshihiko Abe, Tetsutaro Higaki, Yu Miyauchi
We study black hole thermodynamics using a two-dimensional effective theory obtained by dimensional reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory. For spherically symmetric charged black holes, the resulting dilaton gravity has a nonlinear potential that reproduces the semiclassical phase structure of four-dimensional AdS black holes, including the Hawking--Page transition and the small/large Reissner--Nordström--AdS black hole transition. This shows that the two-dimensional theory before taking the near-horizon and near-extremal limits captures non-extremal thermodynamics beyond the Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity regime. We also include electromagnetic Kaluza--Klein modes on the internal sphere and integrate them out to derive the one-loop effective dilaton gravity. At leading order in the derivative expansion, these corrections appear as constant shifts in the black hole entropy and in the effective charge parameter of the dilaton potential. Therefore, the semiclassical phase structure is not qualitatively modified within this leading local approximation.

Materials Science [18]
☆ Hidden Fisher Information in Many-Body Quantum Sensors
Atta ur Rahman, Muhammad Noman, Samira Elghaayda, Saeed Haddadi
Quantum Fisher information (QFI) determines the ultimate precision of a quantum sensor after optimization over all allowed measurements, but it does not quantify how difficult the optimal readout is to implement. We introduce a moment Fisher hierarchy $F_M^{(k)}$, which measures the fraction of QFI accessible to collective spin moments up to degree $k$, together with a readout-complexity scale $k_{90}$ defined by the minimum degree required to recover $90\%$ of the QFI. Applying this framework to a nonlinear collective-spin sensor, we show that many-body dynamics can preserve large QFI while transferring the optimal readout into high-rank $SU(2)$ tensor sectors inaccessible to low-order collective observables. For system sizes up to $N=100$, first moments access only $\sim 10^{-2}$ of the available QFI, while the degree required to recover $90\%$ of it grows to $k_{90}\simeq 28$. A rank-resolved analysis of the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) under weak damping shows that the nonlinear protocol pushes the optimal readout toward the highest available tensor ranks while strongly depleting its low-rank weight. These results identify nonlinear tangent-space shear as the mechanism behind a finite-size readout-complexity bottleneck in many-body quantum metrology.

☆ Annealing-atmosphere control of paramagnetic defects in ZnO microparticles
D. Savchenko, M. Holiatkina, A. Prokhorov, A. Vasin, E. Kalabukhova
In this work, we used temperature-dependent electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy to reveal the effect of high-temperature annealing in N2 and air on paramagnetic and electronic properties of ZnO microparticles. EPR spectral simulations have shown that N2 annealing produces Zni, VO+, and shallow-donor centers, whereas Zni, VO+, and Hi-related centers are observed after annealing the ZnO microparticles in an air atmosphere. The resolved paramagnetic centers exhibit distinctly different behavior over 5-297 K. The shallow-donor and Hi signals are rapidly quenched below approximately 50 K, while the Zni contribution shows a nonmonotonic temperature dependence. In contrast, the VO+ signal persists up to room temperature and increases with temperature, consistent with charge redistribution among donor-related defects involving deep oxygen-vacancy states. The cavity Q-factor generally decreases with increasing temperature for both annealed samples, indicating atmosphere-dependent changes in the microwave losses. These results show that the annealing atmosphere controls the paramagnetic defect population, the temperature dependence of donor-related centers, and the associated electronic response of ZnO microparticles.
comment: 13 pages, 5 figures
☆ First-Principles-Informed Modeling of Thermal Transport and Laser-Induced Heating in Ultrahigh-Temperature Carbides
Shivanand Yadav, Shailendra Kumar Verma, Vardhman Dwivedi, Raihan Ahammed, Rohitash Kumar, Manvendra Sharma, Pritam Chakraborty, Somnath Bhowmick
Using first-principles density functional theory and Boltzmann transport calculations, we systematically investigate the electronic structure, lattice and electronic thermal transport, optical response, and laser-induced heating of ultrahigh-temperature carbides (UHTCs), including Group IV (TiC, ZrC, and HfC) and Group V carbides (VC, NbC, and TaC), and SiC. The transition-metal carbides (TMCs) exhibit metallic electronic structures, whereas SiC exhibits semiconducting character. The calculated thermal transport properties reveal distinct contributions from phonons and electrons, with electronic heat transport becoming increasingly important at elevated temperatures in TMCs. The Group V carbides exhibit substantially lower lattice thermal conductivity than their Group IV counterparts, accompanied by pronounced Kohn anomalies and modified phonon dispersions associated with their distinct electronic structures, suggesting a possible connection between Fermi-surface topology, phonon dynamics, and lattice thermal transport. In contrast, SiC exhibits comparatively high lattice thermal conductivity, consistent with its long-lived acoustic phonons, but no electronic contribution due to its semiconducting nature. Optical calculations reveal relatively high reflectivity in the visible and infrared spectral ranges for the metallic carbides, whereas SiC exhibits lower reflectivity in the infrared region. Finally, one-dimensional and three-dimensional continuum heat-conduction models are employed to compare the thermal responses of these materials under specified laser irradiation conditions. The predicted temperature distributions depend on the thermal and optical properties of the materials as well as the specimen geometry.
☆ Harnessing Electrostructural Bistability to Control Defects in Polarizable Materials
Tyler C. Sterling, Tomke E. Glier, David Abbe, Rahul Nandkishore, Dmitry Reznik
Structural defects are central to the functionalities of materials. However, conventional approaches to defect control are often slow and imprecise. This work identifies and characterizes a distinct physical phenomenon of electrostructural bistability that provides a rapid and precise pathway for engineering materials with defect-controlled physical properties. A generalized theory of conductivity bistability is developed and experimentally validated to unify two distinct regimes: previously reported electrothermal bistability in weakly polarizable insulators, such as silicon, and electrostructural bistability in strongly polarizable materials, such as TiO$_2$. In agreement with the theory, experiments on TiO$_2$ demonstrate that bulk-homogeneous defect concentrations in electrostructurally bistable materials can be tuned rapidly and deterministically by controlling applied electric current. Abruptly interrupting the current quenches the system into long-lived, room-temperature metastable states with distinct properties. This establishes a practical, rapid, and scalable pathway for defect engineering with direct relevance to nonvolatile memory devices.
☆ Aging dynamics and generalized superposition principles in carbon black-carboxymethylcellulose hydrogels
Gauthier Legrand, Guilhem P. Baeza, Jarno L. Waeterloos, Christian Clasen, Sébastien Manneville, Thibaut Divoux
Aqueous dispersions of hydrophobic carbon black (CB) particles can be stabilized by carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), forming CB-CMC hydrogels whose microstructure is controlled by the relative CB-to-polymer content. At low CMC content, CB particles form a percolated, electrically conductive network, whereas at higher polymer content, CB particles act as isolated physical crosslinkers within an electrically insulating polymer matrix [see Legrand \textit{et al.}, Macromolecules 56, 2298-2308 (2023)]. Combining rheology and electrical impedance spectroscopy, we show that these two regimes exhibit markedly different aging dynamics. Conductive hydrogels exhibit logarithmic elastic recovery associated with a percolated CB network, whereas insulating hydrogels exhibit a combination of logarithmic and power-law stiffening, accompanied by dielectric polarization associated with confined ionic motion. The insulating hydrogels further exhibit a time-aging superposition principle, as their viscoelastic spectra measured in a time-resolved fashion can collapse onto a single master curve. Under steady shear, the viscoelastic response measured perpendicular to the flow also obeys a time--shear-rate superposition principle. Remarkably, the scaling between the shift factors under shear is reminiscent of critical-gel behavior, unlike that observed during aging at rest. Finally, time-resolved rheo-USAXS measurements performed during shear-rate cycles reveal structural rearrangements of CB particles and clusters that correlate with rheological hysteresis. These results provide a microstructural basis for understanding the nonlinear rheology of insulating CB-CMC hydrogels and establish generalized superposition principles as a unifying framework for their aging and flow behavior.

☆ Effect of niobium doping on the local structure and oxidation state of Co atoms in SrTiO$_3$
A. I. Lebedev, I. A. Sluchinskaya
XAFS spectroscopy combined with first-principles calculations are used to study SrTiO$_3$ samples simultaneously doped with cobalt and niobium. It is shown that additional doping of the samples with Nb donors results in a decrease in the oxidation state of cobalt atoms to +2, which is accompanied by an increase in the Co--O distance to the nearest oxygen atoms, in agreement with first-principles calculations. The impurity Co atoms are shown to occupy Ti sites and are on-center. The suppression of the oxygen-vacancy formation upon doping SrTiO$_3$(Co) with niobium was revealed. First-principles calculations indicate that the Coulomb interaction of ions with local electric fields generated by non-isoelectronic Nb impurities plays a decisive role in the local distortions of atomic positions observed around the cobalt atom in the unit cell. The possibility of controlling the magnetic moment of Co atoms by intentional change in the lattice parameter is demonstrated.

☆ Perpendicular Anisotropy and g-Factor of Sputtered Ni Films on Si(111) Studied by Angle-Dependent Ferromagnetic Resonance
Dushyant Singh, Tharundev V, Subha Maity, Subhavenkadesh SS, Vigneshwari SR, Krista R. Khiangte
Ni films with thicknesses of 312 and 1011\,Å were grown on Si(111) by dc magnetron sputtering at room temperature and studied by atomic force microscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, X-ray reflectivity, magnetometry and angle-dependent ferromagnetic resonance. Both films are polycrystalline fcc Ni with smooth surfaces, a bulk-like (111) lattice spacing and a saturation magnetization of ${\approx}480$\,emu\,cm$^{-3}$, and both are magnetized in plane. The angular dependence of the resonance field, from the film plane to the film normal, is described by a uniaxial anisotropy model with first- and second-order terms. From this model, $g = 2.160\pm0.005$ and $2.101\pm0.014$ and effective perpendicular anisotropies of $(6.0\pm0.4)\times10^{5}$ and $(4.5\pm0.6)\times10^{5}$\,erg\,cm$^{-3}$ were obtained for the thinner and thicker film, respectively. The conventional analysis of only the in-plane and perpendicular resonances gives $g$-factors that are lower by 0.02--0.04. The perpendicular linewidths give upper limits for the Gilbert damping of $α\le 0.030$ and $\le 0.038$.
☆ Co layer Thickness Driven Structural Evolution and Magnetic Behaviour of Co/Ir/Co Trilayers
Subhavenkadesh SS, Dushyant Singh, Tharundev V, Subha Maity, Navneet Sharma, Vigneshwari SR, Krista R. Khiangte
Ferromagnetic heavy-metal (FM/HM) trilayer heterostructures provide a versatile platform for investigating the interplay between structural and magnetic properties. In this study, we investigate the effect of Co-layer thickness on the structural and magnetic properties of sputter-deposited $\mathrm{Co}(t_{\mathrm{Co}})/\mathrm{Ir}(5\,\mathrm{nm})/\mathrm{Co}(t_{\mathrm{Co}})$ varying from 2 to 10 nm. Structural characterization using grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) reveals a nanocrystalline structure, with the crystallite size increasing with Co-layer thickness. Furthermore, X-ray reflectivity (XRR) reveals a thickness-dependent variation in interface morphology, with the interface roughness ratio reaching a maximum at $t_{\mathrm{Co}} = 4$ nm. Temperature-dependent zero-field-cooled and field-cooled (ZFC-FC) magnetization measurements reveal thickness-dependent characteristic temperatures and multiple relaxation regimes in selected samples, indicating complex thermally activated magnetic behaviour. In contrast, field-dependent hysteresis measurements reveal that the saturation magnetization increases with Co-layer thickness, whereas the coercivity exhibits a pronounced non-monotonic variation, with enhanced values at intermediate thicknesses. Moreover, low-temperature hysteresis loops display thickness-dependent exchange-bias-like shifts, particularly for $t_{\mathrm{Co}} = 2$-$4$ nm. These findings highlight the strong influence of Co-layer thickness on the structural and magnetic properties of Co/Ir/Co trilayers.
☆ First-order magnetostructural transition in Ni-Mn-Sn powder - A matter of particle and grain size
Johannes Puy, David Koch, Enrico Bruder, Sagar Ghorai, Benedikt Beckmann, Heiner Gutte, Volodymyr Baran, Oliver Gutfleisch, Franziska Scheibel
In Ni-Mn-based Heusler alloys, the magnetocaloric effect originates from a first-order magnetostructural transition (FOMST). However, the influence of particle and grain size on thermal hysteresis, transition width, and nucleation and growth mechanism remains poorly understood, as mechanical grinding can introduce residual stresses and processing-induced defects. In this study, we examined the size dependence of the FOMST in gas-atomized Ni-Mn-Sn powder by combining microstructural characterization with temperature-dependent XRD, magnetometry, calorimetry and single-particle measurements, enabling decoupling of size dependence from processing-related influences. We observed a pronounced size dependence of the transition ranges (Ms-Mf) and (Af-As), which decrease with decreasing particle size and approach zero for single-crystalline particles below ~20-30 micrometer. The thermal hysteresis decreases with increasing particle size, reaching a lower limit of 17 K for large polycrystalline particles above 100 micrometer. EBSD reveals a nearly constant grain size, implying a transition from polycrystalline to single-crystalline particles as particle size decreases. In polycrystalline particles, multiple grains transform gradually over an extended temperature interval because grain boundaries act as barriers to the progression of transformation. In contrast, single-grain particles lack preferred nucleation sites, resulting in larger hysteresis, while the absence of barriers to transformation propagation causes the entire particle to transform in a narrow range. These results demonstrate that the size dependence of the FOMST is governed by the interplay between particle size, grain boundaries, and the free particle surface.
☆ Phonon-Dressed Quasiparticles in Epitaxial Scandium Nitride Resolved by Soft X-ray ARPES
Sourav Rudra, Dheemahi Rao, Meng-Jie Huang, Subhajit Manna, Renuka Karanje, Aritra Dey, Sanjoy Kr Mahatha, Samuel Poncé, Bivas Saha
Electron-phonon interactions govern quasiparticle energies, lifetimes, and temperature-dependent band structures in semiconductors. However, direct momentum-resolved experimental evidence of their impact on quasiparticle electronic structure remains scarce, particularly in nitride semiconductors. Here, we present conclusive experimental evidence of electron-phonon interaction-induced quasiparticle renormalization and pronounced spectral broadening in p-type scandium nitride (ScN), using soft x-ray angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. First-principles spectral-function calculations due to electron-phonon coupling reproduce the measured spectra, capturing a pronounced quasiparticle kink ~2.3 eV below the valence-band maximum, phonon satellite features arising from long-range electron-phonon coupling, and a direct bandgap zero-point renormalization of -124.3 meV within the non-adiabatic Allen-Heine-Cardona approach. We further show that the anomalous temperature-induced increase in the direct bandgap in ScN originates from the combined effects of thermal expansion and electron-phonon coupling, contributing comparably near room temperature. Our results establish ScN as a model platform for visualizing electron-phonon coupling and provide a quantitative benchmark for predictive first-principles descriptions of quasiparticle renormalization in semiconductors.
☆ Charge state and hydration of vacancies in silicon and silicon carbide in contact with water: A grand-canonical first-principles stability map
Abhirup Patra
The state of a vacancy in a semiconductor is normally described by the Fermi level alone. These results establish a concrete scattering benchmark for hybrid quantum computers and demonstrate how local real-time observables can probe particle-resonance dynamics.

At some simulation snapshots, the spectrum and morphology of the residuals resemble the Fermi GCE. Our results suggest that the Fermi GCE may be a manifestation of the look-elsewhere effect- a transient fluctuation in diffuse emission from stellar sources, observed at an inopportune moment- and motivate the development of new Fermi-LAT analysis templates that account for time-dependent CR transport.

By comparing baseline RFG predictions against experimental data from MicroBooNE, this research quantifies the necessity of advanced many-body nuclear frameworks. The implementation of the Local Fermi Gas (LFG) model, Random Phase Approximation (RPA) screening, and the SuperScaling Approximation (SuSAv2) are systematically analyzed to resolve kinematic biases. Additionally, the impact of modernized phenomenological constraints, including the updated $M_A^{RES} = 0.96$ GeV for resonant pion production and the 2021 Bodek-Yang parameter updates for Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS), is evaluated. Furthermore, this research integrates university extension initiatives by developing and presenting macroscopic 3D-printed educational models, consisting of a Linear Accelerator (LINAC) analog and a scattering experiment, and finally presenting it into the festival "Mais Ciência Por Favor".

Their predictions depend sensitively on the choice of horizon scale and, for weak gauge-field production, can deviate substantially from the regularized result; for the adopted finite-part prescription, the minimal horizon agrees best with the regularized total energy density. As $|γ_1|\to 2$, where infrared modes dominate, the relative deviation of all prescriptions from the regularized result vanishes, independently of the finite-part prescription. Outside this regime, the separate electric and magnetic contributions, which can become negative after regularization, are not reliably reproduced by any of the horizon-cutoff prescriptions.

We present the complete two-loop QCD amplitudes for the production of a top-quark pair in the quark--antiquark annihilation and gluon-fusion channels in analytic form up to order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2)$. Our analysis maintains full dependence on the top-quark mass and on the number of colours. The amplitudes are expressed in terms of 417 master integrals, which we compute by means of differential equations in $\varepsilon$-factorised form. Their calculation involves several elliptic curves and a hyperelliptic curve of genus two, which makes top-quark pair production an ideal arena for recent methods to construct canonical bases beyond polylogarithms. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first scattering amplitude in which iterated integrals related to a genus-two surface survive in the finite remainder in four space-time dimensions. We provide high-precision series expansions at the threshold and combine them with the numerical solution of the differential equations in a code that evaluates the UV-renormalised infrared-finite remainders at arbitrary points of the physical phase space.

☆ Higher-twist hadronic tensor in deep inelastic scattering with massive quarks
W. Yang, Y. Yang, X. Wang
In this paper, we calculate the inclusive deep inelastic scattering (DIS) with finite quark masses up to twist-4 accuracy based on collinear expansion method. The collinear expansion method not only naturally leads to gauge-invariant correlation functions and parton distribution functions, but also yields a remarkably compact expression for the hadronic tensor. The resulting hadronic tensor can be organized according to the corresponding power behavior in $1/Q$. In particular, the explicit quark-mass dependence gives rise to additional power-suppressed contributions and the ratio $m/Q$ can be counted as a twist-3 contribution in the power expansion. As an application, we further investigate the role of transversity in inclusive DIS with a transversely polarized target. We find that the transversity distribution appears explicitly in the quark-quark correlation function and gives rise to a contribution proportional to $m~h_{1T}/Q$. However, this contribution is exactly cancelled in the hadronic tensor by the one arising from the corresponding quark-gluon-quark correlation function. This cancellation shows that, within the one-photon-exchange approximation, the mass-induced transversity term cancels in the complete twist-3 hadronic tensor, and no net transversity contribution remains at twist-3 accuracy in inclusive DIS. We complement this analytical study with numerical estimates of the $g_T$-related twist-3 asymmetry, comparing predictions with and without the mass-dependent $x\rightarrowχ$ rescaling at the same measured $x$. The results show that these kinematic mass effects become more important at lower $Q^2$ and larger $x$.

Taking the two-channel case as an illustration, we benchmark this parametrization against the Lippmann--Schwinger equation (LSE) by comparing the amplitudes and their inverses at different expansion orders. Even at the lowest order, with only six parameters, the coupled-channel parametrization faithfully reproduces the LSE results and enables precise extraction of the coupling constants, demonstrating its reliability for two-body coupled-channel scattering problems involving particle exchange.

We present a coherent axion-electrodynamics extension of the OSIRIS particle-in-cell code and use it to identify and benchmark a parametric axion-photon instability supported by two equal counter-propagating electromagnetic pumps. The module evolves a cell-centered axion field together with a separately stored first-order electromagnetic response on the native staggered OSIRIS grid. Re-examining the previously proposed strictly co-linear branch shows that it is removed when the axion-Maxwell equations are reduced consistently. A closely related standing-wave geometry, however, supports a distinct Floquet instability. We derive the coupled Floquet problem for an equal-amplitude counter-propagating pump pair and obtain a reduced analytic growth rate and cutoff for the dominant long-wavelength envelope branch. For an axion mass-to-pump-frequency ratio of 0.06 and a per-beam vector-potential amplitude of 0.3, simulations at coupling strengths of 0.60, 0.80, and 1.00 reproduce both the growth-rate spectrum and the coupling-dependent instability boundary. The reduced theory predicts envelope-mode cutoffs of 8.44, 10.80, and 13.23, while OSIRIS finds exponential growth through modes 8, 10, and 13, respectively, with the next resolved modes stable. The electromagnetic diagnostics additionally resolve exponentially growing sidebands at twice the pump wavenumber, while the zero-wavenumber electric component exhibits no sustained growth, as expected for the unstable Floquet eigenvector. The agreement provides an end-to-end benchmark of the coherent axion-electromagnetic coupling and demonstrates that parametric growth of the axion field is present in a two-beam pump geometry.

In this paper, we review the impact of a strong magnetic field on the neutral two-flavor color superconducting (2SC) phase of dense quark matter. Using a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model approach in the mean-field approximation, we first solve the gap equations for the diquark condensate $Δ$ and the electric chemical potential $μ_e$ under a uniform external magnetic field, and discuss the coupled evolution of the chiral and diquark order parameters. We then evaluate the field-dependent Meissner masses of the rotationally charged gluons for a wide range of densities and moderate diquark coupling strengths. Combining the "zero-mode problem" mechanism with the neutrality condition, we show that the gluon masses become tachyonic even at moderate magnetic-field values, signaling a chromomagnetic instability in density regions where the system was stable at zero field. This instability can be resolved through the restructuring of the ground state with the formation of a gluon vortex condensate. A remarkable consequence of the vortex configuration is the paramagnetic amplification of the in-medium magnetic field: seed fields of the order of $10^{15}$ G can be enhanced by up to two orders of magnitude, reaching $\sim 10^{17}$ G, precisely the range predicted for magnetar cores. We compare this microscopic mechanism with the conventional dynamo explanation and discuss how it offers a plausible explanation for the extremely high magnetic fields expected to be realized in magnetar interiors.

Our calculation demonstrates that the $\cosφ_{kΔ}$ azimuthal harmonic of the DSA for the elastic vector meson production at small transverse momentum transfer (with $φ_{kΔ}$ the azimuthal angle between the transverse momenta of the outgoing electron and meson in the dipole/Trento frame) provides a promising probe of the orbital angular momentum (OAM) distributions at small $x$. If the electron mass has an independent origin, the two heavier-generation relations can be realized in theories with a unification scale as low as $(5$-$7)\times10^5$ GeV. We identify two simple theories that accommodate all three relations and in which the measured masses fix the flavor structure. The first unifies all three generations at $4.6^{+1.2}_{-0.9}\times10^6$ GeV; the second, with symmetric Yukawa matrices, at $1.5^{+0.7}_{-0.5}\times10^7$ GeV, and predicts $|V_{cb}|=0.042\pm0.002$. Their shared light-family texture fixes the relevant vector-leptoquark couplings, making $μ\to e$ conversion in nuclei a direct test of unification: upcoming searches will probe part of the region selected by the two theories, and proposed facilities could cover it completely.

We also extended our analysis to the NA64$μ$ experiment and showed that, together with FASER, these experiments can probe the energy dependence of the muon trident cross-section over a broad unexplored energy range.

The relativistic and Newtonian velocity distributions agree at radii far from the Galactic center but begin to differ at distances of order $10^{-5}\,\mathrm{pc}$. Closer to the black hole, the relativistic peak speed can reach approximately twice the Newtonian prediction. Finally, we derive a general expression for dark-matter capture by neutron stars that accommodates arbitrary ambient velocity distributions. Near Sagittarius A$^*$, the relativistic capture factor is nearly an order of magnitude smaller than the Maxwell-Boltzmann prediction, while the Newtonian Eddington result can overestimate it by a factor of approximately two. These results demonstrate the importance of relativistic phase-space reconstruction for dark-matter phenomenology in strong gravitational fields.

Tong Liu, Bohan Li, Gongrui Cheng, Zixiong Yu, Yulan He, Volker Tresp
Beyond math and code, Large language models (LLMs) are beginning to tackle problems that have traditionally required substantial training for theoretical physicists, but it remains unclear how far this capability extends and where it might break. As a first step toward pushing LLMs in high-energy theoretical physics, we introduce QFT-Bench, a benchmark of 75 graduate- to research-level problems requiring extensive reasoning and derivation across core Quantum Field Theory (QFT) subareas. Each question has a well-defined target and closed-form reference answer. Evaluation combines symbolic verification with LLM-based judge. Across 39 proprietary and open-source models, frontier models already demonstrate substantial capabilities on nontrivial QFT calculations, with the strongest models exceeding 95% accuracy. At the same time, clear gaps remain. Even strong models still make errors in calculations, conventions, and instruction following, while weaker models often fail at the level of physical concepts or derivations. We further monitor models' CoTs and show that current models exhibit nontrivial reasoning unfaithfulness, i.e., they could reach correct answers but the reasoning itself does not justify and logically support them. These results provide a quantitative assessment of current LLM capabilities in QFT and a first step toward broader evaluation in high-energy theoretical physics.

The correlator carries a short-distance logarithm with a branch cut at $ν=0$. By the Paley-Wiener theorem, the analytic part transforms into $|x|\le1$, so the exterior is generated solely by this branch cut. At leading power, the exterior carries no independent non-perturbative physics: it is fixed by the light-cone PDF through the renormalization group. In the gluon channel, the matching kernel of Balitsky, Morris and Radyushkin differs from our $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ result by a finite polynomial, identical across index choices. We trace this to contracting an internal loop index over two instead of $d-2$ transverse directions, omitting an evanescent operator on the collinear pole. Using our basis, we show that the independent kernel of Yao, Ji and Zhang agrees with ours, separated from Balitsky et al. by the same polynomial. While the ratio scheme protects the momentum fraction $\langle x\rangle_g$, this kernel difference suppresses the extracted normalized second and third gluon moments by $11\%$ and $13\%$ at $α_s=0.3$, so the true $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ gluon is systematically harder than reported.

We investigate the dynamical and optical properties of a higher-dimensional loop-quantum-corrected black hole in a de Sitter background. We first analyze the horizon structure and identify the admissible nonextremal black-hole domain bounded by the extremal and Nariai configurations, ensuring the existence of distinct inner, event, and cosmological horizons for the parameter sets considered. We then examine the scalar effective potential and show that the loop-quantum correction deforms the classical scattering barrier primarily in the strong-field region while preserving its characteristic single-barrier structure. The quasinormal modes of massless scalar perturbations are computed using time-domain evolution with Prony extraction, the matrix method, and the WKB approximation, showing good agreement among the three approaches. The time-domain waveform and its Prony and matrix-frequency reconstructions provide an additional direct consistency check of the extracted ringdown spectrum. We find that loop quantum corrections induce moderate shifts in the quasinormal spectrum, whereas the spacetime dimensionality has a much stronger impact, leading to higher oscillation frequencies and damping rates. The negative imaginary parts of all modes indicate dynamical stability against massless scalar perturbations within the explored parameter range. Comparison with the corresponding classical black-hole backgrounds shows that the quantum-corrected quasinormal spectrum remains continuously connected to the classical photon-sphere branch, with the loop correction producing quantitative rather than qualitative changes.

Domain walls arising from spontaneous symmetry breaking in the early universe are typically unstable and decay rapidly. Their longevity stems from a potential with two distinct vacua: an interior oscillating in one vacuum and an exterior static in the other. Within a specific parameter regime, radiation is highly suppressed and the lifetime can exceed cosmological timescales. To gain analytical insight into the mechanism, we first consider reduced models with fewer fields (2 and 4 real scalars). These are not approximations to the 2HDM but rather toy models that capture the essential feature of a Z2-symmetric potential with two vacua. Floquet analysis further confirms the stability of these structures under perturbations in both the 4-field toy model and the full 2HDM.

We first consider the idealized case of an electron in the presence of a plane wave and derive an analytical expression of the total yield in the form of a double integral over the laser phase. As it is known, the total yield is finite in the experimentally common case of a plane-wave laser field without a dc component whereas it diverges logarithmically in the complementary case of so-called unipolar fields. Interestingly, we also find that the corrections to the Volkov states stemming from the fact that the field is unipolar cancel out in the computation of the probability of nonlinear Compton scattering, which is in agreement with the fact that in the classical limit the expression of the photon yield is independent of whether the plane wave is unipolar or not. Then, we pass to the more realistic case of an electron in a tightly-focused laser beam by assuming that the electron is ultrarelativistic. In this case we determine analytically the classical angular distribution of the yield of photons with an energy larger than a fixed value $\hbarω_m$ as a double integral over the electron's trajectory. After obtaining also the corresponding quantum expression of the angular distribution of the photon yield within the quasiclassical approximation, we determine analytically the leading-order quantum correction, which scales as $\hbarω_m/\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon$ is the initial electron energy. Considerations on the experimental feasibility of the found results in the latter situations are also presented.

At low temperatures, thermally excited non-singlets backreact on the Fermi sea of matrix eigenvalues, causing it to spill over. At high temperatures, the theory is described by an effective matrix integral obtained by dimensional reduction on the thermal circle; the eigenvalue distribution of the zero mode becomes unstable at the critical coupling. We conjecture that the BKT transition occurs at a special point on the critical curve and estimate its position. Finally, we switch to the regular square lattice and study the MQM-inspired Villain model, where the link factor is the one-dimensional propagator on a circle. The price is that the full curvature, rather than a single component, must be determined, and that the reality of the reconstructed metric becomes a condition, which we argue holds for retarded solutions. We illustrate the scheme for a static point mass in de Sitter space, where it gives a real metric perturbation that agrees with linearised Schwarzschild-de Sitter up to a diffeomorphism. Each of them is described by the ${\rm BC}_1$ version of the classical Sklyanin algebra. In particular case, when 4 pairs of constants coincide, the ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model exactly coincides with the relativistic Zhukovsky-Volterra gyrostat. Explicit change of variables is obtained. We also consider another special case of the ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model with 7 independent constants. We show that it can be reproduced by considering the transfer matrix of the classical 1-site XYZ chain with boundaries. In the end of the paper, using another gauge transformation we represent the Chalykh's Lax matrix in a form depending on the Sklyanin's generators.
comment: 31 pages, minor changes, typos corrected
♻ ☆ Logarithmic corrections to the entropy of near-extremal black holes in New Massive Gravity
Lucas Acito, Mariano Chernicoff, Julio Oliva, Cielo Ramirez de Arellano Torres, Matías Sempe
We study the one-loop correction to the entropy of near-extremal black holes in three-dimensional massive gravity at the special point where the theory exhibits a unique maximally symmetric vacuum and non-constant curvature hairy black holes can achieve extremality even in the static case. Focusing on the near-horizon AdS$_2\times S^1$ geometry, we evaluate the contribution of boundary graviton modes that become exact zero modes in the extremal limit. We show that the resulting one-loop partition function generates logarithmic corrections to the semiclassical entropy, providing a new extension to higher-curvature gravity of what has been recently obtained for near-extremal black holes in General Relativity.
comment: 24 pages, no figures. V2: typos fixed and new references included. V3: Discussion about the regime of validity of the computation included. To appear in JHEP
♻ ☆ Integrable open elliptic Toda chain with boundaries
A. Zotov
In this letter we discuss the classical integrable elliptic Toda chain proposed by I. Krichever. Our goal is to construct an open elliptic Toda chain with boundary terms. This is achieved using the factorized form of the Lax matrix and gauge equivalence with the XYZ chain.
comment: 13 pages, typos corrected, comments and proofs added
♻ ☆ On the existence of toric ALE and ALF gravitational instantons
Hari K. Kunduri, James Lucietti
We establish existence and uniqueness results for asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) and asymptotically locally flat (ALF) gravitational instantons. In particular, we prove the existence of a unique, Ricci-flat, toric ALE and ALF gravitational instanton, for every admissible rod structure, that is smooth up to possible conical singularites. We also give an elementary proof that any toric ALE or ALF self-dual instanton is a multi-Eguchi-Hanson or multi-Taub-NUT solution.
comment: 21 pages. v2: minor edits, published version
♻ ☆ Taub-NUT as gravitational dyon with torsion
Dmitri Gal'tsov, Rostom Karsanov
We show that the Levi-Civita connection for the Taub-NUT metric is singular on Misner strings and generates an Einstein tensor containing the squares of the delta function. This can be improved by introducing torsion, in which case the Einstein tensor may be interpreted as that of a cosmic string with negative variable tension. Komar flows in Misner strings are generated by torsion, which is therefore responsible for the asymptotic Komar charges. The Taub-NUT metric then appears as a soliton supported by two spin-fluid beams.
comment: The journal version (slightly expanded)
♻ ☆ Factorization in deep inelastic scattering at Björken limit: Reduction to (1+1)D integrable models
H. Babujian, M. Karowski, A. Sedrakyan
We study the small-$x$ behavior of the proton structure function $F_2(x,Q^2)$ using the combined HERA inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering data and compare it with exact structure functions obtained in integrable quantum field theories. The data are described by a local power law, $F_2(x,Q^2)=A(Q^2)x^{-γ(Q^2)}$, where the exponent $γ(Q^2)$ increases smoothly with the hard scale. We show that this running exponent is well described by a simple renormalization-group crossover form and is compatible with the illustrative limiting value $C=γ(\infty)\simeq0.431$. This reference belongs to the sine-Gordon power-law universality class among the exactly solvable possibilities and corresponds to the coupling $β^2/π=16/(3-C)\simeq6.23$. The sine-Gordon-constrained fit gives a quantitatively accurate description of the HERA $F_2$ surface, with reduced $χ^2$ close to unity, and is cross-checked with the overlapping final HERA reduced-cross-section data. These results indicate that the small-$x$ growth observed in deep inelastic scattering is naturally organized by a sine-Gordon-type universality class, while the finite-$Q^2$ dependence is controlled by a smooth crossover toward the corresponding asymptotic exponent.
comment: 13 pages, 12 figures
♻ ☆ Elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda and elliptic Toda chains: classical r-matrix structure and relation to XYZ chain
D. Murinov, A. Zotov
We discuss the classical elliptic Toda chain introduced by Krichever and the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda chain introduced by Adler, Shabat and Suris. It is shown that these models can be obtained as particular cases of the elliptic Ruijsenaars chain. We explain how the classical $r$-matrix structures are derived for these chains. Also, as a by-product, we prove that the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda chain is gauge equivalent to discrete Landau-Lifshitz model of XYZ type. The elliptic Toda chain is also gauge equivalent to XYZ chain with special values of the Casimir functions at each site.
comment: 29 pages, minor changes, details added to Section 5, typos corrected
♻ ☆ Field analogue of the Ruijsenaars-Schneider model
A. Zabrodin, A. Zotov
We suggest a field extension of the classical elliptic Ruijsenaars-Schneider model. The model is defined in two different ways which lead to the same result. The first one is via the trace of a chain product of $L$-matrices which allows one to introduce the Hamiltonian of the model and to show that the model is gauge equivalent to a classical elliptic spin chain. In this way, one obtains a lattice field analogue of the Ruijsenaars-Schneider model with continuous time. The second method is based on investigation of general elliptic families of solutions to the 2D Toda equation. We derive equations of motion for their poles, which turn out to be difference equations in space with a lattice spacing $η$, together with a zero curvature representation for them. We also show that the equations of motion are Hamiltonian. The obtained system of equations can be naturally regarded as a field generalization of the Ruijsenaars-Schneider system. Its lattice version coincides with the model introduced via the first method. The limit $η\to 0$ is shown to give the field extension of the Calogero-Moser model known in the literature. The fully discrete version of this construction is also discussed.

E. Zucker, J. Zweizig
We search for gravitational-wave background signals produced by various early Universe processes in the Advanced LIGO O4a dataset, combined with the data from the earlier O1, O2, and O3 (LIGO-Virgo) runs. The absence of detectable signals enables powerful constraints on fundamental physics. We derive gravitational-wave background energy density upper limits from the O1-O4a data to constrain parameters associated with various possible processes in the early Universe: first-order phase transitions, cosmic strings, domain walls, stiff equation of state, axion inflation, second-order scalar perturbations, primordial black hole binaries, and parity violation. In our analyses, the presence of an astrophysical background produced by compact (black hole and neutron star) binary coalescences throughout the Universe is also considered. We address the implications for various cosmological and high energy physics models based on the obtained parameter constraints. We conclude that LIGO-Virgo data already yield significant constraints on numerous early Universe scenarios.

Materials Science [49]
☆ Vacancy-enhanced Li solid-solution anodes for solid-state batteries: computational screening enabling high critical current density
Arseniy S. Burov, Nadezhda A. Ashikhmina, Nurlan Zhanabayev, Anton O. Boev, Aleksandra D. Radina, Ilya V. Chepkasov, Alexander G. Kvashnin, Dmitry A. Aksyonov
Sluggish vacancy-mediated self-diffusion in lithium metal limits the critical current density (CCD) of Li anodes in solid-state batteries by promoting interfacial void formation during stripping. To enhance the effective vacancy concentration while preserving the bcc Li host, we screen 50 substitutional solutes using density functional theory (DFT) within a funnel based on automatic phase diagram construction, solution energies, solute-vacancy binding energies, and experimental solubility limits. Using an adaptation of the Lomer model for the dilute limit, we show that only Ag, Ge, and Cd solid solutions are predicted to reach $1~\mathrm{mA~cm^{-2}}$ within their solubility limits. The thermodynamically estimated CCD of Ag at $\sim 9$ at.% reaches $\sim 4~\mathrm{mA~cm^{-2}}$ at a theoretical capacity of $1522~\mathrm{mAh~g^{-1}}$. Migration barrier calculations indicate that the enhancement may be partially offset by vacancy trapping, necessitating further validation via molecular dynamics simulations. Notably, Hume-Rothery rules alone prove insufficient as prefilters, whereas machine-learning models trained on the DFT data can eliminate most unsuitable solutes early in the funnel and extend the workflow to related solid-solution searches.
☆ CO2-Induced Shifts in the Confined Phase Transformation of CH4 in Metal-Organic Frameworks
Anthony Dorhauer, Bartosz Mazur, Bogdan Kuchta, Carlos Wexler
A sharp increase in gas uptake over a narrow pressure range can occur for fluids confined in nanoporous materials such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), reflecting a transformation between distinct adsorption states, often accompanied by the existence of metastable states. Understanding how co-adsorbed species modify this behavior is important for predicting and optimizing gas storage and separation. Here, we investigate the effect of CO2 on the adsorption transformation of confined CH4 in rigid IRMOF-1 and IRMOF-8. Transition-Matrix Monte Carlo (TMMC) simulations were performed for systems containing 0-75 and 0-150 CO2 molecules in IRMOF-1 and IRMOF-8, respectively. While the addition of CO2 decreases the maximum CH4 uptake, consistent with competition for pore space, remarkably, the presence of CO2 significantly shifts the discontinuity in the CH4 adsorption isotherm to substantially lower pressures relative to the pure CH4 system. This promotion of the high-density CH4 phase at lower pressures demonstrates that CO2 substantially alters the thermodynamic landscape governing confined CH4 through changes in both fluid-fluid and fluid-framework interactions. These results establish CO2 as a thermodynamic modifier of confined CH4 behavior and suggest that controlled co-adsorption provides a means of tuning adsorption transformations in nanoporous materials.
comment: Supplemental Information and Input files available upon request. Under review (ACS Omega)
☆ Combining Simulations and Spectroscopy to Design Protective Coatings on Sulfide Solid Electrolytes
Zhiyi Wang, Leonie Braks, Michele Ceriotti, Ali Coskun, Hanna Türk, Davide Tisi
Sulfide solid electrolytes are attractive for all-solid-state batteries because of their high Li-ion conductivity and favorable processability, but their practical use is limited by electrochemical instability and moisture-induced degradation. Molecular surface coatings offer a scalable strategy to improve humidity tolerance and interfacial stability, yet there is limited understanding of the molecular-level factors governing surface interactions. By combining large-scale atomistic simulations enabled by a machine-learning potential with targeted experiments, we present a comprehensive framework for designing molecular coatings on Li$_6$PS$_5$Cl (LPSCl). Using a PET-MAD interatomic potential fine-tuned on an r$^2$SCAN reference dataset covering LPSCl surfaces, molecular adsorbates, and their interactions, we model surface adsorption of carboxylic (CA), sulfonic (SA), and phosphonic (PA) acids with alkyl chains of varying lengths and the interaction of these coated surfaces with water at finite temperature. The simulations show that lithiated head groups generally exhibit more favorable adsorption energies. Impedance spectroscopy shows that the lithiated coatings maintain 40--55\% of the initial ionic conductivity after powder processing. While adsorption strength is largely controlled by head-group chemistry and lithiation state, coating morphology depends primarily on alkyl-chain length and surface coverage. In particular, long-chain lithiated carboxylates form dense, brush-like hydrophobic layers that reduce water access to reactive Li surface sites, with protection setting in at a coating thickness of approximately 0.8 nm. Consistent with these predictions, longer carboxylate chains suppress H$_2$S evolution more effectively. Because thicker coatings also hinder Li-ion transport, intermediate chain lengths offer the best balance between moisture protection and ionic conductivity.

☆ Rationalizing charge transfer: a single-molecule case study across three distinct surfaces
Benjamin Lowe, Jan Berger, Martin Ondráček, Oleksandr Stetsovych, Shayan Louie, Marco Lozano, Diego Soler-Polo, Shiladitya Karmarkar, Andrés Pinar Solé, Iva Plutnarová, Pingo Mutombo, Manish Kumar, Michael Píro, Ali Cem Demirok, Michael L. Steigerwald, Zdeněk Sofer, Colin Nuckolls, Pavel Jelínek
Organic molecules are versatile building blocks for the formation of complex low-dimensional nanostructures on surfaces. Recently, interest has grown in translating on-surface synthetic protocols from noble metal surfaces to insulating surfaces, which offer technological relevance, and to magnetic or superconducting surfaces, which offer new routes to correlated phases. It is important, therefore, to understand how these alternative surfaces may alter the properties of adsorbates through processes like charge transfer and screening. Evidence for charge transfer is often obtained experimentally via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS), and theoretically via density functional theory (DFT). In this work, we systematically compare the properties of isolated macrocyclic emeraldine (Me$_6$) molecules on three different surfaces: metallic Au(111), a semiconducting ferromagnetic monolayer of FeCl$_2$, and a cleaved superconducting surface of bulk 2H-NbSe$_2$. We show that STS and DFT alone are insufficient to quantify charge transfer for these cases. Instead, we complement these methods with Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements and model Hamiltonian calculations to demonstrate that on Au(111) and FeCl$_2$, Me$_6$ molecules donate a single electron to the substrate, whereas on NbSe$_2$ two electrons are transferred from molecule to substrate. Our work provides insight into the interplay of charge transfer, screening, and molecule-substrate coupling, and develops experimental and theoretical methods for comparing the properties of adsorbates across different surfaces for future studies.
comment: 32 pages, 5 figures
☆ Unconventional charge density wave order in ErTe$_{3}$: symmetry breakings and fluctuations probed by Raman scattering
Théotime Freitas, Mattia Udina, Alexandr Alekhin, Niloufar Nilforoushan, Sarah Houver, Alain Sacuto, Benito A. Gonzalez, Ian R. Fisher, Indranil Paul, Yann Gallais
Recent experiments have revealed unexpected mirror-symmetry breakings in the charge density-wave (CDW) state of rare-earth tritellurides, suggesting a putative ferro-axial CDW state. Here we report polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements tracking the point-group symmetry breakings across the CDW phase transition in the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe$_3$. We show that the mirror-symmetry breakings follow closely the emergence of the CDW order, suggesting a single component CDW order parameter. Furthermore, Raman measurements in the $A_{2g}$ symmetry channel above the CDW transition temperature indicate the absence of significant ferro-axial fluctuations. We discuss the broad implications of these findings with respect to the nature of the CDW state in the tritellurides.
comment: to appear in JPS Conference Proceedings
☆ Ginzburg-Landau Theory with Elastic Incompatibility Describes the Liquid-G-phase-Crystal State Diagram
Alessio Zaccone, Konrad Samwer
We derive a mechanically consistent Ginzburg-Landau theory for the metastable heterogeneous G state reported in deeply undercooled metallic liquids. The central result is that type-II-like mixed-state physics can emerge structurally with the random internal stress field playing the role of the magnetic field. Frozen eigenstrain due to elastic incompatibility between ordered cores and the amorphous matrix generates incompatible stress, while the non-affine internal strain in the liquid-like matrix in between the ordered cores relaxes that stress over a finite screening length $λ_σ$ (analogous to the London length in the superconducting problem). Structural order heals over a distinct mechanically-dressed length $ξ_G$; their ratio $κ_G=λ_σ/ξ_G$ provides the structural counterpart of the Ginzburg-Landau parameter. Because the matrix is transiently rigid yet locally relaxational only over an intermediate time window, the same mechanism selects crystal for slow protocols, a heterogeneous G state at intermediate rates, and a homogeneous L-like glass under rapid arrest. Residual incompatibility frustrates coarsening, allowing finite ordered cores and screened, orientation-dependent core interactions. The resulting texture is an inverted Abrikosov analogue: structural order resides in the cores, whereas incompatible-stress screening is carried by the surrounding disordered matrix. The theory yields direct simulation and experimental tests through stress-decay, structural-healing, non-affine-susceptibility, and kinetic measurements.
☆ Majorana Edge-to-bound State Transition in Interferometric Superconductor Rings
Xiangyu Bi, Aoshen Yang, Hongzi Cao, Ganyu Chen, Yuqiang Fang, Zeya Li, Qizheng Sun, Junwei Huang, Da Wang, Fuqiang Huang, Toshiya Ideue, Qianghua Wang, Yoshihiro Iwasa, Hongtao Yuan
Manipulating flux quanta in topological superconductors is central to vortex braiding in quantum computing. Their interferometric superconducting rings can host either topologically protected edge states with fluxes confined inside the central hollow area or vortex bound states in flux cores at the annulus walls. Here we demonstrate a strategy to drive topological edge states into vortex bound states by tuning the relative scale of vortex size and annulus width in nano-ring interferometric device on 2M-WS$_2$ topological superconductor. Near its superconducting transition where the coherence length exceeds the annulus width, Little-Parks oscillations exhibit expected periods for flux bundles in ring-center, consistent with edge states residing at inner and outer rims of the annulus. Upon cooling, where the coherence length shrinks below the annulus width, the unexpectedly increased oscillation period reflects multiple fluxes distributed along annulus region in flux necklace configuration, implying a transition from extended edge states to localized vortex bound states. Ginzburg-Landau simulations and local density-of-states calculations with Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations reveal that large values for both Ginzburg-Landau parameter and flux-pinning energy are vital for such a transition. Our findings provide a novel strategy for understanding flux manipulation towards flux braiding and topological quantum computing.
☆ Tensor Networks for Materials Simulation and Quantum Chemistry
Saeed S. Jahromi, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Roman Rausch, Sukhbinder Singh, Roman Orus
Predicting the properties of correlated materials and molecules often requires a many-body description that goes beyond single-particle and mean-field approximations. Tensor networks address this challenge by exploiting the entanglement structure of quantum states to construct compact, systematically improvable representations. Although developed largely for idealized model Hamiltonians, these methods are increasingly being integrated into material-specific calculations. This Perspective introduces their underlying principles and examines how network geometry, bond-dimension truncation, and approximate contraction determine the accuracy and computational reach of these approaches. We survey applications across regimes of increasing complexity, ranging from ground-state properties of quantum magnets and itinerant-fermion systems to excitation spectra, nonequilibrium dynamics, finite-temperature and open systems, and molecular electronic structure. We then examine four routes connecting these methods to real materials, including experimentally constrained models, downfolded Hamiltonians, dynamical mean-field theory with tensor network impurity solvers, and quantum embedding. Throughout, we evaluate the maturity of existing capabilities and their principal limitations, synthesizing this assessment into a practical method-selection guide. We argue that reliable materials predictions require quantifying uncertainties introduced at each stage, from constructing material-specific Hamiltonians to extracting experimentally accessible observables. Finally, we identify the algorithmic advances and reproducible computational practices needed to establish tensor networks as a routine tool for predictive materials science and quantum chemistry.
comment: 28 pages, 4 figures
☆ First- and Second-Order Electron Position Correlators Reveal Topological Phase Transitions
Antimo Marrazzo, Christian Loer Llemit, Massimo Capone
The theory of conventional critical phenomena is built around the concepts of fluctuations and correlators of local observables. Here, we show that topological phase transitions can also be characterized through spatial and temporal two-point correlation functions associated with fluctuations of the electronic position operator. The key object is the antisymmetric part of the position-position correlation function, which yields the Chern number in the equal-time and equal-space limit. Here, we propose an interferometric RIXS protocol that instead creates entanglement between spatially separated regions of a solid-state material. Recombining the scattered photons at a second beam splitter and detecting an energy-selected photon then projects the material into a coherent superposition of excitations at the two ends. Using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes, we show that orthogonal and degenerate end excitations yield maximally entangled states. We illustrate this mechanism in three models: (1) two decoupled sites yield a heralded Bell state. (2) An open tight-binding chain exhibits reflection-parity-dependent interference, providing a benchmark for the interferometer's coherence. (3) A spin-1 Haldane (AKLT) chain yields an entangled pair of fractionalized edge spins. We also discuss practical considerations and challenges for realizing the protocol in X-ray experiments.

Crucially, the non-singlets, i.e. states in non-trivial representations of SU$(N)$, implement the effects of vortices on the discretized worldsheets. This random lattice model has the low-temperature $c=1$ and high-temperature $c=0$ phases, with the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition separating them. We study this curve using the non-perturbative matrix bootstrap and low- and high-temperature perturbation theory, which explain the thermal instability. At low temperatures, thermally excited non-singlets backreact on the Fermi sea of matrix eigenvalues, causing it to spill over. At high temperatures, the theory is described by an effective matrix integral obtained by dimensional reduction on the thermal circle; the eigenvalue distribution of the zero mode becomes unstable at the critical coupling. We conjecture that the BKT transition occurs at a special point on the critical curve and estimate its position. Finally, we switch to the regular square lattice and study the MQM-inspired Villain model, where the link factor is the one-dimensional propagator on a circle. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we map out the BKT transition in this model.
